signals.title: Remove `WINDOW VIEW` and reimplement time-window aggregation on top of streaming queries
signals.text: `WINDOW VIEW` (`StorageWindowView`) should be removed, and similar functionality should be implemented on top of streaming queries (`SELECT ... FROM t STREAM`). This issue records the assessment: what the removal takes, what the streaming engine already covers, and the missing pieces for a replacement. The removal does not need to wait for the replacement. ## Why remove now - **The feature has been non-functional since Dec 2024.** Commit `ceae84c87a2` ("mv_dependencies: cleanup") removed the explicit view-dependency registration, and `DDLDependencyVisitor` does not extract the source table of a `CREATE WINDOW VIEW`, so an `INSERT` into the source table is silently not pushed to the window view, and a direct `INSERT` into the window view fails with `std::out_of_range` (see https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493). Nobody noticed for ~1.5 years, which bounds real-world usage at approximately zero. - **It was never ported to the analyzer.** With `enable_analyzer = 1` (the default) `CREATE WINDOW VIEW` throws, and an existing window view loads in a permanently inert state (`disabled_due_to_analyzer`; its background tasks are not even created). Creating one requires `allow_experimental_window_view = 1` and `enable_analyzer = 0` simultaneously. The implementation is built entirely on the old infrastructure: `InterpreterSelectQuery`, `TreeRewriter`, `ExpressionAnalyzer`, AST-rewriting visitors. - **Its tests were already removed** in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73822 (92 files, ~2450 lines), because they were inherently flaky. - **It keeps costing triage time**: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 (server SIGSEGV through `getSourceTableSelectQuery`), https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75191 (breaks `Replicated` databases). - The deprecation phase requested in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61069 has de facto happened, involuntarily, since 24.12. - Even "parity" is not worth copying from the implementation: e.g. the bounded branch of `updateMaxWatermark` advances the watermark bias by the *slide* interval instead of the *watermark* interval, so the documented semantics and the implemented semantics differ. The replacement should target the documentation. ## Part 1: the removal Model it on the `LIVE VIEW` removal (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/88706): delete the code and the parser, no `ATTACH` compatibility shim, and a "Backward Incompatible Change" changelog entry saying window views must be dropped before upgrade. Any window view surviving in metadata has been inert since 24.12 anyway. Checklist: - Delete `src/Storages/WindowView/` (~2.6k LOC: `StorageWindowView`, `WindowViewSource`, `StorageBlocks`) and `src/Processors/Transforms/WatermarkTransform.{h,cpp}` (used only by window views). - Delete the `WATCH` statement stack: `ParserWatchQuery`, `ASTWatchQuery`, `InterpreterWatchQuery`, the `IStorage::watch` virtual and the `StorageProxy` forward. `StorageWindowView` is the last implementor of `watch`, and the `WATCH` docs already carry a deprecation badge. - Delete `ParserCreateWindowViewQuery`, the `ASTCreateQuery` fields `is_window_view`, `is_watermark_strictly_ascending`, `is_watermark_ascending`, `is_watermark_bounded`, `allowed_lateness`, `watermark_function`, `lateness_function`, and the window-view branch of `isCreateQueryWithImmediateInsertSelect` (POPULATE). - Delete the `PushingToWindowViewSink` and `ViewType::WINDOW` branches in `InsertDependenciesBuilder` (~100 LOC of special-casing). - Un-special-case: `InterpreterCreateQuery` (POPULATE path, the `CREATE TABLE AS` guard), the two `DatabaseReplicated` inner-table cleanups, the `DDLDependencyVisitor` window-view exception, the `DatabaseOrdinary` never-lazy-load rule, the `StorageFactory` name mapping and rejection, the ArrowFlight table-type mapping, and `add_object_library(clickhouse_storages_windowview ...)`. - Make the settings obsolete via `MAKE_OBSOLETE`: `allow_experimental_window_view`, `window_view_clean_interval`, `window_view_heartbeat_interval`, `wait_for_window_view_fire_signal_timeout` (the last one is already dead code: it is read into a member that nothing uses). Remove the entry in `enableAllExperimentalSettings` and the BuzzHouse settings list. - **Keep** the `tumble`/`hop`/`tumbleStart`/`tumbleEnd`/`hopStart`/`hopEnd` functions — they are ordinary functions usable in a regular `GROUP BY`, they have their own tests (`03127_window_functions_uint16`, `04115_function_time_window_errors`, `04141_windowID_with_timezone_string`), and they are exactly the vocabulary the replacement will reuse. Only `windowID` is window-view-specific and can be removed. Keep the `WATERMARK` keyword — the streaming `WATERMARK FOR` clause already uses it. - Remove the four remaining window-view tests (`01049_window_view_window_functions`, `02364_window_view_segfault`, `04202_window_view_disabled_with_analyzer`, `04218_window_view_insert_70296`), preserving the plain time-window-function coverage from `01049`. - Docs: delete the `Window View` section of `sql-reference/statements/create/view.md` (and the Mintlify twin and locales) and `watch.md`; keep `time-window-functions.md`. Net roughly −3k LOC. Fully independent of the replacement work below. ## Part 2: what streaming queries already cover `FROM t STREAM` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105114, gated by `enable_streaming_queries`) already provides: gap-free per-partition commit-order reads over `MergeTree`/`ReplicatedMergeTree` with resumable client-side cursors (`STREAM CURSOR {'partition': {'block_number': N, 'block_offset': M}}`), `WHERE`/`PREWHERE`, row policies, `UNION ALL`, `DISTINCT`, `JOIN` against dimension tables, `LIMIT` as a stream terminator, `STREAM BOUNDED`/`UNORDERED`, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` support, and a dedicated background scheduling pool. The `WATERMARK FOR ts AS expr [IDLE TIMEOUT ...]` clause (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112658) parses, validates, and injects the `_time_attribute`/`_watermark` virtual columns — and then throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` at execution: that is the designated hook point. Two window-view features come for free: - **`WATCH`** → an interactive streaming `SELECT` is strictly better: real columns, real formats, no heartbeat hack, and `LIMIT n` replaces `WATCH ... LIMIT`. - **`POPULATE`** → an empty cursor already means "from the beginning", and consistent backfill-then-follow is inherent to commit-order reading; none of the populate/live-data race the window view had. The `WATERMARK FOR ts AS expr` clause subsumes all three window-view watermark strategies: `STRICTLY_ASCENDING` ≡ `AS ts`, `ASCENDING` ≡ `AS ts - INTERVAL 1 SECOND`, bounded ≡ the general form. ## Part 3: the missing pieces 1. **Watermark execution** (front-end merged; execution is `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`). Per-source watermark generation from `_time_attribute`, propagation through the pipeline, min-combining across the N parallel subscription sources and across `UNION`/`JOIN` inputs, idle-timeout advancement. Prerequisite for everything event-time. 2. **Windowed aggregation with emission** — https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/28855, the hard part. A streaming aggregating transform that keys state by window (`GROUP BY tumble(_time_attribute, INTERVAL 10 SECOND)`), finalizes and emits windows whose end the watermark has passed, then frees their state. Emit-on-watermark-close can be the implicit default when the `GROUP BY` contains a time-window function of the time attribute; an explicit `EMIT` clause (`EMIT ON WATERMARK`, `EMIT EVERY INTERVAL 5 SECOND`) covers processing-time mode — replacing both window-view fire modes, including the `now()` hack. Hop windows do not need the gcd-slice trick as a correctness device (assign each row to its covering windows; slicing can return later as a state-size optimization). `ALLOWED_LATENESS` becomes a policy on this operator: keep closed-window state for the lateness interval and re-emit updated rows, with silent-drop as the default. 3. **The sink**: unbounded `INSERT INTO target SELECT ... FROM src STREAM ...`. Nothing wires a streaming select into an insert pipeline today. Replay determinism gives a clean path to effectively-exactly-once: after a restart, re-reading from the last committed cursor yields identical blocks in identical order, so insert-deduplication tokens derived from `(partition, block range, window)` make retries idempotent — at-least-once plus dedup, without Flink-style state checkpointing. 4. **A persistent job object** — the actual `CREATE WINDOW VIEW ... TO target` replacement, along the `CREATE JOB` line from the RFC: a catalog object owning a background streaming `INSERT SELECT`, persisting `(cursor, last_fired_watermark)` in Keeper at output-commit time, resuming after a restart by replaying from the cursor and rebuilding in-memory window state, with `SYSTEM START/STOP` and a system table for observability. The refreshable-materialized-view machinery is the natural scaffolding (background execution, Keeper-coordinated run-on-one-replica) — which immediately beats the window view's `ON CLUSTER` story, where every replica fired independently into the target and produced duplicates. Smaller gaps: - **Start-from-tail.** The window-view default was "only new data" (`POPULATE` was opt-in); `STREAM` defaults to "from the beginning", and there is no way to say "current end" without hand-crafting a cursor. Needs a modifier such as `STREAM FROM LATEST`. - **Source prerequisites.** `STREAM` requires `enable_block_number_column`/`enable_block_offset_column` (+ minmax indexes) on the source table; a job should demand or auto-enable them. Source retention must cover the replay horizon (window size + lateness + downtime); the job should fail loudly, not skip, if the cursor falls off a TTL edge. - **Non-MergeTree sources.** Only the MergeTree family supports `STREAM` today. The `Null`-table pattern (windowed aggregation over data you do not store) and Kafka-family sources are future RFC items; the window view's practical sources were MergeTree anyway. ## Feature mapping | `WINDOW VIEW` | Streaming replacement | |---|---| | `GROUP BY tumble(ts, ...)` / `hop(ts, ...)` | same functions over `FROM t STREAM`, windowed aggregating transform | | `WATERMARK = STRICTLY_ASCENDING` | `WATERMARK FOR ts AS ts` | | `WATERMARK = ASCENDING` | `WATERMARK FOR ts AS ts - INTERVAL 1 SECOND` | | `WATERMARK = INTERVAL x` | `WATERMARK FOR ts AS ts - INTERVAL x` | | processing-time mode / `now()` | `EMIT EVERY INTERVAL x` (needs design, see https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/28855) | | `ALLOWED_LATENESS` | keep-state-past-watermark policy on the emit operator | | `TO target` + fire | unbounded `INSERT SELECT` inside a persistent job | | `.inner.` `AggregatingMergeTree` state + cleanup task | none needed: replay from the durable source using `(cursor, last_fired_watermark)` | | `WATCH [EVENTS] [LIMIT n]` | interactive streaming `SELECT ... [LIMIT n]` | | `POPULATE` | default (empty cursor = from the beginning); the opposite needs `STREAM FROM LATEST` | | `ALTER ... MODIFY QUERY` (drops all state) | recreate the job; replay makes it lossless | | `ON CLUSTER` (uncoordinated, duplicate fires) | Keeper-coordinated run-on-one-replica, as in refreshable materialized views | ## Why the replacement is structurally simpler The window view's complexity was forced by its push-based design: because it consumed inserts as they happened, partial aggregate state had to be durable immediately — hence the `.inner.` `AggregatingMergeTree`, the `windowID` function and the mergeable/final query rewriting, the periodic `ALTER DELETE` cleanup task, a fire task that re-plans a full `InterpreterSelectQuery` per window under a mutex, and the dependency-registration seam whose silent breakage killed the feature. The pull-based streaming engine inverts this: the durable state *is* the source table plus a small cursor, window state lives in memory inside one continuously-running pipeline, and emission is an operator rather than a background task. Roughly 80% of `StorageWindowView` has no equivalent in the replacement — it just disappears. ## Suggested sequencing 1. Remove now (−3k LOC, one PR). No reason to wait for parity: what is being removed does not work. 2. Watermark execution. 3. Windowed aggregation + `EMIT`. At this point interactive streaming window queries already exceed the `WATCH` mode of window views. 4. Unbounded `INSERT SELECT`, then the persistent job object with durable cursors — the full `TO`-table replacement, and simultaneously the reliable-Kafka-consumption vehicle from the RFC, so the work is shared with a much bigger goal. 5. Extras: `STREAM FROM LATEST`, lateness policies, `EMIT EVERY`, `Distributed`/parallel-replicas streaming. When building the semantics test matrix for steps 2–4, the 92 window-view tests deleted in `d6815890526` (`01047`–`01088` et al.) are a ready-made checklist: three watermark strategies × lateness × populate × alter × multi-key `GROUP BY` × `JOIN`. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61069 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/42990 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/28855 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/88706 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73822 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105114 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112658

signals.title: `OPTIMIZE TABLE` on DeltaLake/Paimon/Hudi object-storage tables silently succeeds as a no-op instead of throwing `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`
signals.text: **Describe the unexpected behaviour** `OPTIMIZE TABLE` on an object-storage table whose lake type does not implement compaction — `DeltaLakeLocal`/`DeltaLake`, `Paimon*`, `Hudi`, and plain object-storage engines — returns Ok and does nothing: no files rewritten, no new `_delta_log` commit, no error, nothing in the log. Every other engine that does not support OPTIMIZE throws `Code: 48. Method optimize is not supported by storage <name>` (`Memory`, `Join`, `Distributed`, ...), and Iceberg — the one lake type that does implement compaction — validates its gate loudly (`Code: 36. ... Enable 'allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction' setting to call optimize for iceberg tables`). So within the same `StorageObjectStorage` class, `OPTIMIZE TABLE iceberg_table` either compacts or tells you why not, while `OPTIMIZE TABLE delta_table` silently succeeds as a no-op — a user running it reasonably assumes compaction happened. **How to reproduce** Master `26.8.1.1375`, via `clickhouse local` (the Delta log is bootstrapped by hand with the same pattern as the `04628_delta_lake_partition_special_values` stateless test, because ClickHouse cannot initialize a Delta transaction log itself): ```bash mkdir -p delta/_delta_log cat > delta/_delta_log/00000000000000000000.json <<'EOF' {"protocol":{"minReaderVersion":1,"minWriterVersion":2}} {"metaData":{"id":"optimize-noop-repro","format":{"provider":"parquet","options":{}},"schemaString":"{\"type\":\"struct\",\"fields\":[{\"name\":\"k\",\"type\":\"long\",\"nullable\":true,\"metadata\":{}},{\"name\":\"v\",\"type\":\"long\",\"nullable\":true,\"metadata\":{}}]}","partitionColumns":[],"configuration":{},"createdTime":1700000000000}} EOF for i in 1 2 3; do clickhouse local -q "INSERT INTO FUNCTION deltaLakeLocal('$PWD/delta') SELECT number + $i*100 AS k, number AS v FROM numbers(10) SETTINGS allow_experimental_delta_lake_writes = 1" done ls delta/*.parquet | wc -l # 3 ls delta/_delta_log/*.json | wc -l # 4 clickhouse local -q "CREATE TABLE td ENGINE = DeltaLakeLocal('$PWD/delta'); OPTIMIZE TABLE td; SELECT 'OPTIMIZE returned Ok'" ls delta/*.parquet | wc -l # still 3 — nothing happened ls delta/_delta_log/*.json | wc -l # still 4 — no commit was written ``` The contrast on the same binary: ```sql CREATE TABLE tm (x UInt8) ENGINE = Memory; OPTIMIZE TABLE tm; -- Code: 48. DB::Exception: Method optimize is not supported by storage Memory. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) ``` ```sql -- Iceberg (the one lake with OPTIMIZE support) refuses loudly without its gate: OPTIMIZE TABLE iceberg_table; -- Code: 36. DB::Exception: Enable 'allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction' setting to call optimize for iceberg tables. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` **Mechanism** The base `IStorage::optimize` throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (`src/Storages/IStorage.cpp:261`), which is what makes every non-supporting engine loud. `StorageObjectStorage::optimize` (`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp:727`) overrides it to `return configuration->optimize(...)`, whose default implementations return `false` (`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageConfiguration.h:285`, `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/IDataLakeMetadata.h:138`) — and `InterpreterOptimizeQuery::execute` discards the returned `bool` (`src/Interpreters/InterpreterOptimizeQuery.cpp`, the `table->optimize(...)` call). So the "nothing was optimized" signal exists but is dropped. The override was introduced with the Iceberg compaction work (`IcebergMetadata::optimize` is the only lake implementation), and the silent success for the other lake types looks like collateral rather than a decision. **Expected behavior** When `configuration->optimize` returns `false`, `StorageObjectStorage::optimize` should throw like the `IStorage` default (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, or a hint in the Iceberg gate style), so `OPTIMIZE TABLE` never reports success while doing nothing. Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signals.title: Flaky test: 04625_hash_table_sizes_stats_table_expression_modifiers reports zero preallocated sizes
signals.text: 🕵 `04625_hash_table_sizes_stats_table_expression_modifiers` fails regularly on master and on many pull requests: the hash-table-sizes statistics come back as zero, so the test prints ``` final-prealloc 0 no-final-prealloc 0 ``` instead of the expected `520000` / `650000`. Per CIDB it failed 8 times on master in the last 30 days (most recently 2026-08-13 22:32:26), plus on 42 distinct pull requests, across every build flavour (`Fast test`, `arm_binary`, `amd_debug`, `amd_tsan`, `amd_msan`, `amd_llvm_coverage`), so it is not tied to a particular sanitizer, storage, or analyzer configuration. It also survives the automatic reruns ("Failed 3 out of 3 reruns"), which makes it look like a real regression in a job that hits it. Query for the history: ```sql SELECT toStartOfDay(check_start_time) AS day, count() AS failures, groupUniqArray(pull_request_number) AS prs FROM checks WHERE check_start_time >= now() - toIntervalDay(30) AND test_name = '04625_hash_table_sizes_stats_table_expression_modifiers' AND test_status IN ('FAIL', 'ERROR') GROUP BY day ORDER BY day DESC ``` The test was last touched by 9650bb8cd624 (2026-07-23) "Fix flaky ... under randomized external aggregation", so the earlier flakiness fix looks incomplete. Example report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=105987&sha=77de23431cd96d94d5370923e65911c42dc65480&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20old%20analyzer%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20DBReplicated%2C%20WasmEdge%2C%20parallel%2C%201%2F3%29 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105987

signals.title: Nullable LHS defeats the no-supertype cast guard: nullIn(NULL, 'x') returns 1
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With compare-nulls semantics (`nullIn`/`notNullIn`, or `transform_null_in = 1`) and a `Nullable` left-hand side, a non-constant set element that cannot be represented in the left-hand side type silently becomes a `NULL` set member. `SELECT nullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x'))` returns 1 (and `notNullIn` returns 0) on both analyzers; the correct answer is 0 (resp. 1) because `'x'` is not `NULL`.** - **Root cause:** `cast_elements_to` is initialised to `left_type`, and the guard immediately below only ever *adds* `Nullable` (`makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe`). When `left_type` is already `Nullable`, the guard cannot remove it, so the cast target stays `Nullable` even under compare-nulls semantics and a failed `CAST` produces a matching `NULL` instead of throwing. The PR's own `04839` pins `SELECT nullIn(1, materialize('x'))` as `CANNOT_PARSE_TEXT` for the non-`Nullable` LHS — merely wrapping the same left-hand side in `toNullable` turns that error into a silent answer. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `ActionsMatcher::visit` ([`src/Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp:1094`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp#L1094)) / `QueryAnalyzer::resolveFunction` ([`src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp:1782`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp#L1782)) → no common supertype for `{Nullable(UInt8), String}` → cast-to-LHS-type fallback at resolveFunction.cpp:1808 / ActionsVisitor.cpp:1259 → `CAST('x' AS Nullable(UInt8))` yields `NULL` → `isNotDistinctFrom(NULL, NULL)` / `has([NULL], NULL)` matches. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp:1808`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp#L1808) — Case 3 scalar RHS: cast_elements_to = left_type, then Nullable-only guard - [`src/Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp:1259`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp#L1259) — old-analyzer row-wise rewrite: same cast-to-LHS-type fallback **Impact:** Silently wrong boolean results for `nullIn`/`notNullIn` and for `IN`/`NOT IN` under `transform_null_in = 1` whenever the left-hand side is `Nullable` and the non-constant right-hand side contains a value with no common supertype (e.g. a `String` against a numeric/`Date`/`UUID`/`IPv4` column). Every `NULL` row matches the set, so `WHERE nullable_col IN (some_string_expr)` selects all `NULL` rows and `NOT IN` drops them. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `6c53bb45d8b`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/82b544fb-550e-4257-9a5d-322c41921cf1) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: with compare-nulls IN semantics, a non-constant set element that cannot be represented in -- the left-hand side type must not become a NULL member of the set when the left-hand side is Nullable. SELECT nullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1; SELECT notNullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1; SELECT CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)') IN (materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, transform_null_in = 1; SELECT nullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0; SELECT notNullIn(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)'), materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0; SELECT CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)') IN (materialize('x')) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0, transform_null_in = 1; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 0 1 0 0 1 0 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 1 0 1 1 0 1 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Make the cast target non-`Nullable` under compare-nulls semantics regardless of the left-hand side's nullability — e.g. `cast_elements_to = compare_nulls && !isNullableOrLowCardinalityNullable(right_type) ? removeNullable(left_type) : ...` — so an unrepresentable element throws `CANNOT_PARSE_TEXT` exactly as it already does for a non-`Nullable` left-hand side (`04839`). Alternatively keep the `Nullable` cast but AND the comparison with a cast-succeeded predicate so the phantom `NULL` cannot match. Trade-off: the first option makes `nullIn(toNullable(1), materialize('x'))` throw where it currently returns 0, which is the behavior `04839` already pins for the non-`Nullable` left-hand side. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The multi-element form (`x IN (materialize('a'), materialize('b'))`) goes through `convertTupleToArray`/`makeInArrayArgumentsList` and shows the same phantom `NULL` under the analyzer; that path's `common_type = in_first_argument->getResultType()` fallback predates this PR, so fixing only the scalar path leaves the tuple path inconsistent. Found during automated review of [PR #104993](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr104993_001` </details> cc @niyue @alexbakharew @alexey-milovidov (from #104993)

signals.title: View pushdown force-disables `extremes`, dropping the block on single-shard clusters
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With the default `optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1`, `SELECT ... FROM <trivial view over a single-shard Distributed table> SETTINGS extremes = 1` returns no extremes block at all. The same query against the underlying `Distributed` table, and the same query with the setting turned off, both return it.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2331`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2331) — `read_context->setSetting("extremes", Field(false));`. The comment above it (:2324-2327) justifies the override by asserting "The outer query still runs under query_context, so the limits remain enforced on the result the client receives." That is true for `max_result_rows`/`max_result_bytes`, which are enforced by the pipeline on the final result, but false for `extremes`, which needs either a plan step on the initiator or `add_extremes` on the remote source — and the pushdown removes both. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `buildQueryPlanForTableExpression` ([`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2329-2331`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2329-L2331)) builds `read_context` for the pushed-down read and sets `extremes` to false on it. That context becomes `effective_context` and is passed to `effective_storage->read(...)`, i.e. `StorageDistributed::read`, and from there to `ReadFromRemote` ([`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromRemote.cpp:564`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromRemote.cpp#L564), `add_extremes = context->getSettingsRef()[Setting::extremes]`). So the shard is never asked for extremes. Separately, because the pushdown swaps `effective_storage` to the `Distributed` table, `getQueryProcessingStage` returns `Complete` on a single-shard cluster and the initiator's plan collapses to a bare `ReadFromRemote` — so `Planner.cpp:2677 addExtremesStepIfNeeded` never contributes an initiator-side `ExtremesStep` either. Both producers of the extremes block are eliminated. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2331`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2331) — `read_context->setSetting("extremes", Field(false))` on the context used for the pushed-down `StorageDistributed::read` - [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:1221`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L1221) — sibling optimization `pushOrderByIntoView` bails out when `extremes` is set instead of overriding it — the treatment this path should have used **Impact:** Any client asking for `extremes` (the `extremes` setting, `--extremes`, or the `extremes` key of `JSON*` formats) silently stops receiving min/max rows when reading a qualifying view over a single-shard `Distributed` table. There is no error and no warning — the block is simply absent, so consumers that key off it see no data rather than a failure. Single-shard `Distributed` tables are the common starting topology (and the shape used by `test_shard_localhost` in most of this PR's own tests). Multi-shard clusters are unaffected because the initiator retains an `ExtremesStep`. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `6c53bb45d8b`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/255ed7d0-67d5-43df-8d66-8a5b1bd3a564) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that `extremes` is still reported for a query reading a view over a single-shard Distributed table. SET enable_analyzer = 1; SET enable_parallel_replicas = 0; SET prefer_localhost_replica = 0; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04891_local; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04891_dist; DROP VIEW IF EXISTS t_04891_view; CREATE TABLE t_04891_local (id UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t_04891_local SELECT number FROM numbers(4); CREATE TABLE t_04891_dist AS t_04891_local ENGINE = Distributed(test_shard_localhost, currentDatabase(), t_04891_local); CREATE VIEW t_04891_view AS SELECT id FROM t_04891_dist; SELECT 'control_distributed_table'; SELECT id FROM t_04891_dist ORDER BY id SETTINGS extremes = 1; SELECT 'view_pushdown_off'; SELECT id FROM t_04891_view ORDER BY id SETTINGS extremes = 1, optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0; SELECT 'view_pushdown_on'; SELECT id FROM t_04891_view ORDER BY id SETTINGS extremes = 1, optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1; DROP VIEW t_04891_view; DROP TABLE t_04891_dist; DROP TABLE t_04891_local; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` control_distributed_table 0 1 2 3 0 3 view_pushdown_off 0 1 2 3 0 3 view_pushdown_on 0 1 2 3 0 3 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` control_distributed_table 0 1 2 3 0 3 view_pushdown_off 0 1 2 3 0 3 view_pushdown_on 0 1 2 3 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Do not override `extremes` on `read_context`. Either drop that line entirely (`max_result_rows`/`max_result_bytes` are the only two that need the override, and unlike `extremes` they are enforced at the pipeline boundary), or, matching the precedent set by `pushOrderByIntoView` at :1221, add `settings[Setting::extremes]` to the list of conditions that suppress the pushdown. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - Worth checking whether any other initiator-side step gated on the storage stopping short of `Complete` disappears under the same stage flip — the `where_filters` / row-level-filter step just below the `till_stage` computation is the obvious candidate to audit. Found during automated review of [PR #101791](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101791). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr101791_001` </details> cc @simonmichal @alexey-milovidov (from #101791)

signals.title: Pushdown applies view-level `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` to shards: row set changes, `ILLEGAL_FINAL`
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With the default `optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1`, `FINAL` and `SAMPLE` written on a view reference are propagated to the shard-local table instead of being ignored. Two user-visible consequences: (a) `SELECT id, val FROM <view over ReplacingMergeTree Distributed> FINAL` returns a different row set than before (3 rows -> 2 rows, verified); (b) `SELECT count() FROM <view over plain MergeTree Distributed> FINAL`, which returned a count in every released version, now throws `ILLEGAL_FINAL` (code 181). Same for `SAMPLE`: `SELECT count() FROM view SAMPLE 1/2` went from 1000 to 492.** - **Root cause:** [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2238`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2238) — `dist_table.setTableExpressionModifiers(TableExpressionModifiers{merged_final, merged_sample_size, merged_sample_offset});` is applied unconditionally whenever the outer reference carries modifiers, with no check that the underlying table supports them and no gate on the resulting semantic change. There are two defensible readings of intent and they need different fixes, so this is filed rather than assumed: (i) propagating `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` is the intended behaviour (04092 Test 1 asserts it for `ReplacingMergeTree`) — then the PR is a Backward Incompatible Change, not a Performance Improvement, and the `ILLEGAL_FINAL` case still needs handling because it turns a working query into an error; (ii) the pushdown was meant to be result-neutral — then the modifier merge should be dropped, or the pushdown suppressed whenever the outer reference carries `FINAL`/`SAMPLE`. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `buildQueryPlanForTableExpression` ([`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2227-2239`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2227-L2239)) reads the outer `TableNode`'s `TableExpressionModifiers` (the `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` the caller wrote on the view reference), ORs `FINAL` with the view body's own modifiers, and calls `dist_table.setTableExpressionModifiers(...)` on the inlined `Distributed` table node. That node is then substituted with the shard-local table, so the shard receives `... FROM (SELECT id FROM local_table FINAL) ...`. On the `StorageView::readImpl` path the outer modifiers were never forwarded into the view body, so `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` on a view reference were silently dropped. For a plain `MergeTree` the shard-side analyzer rejects the modifier in `QueryAnalyzer::validateTableExpressionModifiers` and throws `ILLEGAL_FINAL`. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp:2238`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Planner/PlannerJoinTree.cpp#L2238) — unconditional `setTableExpressionModifiers` merging outer `FINAL`/`SAMPLE` into the inlined `Distributed` table node - [`src/Storages/StorageView.cpp:522`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6c53bb45d8b/src/Storages/StorageView.cpp#L522) — `tryGetUnderlyingDistributed` gates the pushdown on parameterized/`DEFINER` views only; it does not consider whether the underlying engine supports the modifiers the caller wrote **Impact:** Queries that ran successfully in every released version start failing with `ILLEGAL_FINAL` after upgrade, with no opt-in, whenever a view over a `Distributed` table backed by an engine without `FINAL` support is read with `FINAL`. Queries over `ReplacingMergeTree`/`CollapsingMergeTree`-backed views silently change their row set. The behaviour is also inconsistent in a way users cannot predict: whether `FINAL` takes effect now depends on whether the view happens to satisfy the AST-level triviality test (a view with an `ORDER BY` in its body, or over a local table, still ignores `FINAL`). </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `6c53bb45d8b`). ### How to reproduce ```sql -- Test that FINAL on a view over a Distributed table behaves the same regardless of -- optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed: the plain MergeTree case must not start failing, -- and the ReplacingMergeTree case must not change its row set. SET enable_analyzer = 1; SET enable_parallel_replicas = 0; SET prefer_localhost_replica = 0; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04892_plain; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04892_plain_dist; DROP VIEW IF EXISTS t_04892_plain_view; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04892_repl; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04892_repl_dist; DROP VIEW IF EXISTS t_04892_repl_view; CREATE TABLE t_04892_plain (id UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t_04892_plain SELECT number FROM numbers(4); CREATE TABLE t_04892_plain_dist AS t_04892_plain ENGINE = Distributed(test_shard_localhost, currentDatabase(), t_04892_plain); CREATE VIEW t_04892_plain_view AS SELECT id FROM t_04892_plain_dist; CREATE TABLE t_04892_repl (id UInt32, val UInt32, ver UInt32) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(ver) ORDER BY id; SYSTEM STOP MERGES t_04892_repl; INSERT INTO t_04892_repl VALUES (1, 10, 1); INSERT INTO t_04892_repl VALUES (1, 20, 2); INSERT INTO t_04892_repl VALUES (2, 30, 1); CREATE TABLE t_04892_repl_dist AS t_04892_repl ENGINE = Distributed(test_shard_localhost, currentDatabase(), t_04892_repl); CREATE VIEW t_04892_repl_view AS SELECT id, val FROM t_04892_repl_dist; SELECT 'repl_off', id, val FROM t_04892_repl_view FINAL ORDER BY id, val SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0; SELECT 'repl_on', id, val FROM t_04892_repl_view FINAL ORDER BY id, val SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1; SELECT 'plain_off', count() FROM t_04892_plain_view FINAL SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0; SELECT 'plain_on', count() FROM t_04892_plain_view FINAL SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 1; DROP VIEW t_04892_repl_view; DROP TABLE t_04892_repl_dist; DROP TABLE t_04892_repl; DROP VIEW t_04892_plain_view; DROP TABLE t_04892_plain_dist; DROP TABLE t_04892_plain; ``` ### Expected behavior ``` repl_off 1 10 repl_off 1 20 repl_off 2 30 repl_on 1 10 repl_on 1 20 repl_on 2 30 plain_off 4 plain_on 4 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` repl_off 1 10 repl_off 1 20 repl_off 2 30 repl_on 1 20 repl_on 2 30 plain_off 4 <run aborts here> Code: 181. DB::Exception: Storage MergeTree doesn't support FINAL. (ILLEGAL_FINAL) (in query: SELECT 'plain_on' AS `'plain_on'`, count() AS `count()` FROM (SELECT `__table2`.`id` AS `id` FROM `test_h4x5c2x3u5n2`.`t_04892_plain` AS `__table2` FINAL) AS `__table1`) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Pick one of the two intents and make it explicit. If propagation is intended: keep the merge but relabel the changelog category as Backward Incompatible Change with an explicit note, and suppress the pushdown (falling back to `readImpl`) when the outer reference carries `FINAL` and the underlying table does not support it, so a previously-working query does not start erroring. If result-neutrality is intended: drop the merge at :2227-2239 and instead suppress the pushdown whenever `table_expression_query_info.table_expression`'s `TableExpressionModifiers` are set. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> Found during automated review of [PR #101791](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101791). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr101791_002` </details> cc @simonmichal @alexey-milovidov (from #101791)

signals.title: optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq changes results: uniq*(tuple(nullable)) drops NULLs and depends on constant folding
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong `optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq` (default `true`) strips injective functions from `uniq*` arguments. When the stripped function is `tuple()` and its argument is `Nullable`, the rewrite is not semantics-preserving: `tuple(NULL)` is a value that `uniq*` counts, but a bare `NULL` is skipped by `uniq*`. So the optimization silently changes the result. ```sql SELECT uniqExact(tuple(x)) FROM values('x Nullable(Int32)', 1, 2, NULL); -- 2 (with the optimization, i.e. by default) SELECT uniqExact(tuple(x)) FROM values('x Nullable(Int32)', 1, 2, NULL) SETTINGS optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq = 0; -- 3 (correct: (1), (2) and (NULL) are three distinct tuples) ``` `EXPLAIN SYNTAX` shows the rewrite dropping the tuple: ```sql EXPLAIN SYNTAX SELECT countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin([NULL]))); -- SELECT uniqExact(arrayJoin([NULL])) ``` A second, related symptom: with the analyzer, whether the optimization applies at all depends on whether the argument happens to be constant-foldable, so semantically identical expressions disagree with each other: ```sql SELECT countDistinct(tuple(NULL)); -- 1 SELECT countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin([NULL]))); -- 0 SELECT countDistinct(tuple(arrayJoin( emptyArrayToSingle([]::Array(Nullable(Int32)))))); -- 0 ``` `tuple(NULL)` has all-constant arguments, so it is folded into a `ConstantNode` during query analysis, and the pass no longer recognises it as a function to unwrap. The `arrayJoin` variants are not folded , so there the `tuple()` is stripped. With `enable_analyzer = 0` all three return `0`, because the legacy `TreeOptimizer` does the same rewrite on the un-folded AST. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/718dd23f-a726-4218-92f5-7b78048bda57 Also reproduces with `uniq`, `uniqHLL12`, `uniqCombined64` and `uniqTheta` (every function listed in `isUniqFunction`), and with `countDistinct` via `count_distinct_implementation`. ### Expected behavior `uniqExact(tuple(x))` should not depend on `optimize_injective_functions_inside_uniq`, on whether the argument is constant-foldable, or on `enable_analyzer`. `tuple()` is injective on the values it receives, but it also removes nullability, and `uniq*` treats NULL specially — so it must not be eliminated when its argument is `Nullable` and its own result type is not. ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

signals.title: HTTP session does not pick up newly granted nested role privileges until reconnect
signals.text: ### Company or project name Local reproducible test case ### Describe the bug An existing HTTP session does not pick up privileges from a role granted to the user after the session was opened. If the user opens an HTTP session first, then an administrator grants a role to that user, the same HTTP session still uses the old active role set and fails access checks. A new HTTP session immediately sees the newly granted role and the same query succeeds. This is especially visible with `clusterAllReplicas(..., system.tables)` and a subquery reading an ordinary table. The old session fails with `ACCESS_DENIED` for the table used in the subquery, even though the role granted after session creation provides that privilege through a nested role. Setting `push_external_roles_in_interserver_queries=0` does not help this scenario because the failure happens before remote execution: the current session does not refresh its active roles/privileges. ### How to reproduce Tested on ClickHouse `26.7.3.19` official build. Minimal topology: multi-replica cluster, HTTP interface enabled, access management enabled. Create test objects and nested roles: ```sql CREATE DATABASE role_cache_repro ON CLUSTER 'test_cluster'; CREATE TABLE role_cache_repro.test_table ON CLUSTER 'test_cluster' ( name String ) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{uuid}/{shard}', '{replica}') ORDER BY name; INSERT INTO role_cache_repro.test_table VALUES ('role_cache_repro'); CREATE ROLE role_cache_main; CREATE ROLE role_cache_subrole; GRANT REMOTE ON *.* TO role_cache_subrole; GRANT SELECT ON system.tables TO role_cache_subrole; GRANT SELECT ON role_cache_repro.* TO role_cache_subrole; GRANT role_cache_subrole TO role_cache_main; CREATE USER role_cache_user IDENTIFIED BY 'password'; ``` Open an HTTP session before granting the role: ```bash curl -u role_cache_user:password \ 'http://localhost:8123/?session_id=role-cache-session' \ --data-binary "SELECT currentUser(), currentRoles()" ``` Grant the role after the session already exists: ```sql GRANT role_cache_main TO role_cache_user; ``` In the same HTTP session, roles are still stale: ```bash curl -u role_cache_user:password \ 'http://localhost:8123/?session_id=role-cache-session' \ --data-binary "SELECT currentUser(), currentRoles()" ``` Run the query in the same old HTTP session: ```bash curl -u role_cache_user:password \ 'http://localhost:8123/?session_id=role-cache-session' \ --data-binary " SELECT hostName(), t.database, t.name FROM clusterAllReplicas('test_cluster', system.tables) AS t WHERE t.database IN ( SELECT name FROM role_cache_repro.test_table ) FORMAT TSVRaw" ``` Actual result in the old session: ```text Code: 497. DB::Exception: role_cache_user: Not enough privileges. To execute this query, it's necessary to have the grant SELECT(name) ON role_cache_repro.test_table. (ACCESS_DENIED) ``` Open a new HTTP session and run the same query: ```bash curl -u role_cache_user:password \ 'http://localhost:8123/?session_id=role-cache-session-new' \ --data-binary " SELECT hostName(), t.database, t.name FROM clusterAllReplicas('test_cluster', system.tables) AS t WHERE t.database IN ( SELECT name FROM role_cache_repro.test_table ) FORMAT TSVRaw" ``` The new session succeeds and returns rows from all replicas. ### Expected behavior After a role is granted to a user, existing HTTP sessions should either: 1. refresh the active role/privilege set before subsequent queries, or 2. clearly document that HTTP sessions cache role grants until reconnect/session expiration. The behavior is surprising because reconnecting immediately fixes the access check without any other access-control changes. ### Error message and/or stacktrace From `system.query_log` for the old session: ```text type: ExceptionBeforeStart exception_code: 497 exception: Code: 497. DB::Exception: role_cache_user: Not enough privileges. To execute this query, it's necessary to have the grant SELECT(name) ON role_cache_repro.test_table. (ACCESS_DENIED) used_privileges: ['SELECT ON system.tables','SHOW COLUMNS ON system.tables','READ ON REMOTE'] missing_privileges: ['SELECT(name) ON role_cache_repro.test_table'] ``` For the new session, the same query finishes successfully and `used_privileges` includes: ```text SELECT(name) ON role_cache_repro.test_table SELECT(database, name) ON system.tables READ ON REMOTE ``` ### Additional context The same result was observed with nested roles: ```sql GRANT role_cache_subrole TO role_cache_main; GRANT role_cache_main TO role_cache_user; ``` The issue is not fixed by adding: ```sql SETTINGS push_external_roles_in_interserver_queries = 0 ``` because the old-session failure is `ExceptionBeforeStart` on the initiator, before remote execution.
signals.author: Glomywow

signals.title: INSERT rejected with NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK when an ALIAS column declares STATISTICS
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A table created with an ALIAS column carrying explicit `STATISTICS(...)` accepts INSERTs on 26.4-26.7 but rejects every INSERT after this PR: `Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK)`. The table becomes effectively read-only after upgrade; SELECT, merges and `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` keep working.** - **Root cause:** The insert path uses `ColumnsStatistics::build` (hard `getByName`) while the merge path uses `ColumnsStatistics::buildIfExists`, which skips columns absent from the block ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:690-700`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L690-L700)). Statistics on non-physical columns are otherwise treated as unsupported — `addImplicitStatistics` skips Alias/Ephemeral columns (Statistics.cpp:927-929) and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS` rejects them via `columns.hasPhysical` (StatisticsDescription.cpp:181) — but the inline `CREATE TABLE ... col T ALIAS expr STATISTICS(...)` form has no such check (ColumnsDescription.cpp:260-261). Flipping `materialize_statistics_on_insert` to `true` turns that latent inconsistency into a hard INSERT failure. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `MergeTreeSink::writeNewTempPart` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp:409`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeSink.cpp#L409)) -> `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeTempPartImpl` ([`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:848`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L848)) -> `ColumnsStatistics` ctor collects every column whose statistics description is non-empty, including ALIAS columns ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:644-647`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L644-L647)) -> `ColumnsStatistics::build` looks the column up with `block.getByName` ([`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684)), and an ALIAS column is never in the written block. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:849`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L849) — insert path calls ColumnsStatistics::build on the written block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:684`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L684) — build() uses block.getByName, which throws for a column not in the block - [`src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp:646`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/Statistics/Statistics.cpp#L646) — ColumnsStatistics ctor does not skip Alias/Ephemeral columns - [`src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp:181`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2746afad95f/src/Storages/StatisticsDescription.cpp#L181) — ALTER path rejects statistics on non-physical columns; the inline CREATE path does not **Impact:** Any table whose DDL puts `STATISTICS(...)` on an ALIAS column stops accepting INSERTs after upgrading to 26.8 (or after `SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1`). The error is an internal-sounding `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` at write time with no hint that statistics caused it, and there is no DDL-time warning. `ALTER TABLE ... DROP STATISTICS <alias_col>` is not a workaround either, since that path also refuses non-physical columns. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `2746afad95f`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/63424d1d-98a2-4f38-92d8-552f32129820) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test that INSERT works when an ALIAS column declares statistics. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; SET allow_statistics = 1; SET materialize_statistics_on_insert = 1; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_alias_statistics; CREATE TABLE t_alias_statistics (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3); SELECT a, b FROM t_alias_statistics ORDER BY a; DROP TABLE t_alias_statistics; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 1 2 2 3 3 4 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Received exception from server (version 26.8.1): Code: 10. DB::Exception: Received from 127.0.0.1:19020. DB::Exception: Not found column b in block. There are only columns: a. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) (query: INSERT INTO t_alias_statistics VALUES (1), (2), (3);) ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Use `statistics.buildIfExists(block)` on the insert path (matching `MergeTask`'s `BuildStatisticsTransform`), or skip Alias/Ephemeral columns in the `ColumnsStatistics` constructor the way `addImplicitStatistics` does. Rejecting the DDL instead is the wrong lever: the same code path parses metadata on ATTACH/startup, so existing tables would fail to load. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same `build` vs `buildIfExists` asymmetry would also fire for any other future column kind that is present in the metadata but absent from the written block. Found during automated review of [PR #109454](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109454). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr109454_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov @rschu1ze @egor-click (from #109454)
signals.author: clickgapai

signals.title: S3Queue `after_processing='delete'` silently leaves objects in the bucket
signals.text: 🕵️ ## Describe what's wrong With `after_processing = 'delete'`, S3Queue consumes every row exactly once but does not always delete the source objects. The leftovers are never re-read either, so they are orphaned: the queue treats them as `Processed` while the object is still in the bucket. Nothing reports this. There is no error, no exception and no log line — the delete simply does not happen for some objects, and 3 of 4 objects in the very same run *are* deleted. The consequence is that a bucket the user has explicitly asked to be drained grows without bound, and no queue-side state reveals it. **This is not a duplicate of #114421** — see the section at the bottom. ## Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduced on **26.8.1.1384** (release build) against MinIO. ## How to reproduce Write four CSV objects of five rows each under one prefix, then: ```sql CREATE TABLE dsink (id UInt64, v String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE dq (id UInt64, v String) ENGINE = S3Queue('http://127.0.0.1:19001/fuzz/<prefix>/*.csv', 'minio', 'minio123', 'CSV') SETTINGS keeper_path = '/clickhouse/s3q/<prefix>', after_processing = 'delete', mode = 'ordered', processing_threads_num = 8, buckets = 1, list_objects_batch_size = 2, max_processed_files_before_commit = 1, polling_min_timeout_ms = 50, polling_max_timeout_ms = 200; CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW dmv TO dsink AS SELECT id, v FROM dq; ``` Wait until `count()` in `dsink` reaches 20, then list the bucket prefix. One or more objects are still there, and stay there. ## Expected behaviour Every object whose rows have been committed is deleted from the bucket. ## Actual behaviour ``` rows=20/20 objects_left: f_1.csv <- 20s after start rows=20/20 objects_left: f_1.csv <- 50s after start, table still running ``` ## It is a race, not a specific setting combination An automated 30-minute campaign (339 S3Queue runs, 3438 oracle checks) hit this 8 times across 4 distinct configurations: | objects left | mode | threads | parallel_inserts | buckets | batch | commit_files | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | ordered | 8 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 1 | | 1 | ordered | 8 | 1 | 7 | 2 | 100 | | 3 | ordered | 8 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 3 | | 2 | ordered | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1000 | 0 | Only `mode='ordered'` and `after_processing='delete'` are constant. `processing_threads_num`, `buckets`, `list_objects_batch_size`, `parallel_inserts` and the commit thresholds all vary across hits, so no single one of them is necessary. Per-configuration rate, 12 trials each, judged after the rows land plus a 6 s grace and a 12 s re-check (so a merely slow delete cannot count as a leak): | configuration | runs leaving objects | |---|---| | `ordered`, threads=1 (else default) | 0/12 | | `ordered`, threads=8 (else default) | 0/12 | | `unordered`, threads=8 (else default) | 0/12 | | `ordered`, threads=2, `parallel_inserts=1` | 1/12 | | **full combination from the repro above** | **8/12** | Reading the two tables together: - `mode='ordered'` looks genuinely required — `unordered` is 0/12 here and all 8 campaign hits were ordered. - Concurrency alone is not enough: neither `threads=8` nor `threads=1` on an otherwise default ordered queue ever failed. - The full combination is the reliable trigger at **8/12**, so that is the one to use when reproducing. - But it is not the only trigger. `threads=2 + parallel_inserts=1` reaches it at 1/12, and the campaign independently hit it at `threads=2, batch=1000, commit_files=0, buckets=2, parallel_inserts=1` — a configuration the full-combination repro shares almost nothing with. So this is a race in the ordered-mode post-commit delete path that several different concurrency shapes can lose; the settings in the repro make it likely, not possible. ## What is and is not affected - **No data loss and no duplicates.** All 20 rows arrive exactly once in every run, including the failing ones. The bug is confined to the post-commit delete. - **The object is orphaned, not pending.** It is not re-read while the table keeps running (the row count stays flat for a further 30 s), so Keeper has the file as processed while the object is still in the bucket. ## Why this is not #114421 **#114421** ("S3Queue: swallowed `after_processing='delete'` failure silently re-ingests files as duplicates") reaches a similar end state by a different route: there the delete *errors* — `AccessDenied` from a least-privilege credential, or a transient failure past `after_processing_retries` — and the exception is swallowed in `ObjectStorageQueuePostProcessor.cpp`, which logs `LOG_WARNING "Failed to tag all N objects"`. That warning never appears here. Grepping the server log across the repro runs gives zero PostProcessor lines, zero `AccessDenied` and zero "Failed to tag", at `warning` level where they would have shown. The credentials are full, and most objects in the same run are deleted successfully. So the swallow path is not being hit: nothing fails, and nothing is logged. A fix for #114421 (don't mark `Processed` unless the action completed) would likely mask this one without addressing the underlying race. Adjacent but distinct: **#114595** (stale per-server `Processed` cache) and **#112341** (files marked `Processed` while rows are discarded). S3Queue's `Processed` bookkeeping has an active cluster of reports, but neither of those involves the post-commit delete. ## Notes `system.s3_queue_metadata` confirms the queue considers the run clean: `failed_nodes_count` is 0 for the affected `keeper_path`, so the leftover object is not sitting in a retry or failure state — it is simply never deleted. The object is also never re-read while the table keeps running. A trace-level run was also taken to count `Removing N objects` calls, but the 30-minute campaign was creating its own `after_processing='delete'` tables at the same time, so those lines cannot be attributed to this repro. Not used as evidence. The absence of the `Failed to tag` warning is unaffected: contamination can only add lines, not remove them.
signals.author: PedroTadim

signals.title: Stress test: logical error `Digest does not match` in `DatabaseReplicated::assertDigestWithProbability` under concurrent fuzzed DDL
signals.text: The stress test (observed with TSan, `arm_tsan`) intermittently aborts with an exception: ``` Logical error: 'Digest does not match'. ``` Stack (from [this report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114204&sha=833228d5fdaee4da8246fb5d39aa55bb77f0dad5&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29)): ``` src/Databases/DatabaseReplicated.cpp:1303: DB::DatabaseReplicated::assertDigestWithProbability src/Databases/DatabaseReplicated.cpp:1328: DB::DatabaseReplicated::assertDigest src/Databases/DatabaseReplicated.cpp:2644: DB::DatabaseReplicated::commitCreateTable src/Databases/DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:304: DB::DatabaseOnDisk::createTable src/Interpreters/InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2441: DB::InterpreterCreateQuery::doCreateTable ``` The failing `CREATE TABLE` runs through `DatabaseReplicatedDDLWorker::tryEnqueueAndExecuteEntry`, while a concurrent connection executes fuzzed queries (`executeASTFuzzerQueries` is in the outer frames), i.e. the digest assertion fires under concurrent DDL on a `Replicated` database. Per CIDB, this failure family (same source site, several `STID: 5007-*` message variants) appears only in stress checks, on many unrelated PRs, and is ramping up: | week | failures | |---|---| | 2026-07-26 | 2 | | 2026-08-02 | 5 | | 2026-08-09 | 8 | There were no occurrences before the week of 2026-07-26 in the last 90 days, which points to a change merged around that time making the digest tracking racy under concurrent replicated DDL (or introducing a real digest divergence). [CIDB query](https://play.clickhouse.com/play?user=play#) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114204
signals.author: andyzzhao

signals.title: `RowsReadByMainReader` exceeds `SelectedRows`/`read_rows` for read-in-order queries with LIMIT over Wide parts
signals.text: 🕵️ ## Describe what's wrong For a `SELECT ... ORDER BY <desc prefix of sorting key> LIMIT n` served by `optimize_read_in_order`, the per-reader row counters report substantially more rows than the query's own accounting of rows read: ``` main_reader_rows (ProfileEvents['RowsReadByMainReader']): 148192 selected_rows (ProfileEvents['SelectedRows']): 92896 read_rows (system.query_log): 92896 ------- unaccounted: 55296 (+59.5%) ``` `RowsReadByMainReader` is documented as *"Number of rows read from MergeTree tables by the main reader (after PREWHERE step)"*, and `SelectedRows` as *"Number of rows SELECTed from all tables"*. Rows reaching the main reader are a subset of the rows read, so `RowsReadByMainReader <= SelectedRows` should hold. Here it is 59% larger. The excess is always a whole number of granules (`55296 = 108 * 512`) and is stable across repeated executions of the same query. The concerning half is `read_rows`: it tracks `SelectedRows`, and it is what feeds query progress, `max_rows_to_read` and quotas. If the main reader really did move 148192 rows, then ~37% of the rows read by this query are invisible to those mechanisms. If instead the reader counters double count, they are misleading for read-amplification analysis. ## Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduced on a `master` build, version `26.8.1.1`, revision `54513`, git hash `a67a8e767aed3ffb5951cf7615d8f2c20f906a97` (Debug build, UBSan). I have not checked a release build or older versions. ## How to reproduce ```sql DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS mr_repro SYNC; CREATE DATABASE mr_repro; CREATE TABLE mr_repro.t (k UInt64, p UInt8, s String) ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY p % 4 ORDER BY (p, k) SETTINGS index_granularity = 512, min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0; -- keep the inserts as separate parts, so each partition ends up with one large -- part plus two much smaller ones SYSTEM STOP MERGES mr_repro.t; INSERT INTO mr_repro.t SELECT number, toUInt8(rand(1) % 8), randomPrintableASCII(rand(2) % 40) FROM numbers(500000); INSERT INTO mr_repro.t SELECT number + 500000, toUInt8(rand(1) % 8), randomPrintableASCII(rand(2) % 40) FROM numbers(36000); INSERT INTO mr_repro.t SELECT number + 536000, toUInt8(rand(1) % 8), randomPrintableASCII(rand(2) % 40) FROM numbers(800); -- reads in reverse sorting-key order and stops early because of the LIMIT SELECT s FROM mr_repro.t ORDER BY p DESC, k ASC LIMIT 100 SETTINGS optimize_read_in_order = 1, max_threads = 2, use_query_condition_cache = 0, log_comment = 'mr_repro_on' FORMAT Null; -- same query without read-in-order, for comparison SELECT s FROM mr_repro.t ORDER BY p DESC, k ASC LIMIT 100 SETTINGS optimize_read_in_order = 0, max_threads = 2, use_query_condition_cache = 0, log_comment = 'mr_repro_off' FORMAT Null; SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS query_log; SELECT log_comment, ProfileEvents['RowsReadByMainReader'] AS main_reader_rows, ProfileEvents['SelectedRows'] AS selected_rows, read_rows, ProfileEvents['SelectedMarks'] AS selected_marks, ProfileEvents['SelectedParts'] AS selected_parts, main_reader_rows - selected_rows AS unaccounted_rows FROM system.query_log WHERE type = 'QueryFinish' AND log_comment LIKE 'mr_repro_%' ORDER BY event_time_microseconds FORMAT Vertical; ``` ## Expected behaviour `RowsReadByMainReader <= SelectedRows`, and `read_rows` accounting for every row the readers actually read. ## Actual behaviour ``` Row 1: ────── log_comment: mr_repro_on main_reader_rows: 148192 selected_rows: 92896 read_rows: 92896 selected_marks: 1055 selected_parts: 12 unaccounted_rows: 55296 <-- main reader read 59% more rows than the query accounted for Row 2: ────── log_comment: mr_repro_off main_reader_rows: 291456 selected_rows: 536800 read_rows: 536800 selected_marks: 1055 selected_parts: 12 unaccounted_rows: -245344 <-- expected direction: main reader is a subset ``` ## Conditions Narrowed down by removing one factor at a time. All four of these are required: | condition | reproduces | | --- | --- | | Wide parts (`min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0`) | yes | | Compact parts (default for this data size) | **no** | | uneven part sizes per partition (500000 / 36000 / 800) | yes | | even part sizes (3 × 180000) | **no** | | `PARTITION BY p % 4` | yes | | no partitioning | **no** | | `optimize_read_in_order = 1` (DESC prefix + LIMIT → early termination) | yes | | `optimize_read_in_order = 0` | **no** | | same table 10× smaller (no early termination) | **no** | Makes no difference: `max_threads` (1/2/4 give the identical excess), `read_in_order_use_buffering`, `merge_tree_min_rows/bytes_for_concurrent_read`, `use_query_condition_cache`, `query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization`, and `MergeTree` vs `ReplicatedMergeTree` (both replicas of the same table show the identical excess). `RowsReadByPrewhereReaders` shows the same overshoot when a `PREWHERE` is present.
signals.author: PedroTadim

signals.title: `SelectedRows`/`SelectedBytes`/`read_rows` overstate the work done by lazy materialization, reporting +35% for a plan that reads 58% fewer compressed bytes
signals.text: 🕵️ ## Describe what's wrong With `query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization = 1` (the default), the row/byte accounting counters move in the *opposite direction* from the actual reading the query performs. For the same query on the same table, changing only that setting: | counter | lazy off | lazy on | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `ProfileEvents['SelectedRows']` | 65536 | 73728 | **+12.5%** | | `ProfileEvents['SelectedBytes']` | 851968 | 1146880 | **+35%** | | `read_rows` (`system.query_log`) | 65536 | 73728 | **+12.5%** | | `ProfileEvents['SelectedMarks']` | 440 | 440 | unchanged | | `ProfileEvents['ReadCompressedBytes']` | 792608 | **335538** | −58% | | `ProfileEvents['FileOpen']` | 48 | **34** | −29% | | `ProfileEvents['MarkCacheMisses']` | 24 | **17** | −29% | The optimization is doing its job — it reads less than half the compressed bytes and opens fewer files — but `SelectedBytes` claims it read 35% *more*, and `read_rows` bills it for 12.5% more rows. This makes the counters actively misleading for the thing they are most likely to be used for: deciding whether lazy materialization helps a given query. Judging it by `SelectedBytes` or `read_rows` in `system.query_log` leads to the conclusion that the optimization is a regression, on a query where it halves physical reads. `read_rows` is also the progress/quota metric, so a plan that reads strictly less data is accounted for more rows read than the plan it replaced. Note that `SelectedMarks` is unchanged, so the divergence is specifically in the row and byte accounting, not in mark/range selection. ## Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Reproduced on a `master` build, version `26.8.1.1`, revision `54513`, git hash `a67a8e767aed3ffb5951cf7615d8f2c20f906a97` (Debug build, UBSan). Not checked on a release build or older versions. ## How to reproduce All settings other than the one under test are at their defaults — in particular `query_plan_max_limit_for_lazy_materialization` stays at 10000, so this is reachable out of the box. ```sql DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS lazy_bytes SYNC; CREATE DATABASE lazy_bytes; CREATE TABLE lazy_bytes.t (p UInt8, k UInt64, i32 Int32, s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (p, k) SETTINGS min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0; SYSTEM STOP MERGES lazy_bytes.t; -- 8 Wide parts, 500k rows each (repeat with offsets 0, 500000, ... 3500000) INSERT INTO lazy_bytes.t SELECT toUInt8(rand(1) % 8), number, toInt32(rand(2) % 100000), randomPrintableASCII(rand(3) % 40) FROM numbers(500000); -- ... 7 more inserts, each offset by 500000 ... SYSTEM DROP MARK CACHE; SYSTEM DROP UNCOMPRESSED CACHE; SELECT i32, k FROM lazy_bytes.t WHERE p != 0 ORDER BY p ASC, k ASC LIMIT 100 SETTINGS query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization = 0, max_threads = 2, use_query_condition_cache = 0, log_comment = 'lazy_off' FORMAT Null; SYSTEM DROP MARK CACHE; SYSTEM DROP UNCOMPRESSED CACHE; SELECT i32, k FROM lazy_bytes.t WHERE p != 0 ORDER BY p ASC, k ASC LIMIT 100 SETTINGS query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization = 1, max_threads = 2, use_query_condition_cache = 0, log_comment = 'lazy_on' FORMAT Null; SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS query_log; SELECT log_comment, ProfileEvents['SelectedRows'] AS selected_rows, ProfileEvents['SelectedBytes'] AS selected_bytes, read_rows, ProfileEvents['SelectedMarks'] AS selected_marks, ProfileEvents['ReadCompressedBytes'] AS read_compressed_bytes, ProfileEvents['FileOpen'] AS file_open, ProfileEvents['MarkCacheMisses'] AS mark_cache_misses FROM system.query_log WHERE type = 'QueryFinish' AND log_comment IN ('lazy_off', 'lazy_on') ORDER BY event_time_microseconds FORMAT Vertical; ``` (The dropped caches are only needed to make `ReadCompressedBytes` comparable; the `SelectedRows`/`SelectedBytes` discrepancy shows up without them.) ## Expected behaviour `SelectedRows`/`SelectedBytes`/`read_rows` should reflect the data the plan actually reads. At minimum they should not increase for a plan that reads strictly fewer columns and fewer compressed bytes. ## Actual behaviour ``` Row 1: ────── log_comment: lazy_off selected_rows: 65536 selected_bytes: 851968 read_rows: 65536 selected_marks: 440 read_compressed_bytes: 792608 file_open: 48 mark_cache_misses: 24 Row 2: ────── log_comment: lazy_on selected_rows: 73728 selected_bytes: 1146880 read_rows: 73728 selected_marks: 440 read_compressed_bytes: 335538 file_open: 34 mark_cache_misses: 17 ``` ## What the numbers say about the mechanism The lazy plan reads the sorting/filter columns first, then re-reads the granules holding the surviving rows to materialize the remaining columns, and that second pass is *added* to `SelectedRows`/`SelectedBytes`. `SelectedRows` grows by exactly one granule (`65536 → 73728`), which is consistent and unsurprising. The byte figure does not decompose so cleanly. That one extra granule of 8192 rows is charged **294912 bytes = 36 bytes/row**, but the widest possible per-row cost of the columns this query touches is 13 bytes (`p` 1 + `k` 8 + `i32` 4). 36 bytes/row is close to the table's *full* row width including the `s` column the query never reads (measured at ~35.5 bytes/row), which would suggest the second pass is accounted for every column in the table rather than the ones being materialized. That does not hold up for a wide-payload variant though — `SELECT s` leaves ~86 bytes/row unaccounted for by the same arithmetic — so this is an observation that does not close, not a conclusion. Two things it is *not*: - Not a re-read of the sorting key for output: `SELECT i32, k` and `SELECT i32` produce byte-identical counters (851968 → 1146880 in both), so whether the sorting key appears in the SELECT list makes no difference. - Not specific to wide/uneven/partitioned layouts: it also reproduces on a single unpartitioned Compact part. The direction depends on payload width. With a wide payload the counter falls, as you would expect from a working optimization: | query | `SelectedBytes` off | on | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `SELECT i32, k` | 851968 | 1146880 | +35% | | `SELECT i32` | 851968 | 1146880 | +35% | | `SELECT s` | 2065574 | 1299767 | −37% | | `SELECT i32, s` | 2327718 | 1332535 | −43% | `ReadCompressedBytes` falls in every one of these (to 0.42×, 0.42×, 0.26×, 0.23× respectively), so the plan reads less from disk in all four cases while `SelectedBytes` claims a 35% increase in the first two.
signals.author: PedroTadim

signals.title: S3Queue `after_processing='move'` silently destroys a consumed file on a basename collision (default `move_preserve_path=false`)
signals.text: ### Company or project name _(quality/durability testing)_ ### Describe what's wrong With `after_processing = 'move'` and an `after_processing_move_prefix` set, S3Queue relocates each consumed object to `<move_prefix>/<basename>`, because `after_processing_move_preserve_path` defaults to `false`. When two consumed objects share a basename under different source prefixes — e.g. `data/a/part.csv` and `data/b/part.csv`, both matched by a glob like `data/*/part.csv` — they both resolve to the **same** destination key `<move_prefix>/part.csv`. The move is a per-object copy-then-delete (`ObjectStorageQueuePostProcessor::moveWithinBucket`): `copyObject(src -> dst)` followed by `removeObjectIfExists(src)`. So the second object's `copyObject` **overwrites** the first at the destination, and both source objects are then deleted. An S3 overwrite is not an error, so no exception is raised, nothing is logged, and `ObjectStorageQueueMovedObjects` counts both moves as successful. Net effect: one consumed file's content is permanently destroyed — gone from the source, overwritten at the destination — while the queue reports both files moved. The `move` action exists specifically to *retain* consumed files (audit, replay, or relocating them out of the ingest prefix), so this silently violates the very guarantee the feature provides, and it happens with the default settings. Same-basename objects across prefixes are common in practice (e.g. partitioned exports `date=2026-01-01/part.csv`, `date=2026-01-02/part.csv`). ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce - ClickHouse version 26.8 (also present in current master). - Object storage layout — two files that share the basename `part.csv` under different prefixes, with distinct content: - `s3://<bucket>/data/a/part.csv` → rows `0..9` - `s3://<bucket>/data/b/part.csv` → rows `100..109` ```sql CREATE TABLE dst (id UInt64, val UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE q (id UInt64, val UInt64) ENGINE = S3Queue('https://<bucket>.s3.amazonaws.com/data/*/part.csv', '<key>', '<secret>', 'CSV') SETTINGS mode = 'unordered', keeper_path = '/clickhouse/s3q_move_demo', after_processing = 'move', after_processing_move_prefix = 'archive'; -- after_processing_move_preserve_path defaults to false CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv TO dst AS SELECT id, val FROM q; ``` After both files are consumed: ```sql SELECT count(), uniqExact(id) FROM dst; -- 20, 20 → both files were ingested/acked ``` List the bucket: ``` archive/part.csv <- ONE object (only one file's content survives) data/a/part.csv, data/b/part.csv <- both GONE (deleted after the move) ``` One consumed file's bytes are destroyed. Setting `after_processing_move_preserve_path = 1` avoids it — the archive then keeps both `archive/data/a/part.csv` and `archive/data/b/part.csv`. ### Expected behavior Every object retained by `after_processing = 'move'` should survive exactly once. A destination-key collision under the default `after_processing_move_preserve_path = false` should not silently overwrite-and-delete a consumed file. Reasonable options: default `preserve_path` to `true`, fail the move loudly on a collision, or skip an existing destination — but not destroy data without any error or log line. ### Error message and/or stacktrace None — the loss is silent. `ObjectStorageQueueMovedObjects` reports both objects moved even though only one survives at the destination. ### Additional context Related to the `after_processing = 'delete'` silent-leftover behaviour in #114801 and the re-ingestion duplication in #114421; this is the `move`-leg sibling, but here the consequence is data loss (a destroyed file) rather than leftover or duplicated objects. Source (current master): `applyMovePrefixIfPresent` builds the destination as `move_prefix / fileName(remote_path)` when `preserve_path` is false, and `moveWithinBucket` does `copyObject` then `removeObjectIfExists` per object, swallowing per-object failures — in `src/Storages/ObjectStorageQueue/ObjectStorageQueuePostProcessor.cpp`.
signals.author: zlareb1

signals.title: Iceberg writer serializes day/hour partition transforms as non-canonical `days`/`hours`, breaking external readers (pyiceberg: UnknownTransform)
signals.text: **Describe what's wrong** The Iceberg writer serializes the `day` and `hour` partition transforms under the non-canonical plural names `days` / `hours` in the table metadata. The [Iceberg spec](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/#partition-transforms) defines the transform names as `year`, `month`, `day`, `hour` (singular), and that is what other writers emit. Spec-following readers do not recognize the plural forms: pyiceberg 0.10.0 parses them as `UnknownTransform(transform='days')`, so a ClickHouse-written time-partitioned Iceberg table silently loses its partition information (and with it partition pruning) in external readers. The writer is also internally inconsistent: the *sort order* serialization path maps the same functions to the canonical singular names (`{"toRelativeDayNum", "day"}, {"toRelativeHourNum", "hour"}` in `parseFunction`, `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp`), while the *partition spec* path emits the plural (`getPartitionField` writes `"days"` / `"hours"`, same file). `year` and `month` are emitted correctly in both paths. ClickHouse's own reader is lenient (`parseTransformAndArgument` accepts `day`, `date`, `days`, `dates`, …), so the bug is invisible in ClickHouse-only round-trips — it only breaks interoperability, which is the main reason to write Iceberg metadata in the first place. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduces on master 26.8.1.1375, on every write. **How to reproduce** ```bash clickhouse local --path . --query " CREATE TABLE t (k Int64, ts DateTime) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('\$PWD/ice/', 'Parquet') PARTITION BY (toRelativeDayNum(ts)) SETTINGS allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, toDateTime('2026-01-01 00:00:00') + number * 3600 FROM numbers(100) SETTINGS allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1; " grep -ho '"transform" : "[^"]*"' ice/metadata/*.json | sort -u ``` **Expected behavior** ``` "transform" : "day" ``` **Actual behavior** ``` "transform" : "days" ``` And through pyiceberg 0.10.0: ```python from pyiceberg.table import StaticTable t = StaticTable.from_metadata('ice/metadata/<latest>.metadata.json') print([repr(f.transform) for f in t.spec().fields]) # ["UnknownTransform(transform='days')"] ``` `PARTITION BY (toRelativeHourNum(ts))` produces `"transform" : "hours"` with the same result. `toYearNumSinceEpoch` / `toMonthNumSinceEpoch` correctly produce `year` / `month`. Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).
