signals.title: Support PromQL histogram_fraction for classic histograms
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL: support `histogram_fraction()` for classic histograms. ### Description **What was missing** Prometheus supports `histogram_fraction(lower, upper, b)` for estimating the fraction of observations between two bounds. ClickHouse previously rejected this function in TimeSeries PromQL queries. **What this PR adds** - Adds support for classic Prometheus bucket series. - Reuses the existing classic histogram handling used by `histogram_quantile`. - Matches Prometheus behavior for interpolation and bucket edge cases. - Keeps different histogram metric names separate during aggregation. - Removes the input metric name from the result. Example: ```promql histogram_fraction(0.1, 0.5, http_request_duration_seconds_bucket) ``` ### Why this matters **This is used for real latency and SLO queries**, not only parser compatibility. - **Pyrra:** generates `histogram_fraction()` in native-histogram latency SLO rules. See the [query generator](https://github.com/pyrra-dev/pyrra/blob/main/slo/promql.go#L761-L784) and [example SLO config](https://github.com/pyrra-dev/pyrra/blob/main/examples/pyrra-connect-latency.yaml#L14-L20). - **Grafana SLO:** uses it in a [request-latency SLI query](https://grafana.com/docs/plugins/grafana-slo-app/latest/sli-examples/latency/). - **Grafana Mimir:** documents it for calculating the [fraction of requests in a latency range](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/visualize/native-histograms/). - **Prometheus:** uses it for [fraction and Apdex calculations](https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/histograms/). Without this function, PromQL copied from these workflows fails in ClickHouse. ### Scope - **Supported:** classic `*_bucket` histogram series. - **Supported:** constant scalar lower and upper bounds. - **Not supported yet:** native histogram samples. - **Not supported yet:** non-constant bound expressions. Native histogram samples are not supported by the current TimeSeries Engine. This PR intentionally covers the classic bucket form first. ### References - [Prometheus histogram functions](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/functions/#histogram_fraction) - [Prometheus classic histogram implementation](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/promql/quantile.go) ### Changes - **Function support:** add `histogram_fraction` to the TimeSeries function registry and support documentation. - **Execution:** add a Prometheus-compatible classic histogram fraction aggregate. - **Shared logic:** reuse the histogram SQL-building pipeline with `histogram_quantile`. - **Precision:** preserve Float64 bound literals for Float32 tables and exact cumulative-count differences for large UInt64 counts. ### Tests - **Interpolation:** normal buckets, `rate()` input, negative bucket bounds, and bounds inside buckets. - **Bucket edges:** exact boundaries, degenerate buckets, `+Inf`, `NaN`, malformed `le`, and out-of-range bounds. - **Grouping:** range queries with multiple histogram groups and `sum by (le)` aggregation. - **Input validation:** invalid argument types and non-constant bounds. - **Float32:** regression coverage for precision near an `le` boundary. - **UInt64:** regression coverage for one-count differences above `2^53`. - **Compliance:** add classic histogram fraction queries to the PromQL compliance cases. - **Checks:** `git diff --check` and Python syntax validation for the integration test files.

Both were carved out of a broader parent permission and were not documented: - `control-plane:organization:create-service`, split out of `organization:manage` - `control-plane:service:delete`, split out of `service:manage` Splitting `service:delete` out also renames the role editor label for `service:manage` from "Manage and delete selected services" to "Manage selected services". The docs quoted the old label in two places, which would have contradicted the new `service:delete` row by implying `service:manage` still covers deletion, so both are corrected: the ClickPipes row on this page and the **Data Sources** tab note in the custom roles guide. ### Test plan Docs-only change, no code paths touched. - Render `/cloud/security/console-roles` and confirm the two new rows appear under **Organization** and **Service (general)**. - Render the custom roles guide and confirm the **Data Sources** callout names the current label. ### Edge cases - `grep` confirms no occurrence of the old `Manage and Delete Selected Services` label remains in the English docs. - Only the English sources are edited. The `ja`, `ru`, `zh`, `ar`, `pt-BR`, `ko`, `fr`, and `es` copies use a machine-translation structure (`<div id=...>` wrappers rather than `{#anchor}` headings) and look pipeline-generated, so they are expected to pick this up on the next regeneration rather than being hand-edited here. - Both permissions sit behind system feature flags that are currently off in production. While a flag is off, the child permission is hidden in the role editor and the parent still covers the behavior, so this describes the post-rollout state and should land after the flags reach full rollout. - `service:manage` is still described as covering "lifecycle operations". Deletion is arguably a lifecycle operation, so that phrase is a little loose now that `service:delete` exists, but the separate row resolves it in context and a negative disclaimer on one row would break the table's one-line style. ### Risks Low. Documentation text only, no build or runtime impact. The main risk is timing rather than correctness: until the feature flags are fully rolled out, these pages describe labels and a permission split that are not yet visible in the console.

signals.title: Do not prune with an invalid polygon in pointInPolygon key analysis
signals.text: Do not prune with an invalid polygon in pointInPolygon key analysis <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114630 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed rows missing from the result of a `SELECT` filtered by `pointInPolygon` over a MergeTree primary key when the polygon argument is an invalid constant literal and `validate_polygons = 0`. Primary key analysis derived granule pruning from a polygon it never validated, and dropped granules holding matching rows. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114630 ### Description Two defects, both making primary key analysis prune from a polygon that disagrees with the one `pointInPolygon` evaluates. **Invalid ring.** The constant ring was never checked with `boost::geometry::is_valid`, unlike `parseConstPolygon` and the GeoParquet pruning path. `bg::correct` does not repair a self-intersection, so the unusable ring reached `bg::intersects`, whose relate-based answer disagrees with the grid algorithm the function evaluates. On the reporter's reproducer: 849 rows against 875 for the same data with a key permitting no such atom, 26 lost. Both argument forms are affected, correcting the issue text: they reach the same lambda, as the reporter's own three-argument case (794 against 820) shows. **Invalid assembly (found in review).** Holes are not stored, so the filter tests the shell alone, which over-approximates the function only while the assembled shell-plus-holes shape is valid. A valid *concave* shell with a self-intersecting hole loses rows: an L-shaped shell with a bowtie hole returned 3446 against 3556, the 110 missing rows all in the shell's notch, which the shell excludes but the assembly includes. A convex shell cannot expose this, having no notch outside its own outline. Both are fixed by validating the shape the function itself validates and declining the atom otherwise, so no pruning happens and the scan returns the correct rows. This mirrors `GeoBbox.h`, which refuses a pruning bbox rather than throwing; index analysis must not raise user errors. Neither check is gated on `validate_polygons`: with validation enabled the query already fails earlier, so gating would keep the bug for exactly the users who can reach it. `force_primary_key = 1` now raises `INDEX_NOT_USED` on these shapes, no key atom being left to force. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Debug build, both directions, Build IDs asserted against the running servers. | Case (`validate_polygons = 0`) | Before | After | Expected | |---|---|---|---| | bowtie ring, 2-arg, both modes | 849 | 875 | 875 | | bowtie ring, 3-arg with hole, both modes | 794 | 820 | 820 | | rows lost / gained | 26 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | | valid concave shell + bowtie hole, both modes | 3446 | 3556 | 3556 | | rows lost, that case | 110 | 0 | 0 | | degenerate 2-point ring | 8 | 8 | 8 | | valid convex ring | 1681 | 1681 | 1681 | | valid ring, granules | 289/1250 | 289/1250 | unchanged | | valid shell + valid hole, granules | 85/1250 | 85/1250 | unchanged | | invalid ring, granules | 188/1250 | 1250/1250 | no pruning | | invalid assembly, granules | 733/1250 | 1250/1250 | no pruning | Every shape newly declined is already rejected by the function under the default `validate_polygons = 1`, verified per shape, so pruning changes only under the explicit opt-out. Valid shapes keep pruning: interior hole, two disjoint holes, holes sharing a vertex, clockwise and explicitly-closed holes, concave shell with interior hole, and the existing with-holes minmax test. The test fails on the unpatched binary with exactly the pre-fix counts and passes 50/50 randomized. Of 153 selected `polygon`, `key_condition`, `primary_key_index`, `geo_` and `minmax_index` tests, 15 failed and none is attributable: 9 fail identically unpatched, and 6 are order or sandbox-config flakes measured on both binaries. </details>

signals.title: Check PREWHERE column support inside lambda bodies
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114206 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a logical error and a `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` error when a `PREWHERE` expression reads a table column inside a lambda body, e.g. `PREWHERE arrayMap(x -> t.c, [1])[1] > 0`. Such a column was never checked against the table expression's supported `PREWHERE` columns, so a `Merge` whose children declare it with different types built the filter against the wrong one rather than refusing it. Also fixes `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION` for a `PREWHERE` expression calling an executable or WebAssembly UDF that does not itself read a `JOIN` column. ### Description `CollectPrewhereTableExpressionVisitor::needChildVisit` skipped `LAMBDA`, so a column read only inside a lambda body never reached `visitImpl`, the one place that picks the table expression `PREWHERE` reads from and enforces `supportedPrewhereColumns`. On master: - A `Merge` whose children declare `x` as `UInt32` and `Nullable(UInt32)` excludes `x` from its contract, but the guard that would refuse it never runs. The filter is built against the root's type while a child reads another, so the lambda's `ColumnFunction` capture fails in the reader: `Cannot capture column N ... incompatible type`, a logical error, so an abort under sanitizers. - With no column visited, `PREWHERE` is pinned to the first table expression, so a lambda over another fails `Code: 10` (#114206). The fix descends into lambda bodies, skipping only the lambda's own parameters by testing for a `LAMBDA_ARGS` column source, as the sibling `CollectSourceColumnsVisitor` already does: a node type, not a function name, so all higher-order functions are covered. Collecting those columns makes two latent omissions live. `ReplaceColumnsVisitor` never entered a lambda either, so the `JOIN` type substitution that `PREWHERE` must roll back survived inside a lambda and aborted at `join_use_nulls = 1`. Rolling it back also re-derives the lambda's parameter types from the array its higher-order function iterates. It also rebuilt every function in the expression, replaced or not, through `FunctionFactory`, which does not own UDFs: hence the `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`. It is now bounded to replaced subtrees, so a UDF reading a restored `JOIN` column stays refused as on master. Reported by @ nikitamikhaylov on [#113768](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113768#issuecomment-5268962866): one `Server died` in that PR's unrelated Stress test (amd_msan), [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113768&sha=8f8aef10f381104c26153d7fb829b7e196825b0b&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress+test+%28amd_msan%29). <details><summary>Validation</summary> Reproducer (aborts on master, `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` with this change): ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); CREATE TABLE t2 (x Nullable(UInt32)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t VALUES (100); INSERT INTO t2 VALUES (300); SET enable_analyzer = 1; SELECT x FROM merge(currentDatabase(), '^t') AS m PREWHERE (arrayMap(x -> m.x, [1])[1]) > 50; ``` `04879_prewhere_lambda_body_column_check`: 29 arms A/B'd against a base build, 8 refusals and 21 row-returning. Every refusal and every `join_use_nulls` shape is paired with the same query without a lambda, so each expected outcome is justified against master's own answer. | arm | base | with this change | |---|---|---| | diverging child types, lambda reads `m.x` (also `*`, `arrayFilter`) | abort | `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` | | `ARRAY JOIN`ed alias inside a lambda | `Code: 10` | `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` | | lambda over the second table of a `JOIN` | `Code: 10` | resolves to that table | | `LEFT JOIN`, right column in `arrayExists`, `join_use_nulls` 0 and 1 (#114206) | abort or `Code: 10` | `1` / `2` | | the same four without a lambda | as after the change | unchanged | | agreeing types; `WHERE`; unrestricted table; shadowed parameter | rows | unchanged | `04889_prewhere_lambda_executable_udf` covers the UDF case in 9 arms, with a built-in control. Five mutation arms, disjoint casualties: reverting `needChildVisit` re-introduces the abort and the `Code: 10`; dropping the `LAMBDA_ARGS` guard breaks `04108`; reverting `ReplaceColumnsVisitor` aborts in `ActionsDAG`; dropping either return-type refresh or the parameter-type re-derivation aborts in planning or in `ColumnFunction::appendArgument`. `04108`, `03036_prewhere_lambda_function`, `00729_prewhere_array_join` and `02955_analyzer_using_functional_args` pass unchanged. Both new tests ran 50x, 0 failures: `04879` under randomized settings, `04889` at `clickhouse-local` defaults. </details>

signals.title: Show file sizes next to artifact links in CI reports
signals.text: Praktika reports link to files — build artifacts, job logs, uploaded reports — without saying how large they are. A link to `clickhouse-common-static_26.8.1.1332_amd64.deb` gives no hint whether it is 300 KiB or 1.2 GiB, which matters when deciding what to download from a report such as https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=1bfa2815c410fb75b3fe6cfa4ef7877d82b63ea6&name_0=MasterCI Now every link to an uploaded file shows its size: `clickhouse-common-static_26.8.1.1332_amd64.deb (1.2 GiB)`, in both places file links appear — the widget on a job page and the expanded info row of any result. The size cannot be fetched by the report page itself: it is served from `s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports`, build artifacts live on `clickhouse-builds.s3.amazonaws.com`, and neither bucket sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so a cross-origin `HEAD` request is blocked by the browser. Instead the size is recorded at upload time: `copy_file_to_s3` remembers the size of every object it uploads, and `Result` stores it in `ext["link_sizes"]` as a `{link: bytes}` map for `json.html` to render. This costs about 0.3% of a gzipped report. Links with no recorded size — a link to another report, or any report produced before this change — render exactly as before. `json.html` has to be deployed for existing report URLs to pick up the rendering change. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1383` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: CI: run the full test suite only when review threads are resolved
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114724 While a PR has unresolved review threads, running the full test suite is a waste: the code is expected to change again once the review comments are addressed. This PR implements the gate requested in the issue: - A new `review_threads.py` pre-hook in the `Config Workflow` counts the PR's unresolved review threads (via GraphQL `reviewThreads`) and stores the state in the workflow kv data. While threads are unresolved, `should_skip_job` runs only builds and the preliminary checks (`Style check`, `Fast test`), plus the `Code Review` job — the AI review keeps re-checking pushed code and resolves its own addressed threads, which is what re-triggers the full suite automatically. - The `can_be_merged.py` post-hook re-checks the live thread state at finish time and turns the `Mergeable Check` red while threads are unresolved, or while only the limited pipeline ran (even if the threads were resolved mid-run — the full suite still has not run). The per-run verdict is recorded in a new `Review Threads` commit status, which doubles as immediate feedback on the PR. This also makes the decision on the AI review's comments once they are ready, as suggested in the issue: comments posted during the run are seen by the finish-time check. - A new `Rerun On Review Threads` workflow detects state changes and re-runs the last completed `PR` workflow run for the current head commit whenever the recorded verdict disagrees with the live state (thread resolved/unresolved, new review comments, the override label added/removed). Previously succeeded jobs are restored from the CI cache, so the re-run only executes the previously skipped jobs. Review-thread events on PRs from forks carry a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so they are relayed through a trivial `Review Threads Signal` workflow and handled on its `workflow_run` completion in the trusted default-branch context; `PR` workflow completions are watched too, to catch threads resolved while a run was still in flight. A safety cap (5 attempts per run) prevents any reconciliation bug from re-running one workflow forever. - The gate can be bypassed with the new `ignore-unresolved-threads` label (fetched fresh from the API, so adding the label and re-running works; the label also triggers the re-run automatically). `ci-force-all` bypasses it as well, like all other job filtering. - `retry_infra_failures.yml` learned to not treat a `Finish Workflow` failure caused by this merge gate as an infrastructure failure. - Failure direction: if the thread state cannot be fetched at config time, nothing is skipped (fail toward more testing); at finish time the check fails close (the `Mergeable Check` goes red). The `ignore-unresolved-threads` label has been created in the repository. Documentation: a new `Review threads check` section in `docs/resources/develop-contribute/contribute/continuous-integration.mdx`. Tests: `ci/tests/test_review_threads_gate.py` pins the decision functions and their integration into `should_skip_job` (what is skipped, what keeps running, the merge-gate truth table, the commit-status description budget). ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)

signals.title: CI: run only the selected tests in the sanitizer functional tests in PRs
signals.text: The sanitizer flavors of `Stateless tests` ran the whole suite in every pull request: 17 jobs for the ASan/UBSan, TSan and MSan builds. Under the assumption in the issue - that the stress tests with sanitizers are a stronger check than a plain functional run - those jobs now run only the tests selected for the change. The new `selected tests` option of `ci/jobs/functional_tests.py` runs an ordinary functional test run over the subset that `Targeting` already computes for the targeted check: the tests the pull request changes, the tests that already failed in this pull request, and the tests covering the changed lines according to the coverage database. Unlike the `targeted` check, it does not rerun that selection many times - it is a plain run with a shorter list of tests. The selection is a few hundred tests, so the batches of the full-suite jobs collapse into a single job per flavor: 17 jobs become 8. What still covers the whole suite in a pull request: the debug and plain binary functional test jobs, and the stress tests, which run the functional tests under every sanitizer with heavy concurrency and randomized settings. The master workflow is unchanged and keeps running the full suite in every flavor. Also in this change: * When the selection cannot be fetched (the coverage database or the GitHub diff is unavailable), the job runs the full suite instead of testing less than it would have without the selection, and says so in the report. This also makes a local run of these jobs work. * Tests the job flavor would never run (`no-parallel` tests in a `parallel` job and vice versa) are dropped from the selection, and the job is skipped when nothing is left for it. * `clickhouse-test` exits with code 1 when every test it was given is filtered out - e.g. all the selected tests are tagged `no-tsan` in a TSan job. For a run over an explicit list of tests (flaky, targeted, `selected tests`) that is now reported as SKIPPED instead of a failure; for a full-suite run it stays a failure, since there it means a broken filter. Unit tests for the new logic are in `ci/tests/test_selected_tests_run.py`. `.github/workflows/pull_request.yml` was regenerated via `python3 -m ci.praktika yaml`. ### Verification in this pull request's own CI This pull request changes no source file and no test under `tests/queries`, so nothing is relevant to select and the new jobs correctly report SKIPPED. To exercise the path that actually runs a subset, commit 85362432c858e0cd9aadbf57f2895888b9d35863 temporarily touched `00001_select_1.sql` (reverted in the following commit). On that commit, with all builds served from the cache: * `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel, selected tests)` and `Stateless tests (amd_asan_ubsan, distributed plan, parallel, selected tests)` ran, and the report shows the three selection passes followed by the single selected test - `00001_select_1 OK 1.01s`. * `Stateless tests (amd_asan_ubsan, db disk, distributed plan, sequential, selected tests)` skipped, because the only changed test is parallel-safe and the flavor filter left it nothing to run. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114730&sha=85362432c858e0cd9aadbf57f2895888b9d35863&name_0=PR Possible follow-up, not done here: once the test list is short, the job start dominates the run - in the TSan run above, `Start ClickHouse Server` (which prepares the stateful datasets `test.hits`, `test.visits`, TPC-DS and TPC-H) took 324 seconds out of a 418-second job. Skipping the stateful preparation when no stateful test is selected needs a reliable way to tell, so it is left out of this change. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114725 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ...

signals.title: Keep two refreshable-MV tests runnable on a Replicated database
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112247 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04501_distributed_query_client_version_internal_contexts` and `04661_refreshable_mv_cancel_during_planning` each create a non-APPEND refreshable materialized view over a non-replicated target. On the `DBReplicated` test arm the server refuses that shape by design (`Code: 36 ... refreshable materialized view, no APPEND, replicated database, non-replicated table ... Refusing to create`), so the CREATE always fails and neither test reaches its assertions. This is not intermittent: every run of both tests on that arm carries the refusal, master included. The failures were invisible because the functional-test diagnostics rerun rebuilds the command without the job's own `--replicated-database` flag, so the failure does not reproduce, is labelled flaky, and is reported green on the coverage job. That half is a separate defect, tracked in #112247. I did not add `no-replicated-database`. Both covered sites are APPEND-independent, so an APPEND fixture keeps the tests running on every flavour instead of skipping them, which is what commit `e73f3f142e5f` established for this refusal. Each test switches to `APPEND` with `all_replicas = 1` (`SYSTEM REFRESH VIEW`, `system.processes` and a non-replicated target are all replica-local, so the refresh has to stay on the connected replica), a relative `AFTER 1 YEAR` period, and `EMPTY`. 04661 additionally triggers its one refresh explicitly, which also removes the cross-replica concurrency its old `every 1 second` schedule had. Two test files, no source change. Validated locally against a 3-server Replicated cluster built from `tests/config/install.sh --db-replicated`: both tests fail before the change and pass after it, and reverting each test's covered site (the initiator version fill in `createRefreshContext`; the early `executing_query_status` publication in `refreshTask`) makes the corresponding test fail again, so neither fixture passes vacuously. 100/100 randomized runs green on the Replicated arm and 100/100 on the ordinary one, with no skips. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1413` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Split 03469_json_read_subcolumns_combined_2_wide_merge_tree into four smaller tests
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `03469_json_read_subcolumns_combined_2_wide_merge_tree` builds an 80k-row Wide-part `JSON` table and runs 71 SELECTs over its subcolumns, 60 of them `format Null` full-table scans. In a Wide part every JSON path/type pair is its own substream, so each scan re-reads all of them, and on object storage under a sanitizer that is a round trip per granule. On `Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, parallel, 1/2)` the worst passing run is 436960 ms against the 600 s cap, on a p50 of 112 s. The compact sibling, same fixture and SELECTs, crossed that cap 6 times in the last 60 days, 4 on master. This is margin restoration, not a fix for a currently red test. @ Avogar asked for this split and scoped it to the public repo. The request was relayed from a repository not readable here, so I have no comment link to give. A `Random settings limits` clamp cannot help here: this test's DDL already pins `index_granularity=8192`, so no randomized value is left to floor. (Such a clamp did fix the compact sibling, whose DDL never pinned it.) The remaining lever is less work per file. This splits the 71 SELECTs across four files, `_2_1_` through `_2_4_`, along the blank-line block seams the file already had. Every statement is carried verbatim and each file repeats the preamble byte for byte, so the four union to the original statement list and their `.reference` files to the original 26 lines. Object storage keeps running all of it: no storage-skip tag and the fixture stays at 80k rows. All four pass with no reference diff, plus 50 randomized runs each. The worst file runs in 43% of the original's wall time on 30% of its scan bytes, still on `Wide` parts with 80000 rows. Arity is four because three was measured and fell short. <details> <summary>Measured per-file cost (local debug build, 3 runs each)</summary> | file | blocks | stmts | wall | vs original | scan MiB | vs original | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | original | 1-11 | 71 | 1.799 s | 100% | 533.2 | 100% | | `_2_1_wide` | 1, 2 | 6 | 0.711 s | 39.5% | 162.6 | 30.5% | | `_2_2_wide` | 3, 4, 5, 6 | 33 | 0.736 s | 40.9% | 144.6 | 27.1% | | `_2_3_wide` | 7, 8 | 14 | 0.699 s | 38.9% | 101.0 | 18.9% | | `_2_4_wide` | 9, 10, 11 | 18 | 0.776 s | 43.2% | 125.1 | 23.5% | A three-file split was implemented and measured first: its worst file was 52.8% of the original's wall time, because block 2 alone is 29% of the scan bytes and blocks are atomic seams. Local disk bounds compute and bytes read, not object-storage latency, so this is a lower bound on the CI win rather than a prediction. The insert preamble now runs four times instead of once, which is the price of the split; at five files the extra preamble costs more than the scan reduction saves. On the clamp: `ClientBase::addMergeTreeSettings` only injects a randomized MergeTree setting when the DDL has not already set it, so `index_granularity=8192` in the `CREATE TABLE` wins. Across the 200 randomized runs, 224 of 224 `CREATE TABLE` statements carried both that pin and `min_rows_for_wide_part=1`, so the granule explosion that hit the compact sibling stays shut in all four copies. `03469_json_read_subcolumns_combined_1_wide_merge_tree` carries a `no-s3-storage, no-azure-blob-storage` "too slow" skip and is arguably a second split candidate, but it is out of scope here. </details> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1414` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Adaptive lazy execution of short-circuit function arguments (continues #73776)
signals.text: This continues #73776 by @lgbo-ustc, whose branch was ~17 months behind `master` and could no longer be merged mechanically (27 conflicting files in the hottest central code). The author's commits are preserved; on top of them this reconciles the change with the current `master` and reworks the plumbing. Short-circuit evaluation decides *statically* which arguments of `and`, `or`, `if` and `multiIf` are executed lazily. Lazy execution is not free: the rows which are not needed are filtered out and the result is expanded back to the original size. When the filtered out part is small, or the argument itself is cheap, this overhead is larger than the work it saves. This adds an opt-in adaptive mode: the execution of every function is profiled (elapsed time and processed rows), and every 20000 rows the decision is revisited per action - lazy execution is turned off when the estimated cost of the full execution is lower than the measured cost of the lazy execution, and turned back on when the per-row cost of the action grows significantly. Actions whose function can throw an exception on invalid input values (for example `intDiv(1, 0)`) are never switched to eager execution, so the short-circuit protection is preserved. The mode is disabled by default and enabled with the new experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`. Changes on top of the original branch: * The flag no longer travels through `ExpressionStep`/`FilterStep` constructors, the query plan optimizations, the planner and the step serialization. It lives in `ExpressionActionsSettings` next to `enable_lazy_columns_replication`, which removes ~20 files from the change and all the ripple through `QueryPlan/Optimizations`. * `ExpressionActions::execute` and `executeOnColumns` stay `const`; the free `executeAction` became a member with three virtual hooks (`shouldExecuteLazily`, `executeFunction`, `finalizeBlockExecution`) which `AdaptiveExpressionActions` overrides. * The profile plumbing follows the current `IExecutableFunction` chain, including `executeWithoutReplicatedColumns`, which did not exist when the branch was written. * `is_no_except` is computed only when the setting is enabled, so nothing changes for the default path. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`, which enables dynamic evaluation of whether a short-circuit function's argument should be lazily executed. The execution of the functions is profiled at runtime, and the lazy execution of an argument is disabled when it costs more than executing the argument on all the rows. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73776

signals.title: Build Debian packages for the release builds only
signals.text: The `Stress test` was the only job installing the Debian packages of the debug, sanitizer and CFI builds, and it can take the plain `clickhouse` binary instead — that binary is built and uploaded for every build type anyway. Every other consumer of the packages (`Install packages`, `Compatibility check`, `Upgrade check`, the server Docker images and the release jobs) runs on a release build. So the release builds keep their packages, and nine of the eleven packaging steps go away, together with the `DESTDIR` install that copies the whole binary, and the upload and download of the resulting packages. The stress test now sets up the paths the packages own from the binary: `install_binary` in `stress_tests.lib` symlinks `/usr/bin/clickhouse*` at it, installs the default `config.xml` and `users.xml`, and unpacks the self-extracting archive up front — decompressing a sanitizer build under `clickhouse start` would eat into its wait for the pid file and race any concurrent `clickhouse local`. `install_packages` stays for the upgrade check, which installs an actual release. Symbolization is unaffected: `clickhouse_split_debug_symbols` leaves `programs/clickhouse` untouched and strips only the copy it installs, so the binary artifact carries its debug info even for a release build. For the sanitizer builds `clickhouse-common-static-dbg` was empty to begin with, since they do not set `SPLIT_DEBUG_SYMBOLS`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)

signals.title: Fix a server crash when merging -OrNull/-OrDefault states under group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114690 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server crash that happens when aggregate states of the `-OrNull` or `-OrDefault` combinators are merged with `group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'` and a non-zero `max_rows_to_group_by`, for example when a query reads through an aggregate projection. ### Description Under `group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'` the aggregator freezes its hash table once `max_rows_to_group_by` is exceeded, and every subsequent row whose key is absent gets the overflow-row pointer. That pointer is `nullptr` whenever `overflow_row` is off, which is the case for any query that is not `GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS`, so `places[i] == nullptr` is a normal value on the merge path meaning "this key did not fit, skip the row". `Aggregator::mergeStreamsImplCase` states this in an in-source comment and hands the array to `mergeBatch` without filtering. Every batch consumer honours that contract except `AggregateFunctionOrFill::mergeBatch`, which unconditionally dereferenced `places[i]` to OR its trailing "was anything aggregated" flag byte, so a null place became a write through a null pointer. `IAggregateFunctionHelper::mergeBatch` and `AggregateFunctionOrFill::addBatch` already carry the same `if (places[i])` guard; this adds the third and last instance of it. Reproduced on master `bf580ecb357f39df87f814ad214698f2c8aeab17` with a debug build: a `MergeTree` table with an aggregate projection queried with `max_rows_to_group_by = 10, group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'` dies with `Address: 0x8. Access: write` at `AggregateFunctionOrFill.h:258`, for both `-OrNull` and `-OrDefault` and for both the single-number and the fixed-keys aggregation methods. The added test covers those arms plus both `-Tuple`/`-OrNull` nesting orders, and fails (the server dies) without the change. Behaviour changes only for rows the aggregator has already decided to drop, so no query that never trips `max_rows_to_group_by` under mode `any` is affected. Found by the targeted AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)` and `..., old_compatibility`, STID 2575-398a): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114690&sha=9b5110134d760b3aace6e8c767073cb51c338233&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29. The defect is on master and independent of that PR, which only made the path easier to hit.

signals.title: Do not read FINAL merging columns that the output header no longer carries
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/91849 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Unexpected number of kept output positions after removing unused columns from `ReadFromMergeTree`") raised by a `SELECT ... FINAL` whose `PREWHERE` uses a column that `FINAL` needs for merging (`ver`, `is_deleted`, `sign`) and which does not select that column. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/91849 ### Description A `SELECT ... FINAL` whose `PREWHERE` consumes a merging column it does not select fails with `LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected number of kept output positions after removing unused columns from ReadFromMergeTree`. `removeUnusedColumns` added back to the read set every `getColumnsRequiredForMergingFinal` column, including ones `PREWHERE` had consumed and the output header no longer carried. `kept_output_positions` is sized from the old header, so the header recomputed from the widened read set was longer and tripped the count assertion. That widening is redundant: `initializePipeline` already appends the sorting-key columns plus `is_deleted`/`sign`/`version` for `FINAL`, and passes `original_column_names` separately so the extras are projected back off. So retain a merging column at analysis time only when the output header has it. The header keeps its size, `kept_output_positions` stays correct, and the assertion is kept. This is option 1 of the two I put to @antaljanosbenjamin above, reached by not widening the read set at all, so no position mapping is rebuilt and no grown root header has to be reconciled. Say so if you would rather the general fix (option 2) land. It also drops the first version's `canRemoveUnusedColumns` exclusion, so pruning now applies where that version declined it. The merge still gets its key columns: `is_deleted` stays in the read set, and every merging mode returns the same deduplicated rows as with `query_plan_remove_unused_columns = 0` on multi-part tables. Test `04906` covers both entry points, four merging modes, the optimizer-moved `PREWHERE`, the two late header rebuilds and duplicate output names, and asserts pruning still applies. Found by the AST fuzzer and the stress test on unrelated pull requests; also reproduces on a plain `FROM t FINAL`. - `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107305&sha=1a49e7372d0f969cd06d7ba237d8eb3b3461e814&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - `Stress test (arm_asan_ubsan, s3)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108069&sha=77f495e71c33bb2c27441fa12f9deb0fdb7e24f2&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29

signals.title: Remove `WINDOW VIEW`
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61069 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/88706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `WINDOW VIEW` feature is removed, together with the `WATCH` statement and the `windowID` function. It has been non-functional since version 24.12 (inserts into the source table were silently not delivered to window views) and was never supported by the analyzer, which is enabled by default since 24.3. The settings `allow_experimental_window_view`, `window_view_clean_interval`, `window_view_heartbeat_interval`, and `wait_for_window_view_fire_signal_timeout` are kept as obsolete no-ops. The time-window functions `tumble`, `tumbleStart`, `tumbleEnd`, `hop`, `hopStart`, and `hopEnd` are kept. If you still have window views defined, drop them before upgrading: a server that finds a window view in its metadata fails to start (`Cannot parse definition from metadata file ... (SYNTAX_ERROR)`), the same way the removal of the `Lazy` database engine behaves. Similar functionality will be reimplemented on top of streaming queries (issue [#114738](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738)). The removal, in detail: - `src/Storages/WindowView/` (`StorageWindowView`, `WindowViewSource`, `StorageBlocks`), `WatermarkTransform`, the `ParserCreateWindowViewQuery` parser, and the whole `WATCH` statement stack (`ParserWatchQuery`, `ASTWatchQuery`, `InterpreterWatchQuery`, the `IStorage::watch` virtual) — window views were the last implementor of `watch`, and the `WATCH` statement was already documented as deprecated. - The `ASTCreateQuery` watermark/lateness fields and their AST JSON serialization and validation. The `clickhouse_json` boundary fails closed rather than silently reinterpreting legacy payloads: `ASTCreateQuery::readJSON` rejects a set `is_window_view`, watermark strategy or `allowed_lateness` flag and the `watermark_function` / `lateness_function` children (otherwise such a payload deserialized as an ordinary `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` and was executed as an immediate-population table create), while `ASTViewTargets::readJSON` rejects the `Inner` target kind, which nothing produces any more and which formatted back to parser-impossible `INNER ENGINE ...` SQL. Both are covered by `04892_ast_json_removed_window_view_state`; the `PushingToWindowViewSink` and `ViewType::WINDOW` branches in `InsertDependenciesBuilder`; window-view special cases in `InterpreterCreateQuery`, `InterpreterInsertQuery`, `StorageFactory`, `DatabaseOrdinary`, `DatabaseReplicated`, `DDLDependencyVisitor`, `QueryFuzzer`, BuzzHouse, and the ArrowFlight table-type mapping. - The `windowID` function and the `UInt32` single-argument forms of `tumbleStart`/`tumbleEnd`/`hopStart`/`hopEnd` (they only accepted `windowID` output). The rest of the time-window function family stays, since these are ordinary functions usable in a regular `GROUP BY` and are exactly the vocabulary for the streaming-queries replacement. - The keywords `WATCH`, `EVENTS`, `ALLOWED_LATENESS`, and `STRICTLY_ASCENDING` (the `WATERMARK` keyword stays: the streaming-queries `WATERMARK FOR` clause uses it), the error code `QUERY_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_WINDOW_VIEW`, and the corresponding fuzzer dictionary and ANTLR grammar entries. - Kept for compatibility: `QueryViewsLogElement::ViewType::WINDOW` (so existing `system.query_views_log` tables keep their schema) and `ViewTarget::Inner` (so old DDL log entries still parse), following the same pattern as the `LIVE VIEW` removal. - The `allow_experimental_window_view` constraint in `tests/docker_scripts/stress_tests.lib` is kept (only the constraint, not the profile value, which would mark an obsolete setting as changed and add a `system.warnings` entry): the upgrade check runs the previous release's suite under the previous release's binary, whose window-view tests are not dropped afterwards because `--upgrade-check` implies `--fake-drop`, and the leftover metadata would then stop the new server from starting. - Tests: the four remaining window-view tests are removed. The pure time-window-function coverage of `01049_window_view_window_functions` moved to a new `04891_time_window_functions` test, which also pins the new `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` behavior of `tumbleStart(UInt32)`. - Docs: the `Window View` section of `CREATE VIEW`, the `WATCH` page (with its navigation entries and locale twins) are removed and the old-slug redirects retargeted; the window-view entries are removed from the generated settings/functions reference pages (second commit, hence the `pr-autogenerated-docs` label): the `window-view.mdx` settings page, the four settings' entries in the pages/manifest/navigation/settings explorer, and the `windowID` section of `time-window-functions.mdx`. The unrelated drift accumulated on master since the last nightly regeneration is deliberately not included; the nightly docs-autogen job will pick it up. Why now: the feature has been non-functional since Dec 2024 — commit `ceae84c87a2` removed the explicit view-dependency registration and `DDLDependencyVisitor` never extracted the source table of a `CREATE WINDOW VIEW`, so inserts into the source table were silently not pushed to window views, and direct inserts failed with `std::out_of_range` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493). Nobody noticed for ~1.5 years. It was never ported to the analyzer (with `enable_analyzer = 1`, the default, existing window views load permanently inert), its tests were removed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73822 because they were inherently flaky, and it kept costing triage time (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 is a recent server SIGSEGV through `getSourceTableSelectQuery`). The full assessment, including the plan for reimplementing this functionality on top of streaming queries (`SELECT ... FROM t STREAM`, `WATERMARK FOR`, emit-on-watermark windowed aggregation), is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Treat a NULL nullable string column on the right of IN as absent
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN` for a tuple on the left of `IN` and a `Nullable(String)` column on the right, as in `SELECT (1, 2) IN (rhs) FROM (SELECT CAST(NULL AS Nullable(String)) AS rhs)`. A `NULL` value of such a column is now an absent set element, so the query returns `0` for `IN` and `1` for `NOT IN`, matching the constant right-hand side and the `Nullable(Nothing)` column already covered by test `04870`. ### Description Follow-up to #104993 for the review finding at https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993#discussion_r3773210901. The row-wise rewrite for a bare column on the right of `IN` casts a string-typed right-hand side to the tuple type of the left-hand side. Its guard strips `Nullable` and `LowCardinality`, so a `Nullable(String)` column enters that branch, while the cast target stays the non-`Nullable` tuple. `CAST(Nullable(String) -> Tuple(...))` rejects a `NULL` source value, so the `NULL` row failed with `Code: 349 CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN` instead of being treated as absent from the set. The fix handles nullability before the cast and keeps the cast target non-`Nullable`, as the block intends: * the right-hand side is wrapped in `ifNull(rhs, <tuple default>)`, which makes the cast total, so it cannot throw whatever `short_circuit_function_evaluation` is set to; * the comparison is wrapped in `if(isNull(rhs), <absent>, ...)`, which supplies the "element absent" answer and makes the substituted value unreachable. Both layers are needed: without the guard, a left-hand tuple that equals the substituted default compares equal and returns wrong results; without the substitution, a lazy guard alone still throws under `short_circuit_function_evaluation = 'disable'`. Test `04898` pins each direction, and its left-hand tuples are the default value of their type on purpose so that removing the guard reddens it. Only the `NULL` row changes. A present value is still parsed and compared, a non-parseable one still raises `CANNOT_PARSE_INPUT_ASSERTION_FAILED` (`04871`), a plain `String` right-hand side keeps its exact node shape, a `Nullable` tuple on the left keeps its three-valued result, and a tuple with a bare `Nothing` element keeps the previous lowering because it has no default value to substitute. `FixedString` is excluded because its cast to a tuple is unsupported for either nullability.

signals.title: Support DEFINER / SQL SECURITY for dictionaries
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85293 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Support `DEFINER` and `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` for dictionaries, like for views. A dictionary with a local `CLICKHOUSE` source can name the user whose privileges its load runs with, instead of storing a user and password in `SOURCE(...)`. Rotating that user's password no longer breaks the dictionary. ### Description A dictionary with a `CLICKHOUSE` source authenticates every load with the credentials in `SOURCE(...)`, so rotating that password breaks all later reloads. A deployment issuing short-lived credentials must embed a long-lived one, or load as `default` with excess authority. Name the identity instead: `DEFINER = dict_owner`, with no `USER`/`PASSWORD` in `SOURCE(...)`. The load then runs with that user's privileges, consults no credential, and is bounded by the definer's settings constraints. It reuses the view definer machinery, inheriting the `SET DEFINER` grant check and the guard against dropping a live definer. `04869_dictionary_definer.sh` covers rotation against a stored-credential control, privilege and settings bounding, `SET DEFINER`, the metadata round trip, every rejection, and locality both ways, each arm mutation-verified. Scoped to a **local** `CLICKHOUSE` source, as @ pufit confirmed on the issue: any other authenticates against a foreign system with credentials a locally resolved identity cannot replace, so the clause is rejected at `CREATE` time. Locality is decided on the effective configuration, resolving named collections and `PORT tcpPort()` first; an unprovable source is rejected too. `DEFINER` is the only accepted type and must name somebody: `INVOKER` because a dictionary loads from a background pool with no invoker, `NONE` because nothing consults the type at load time. A dictionary without the clause is unchanged; `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Dictionary(...) SQL SECURITY ...` keeps failing closed. Three limits come from the shared UUID-keyed definer registry, and each is master's behaviour for views today: an ephemeral `<user>:definer` clone can go uncollected when a `CREATE` is rejected late or the object leaves a UUID-bearing database; drop protection does not apply in `Memory` or `Ordinary` databases; and a `DROP USER` racing a `CREATE` can pass its dependency check before the object registers (over 60 attempts, 21 hits for views on master against 2 for dictionaries here).

signals.title: continue-all-prs: support `codex` workers and GPT models
signals.text: Add support for running `utils/continue-all-prs.sh` workers with the `codex` CLI and selecting Codex or general-purpose GPT models. Estimate OpenAI API cost from model-specific input, cached-input, and output pricing, and preserve the existing `claude` behavior by default. signals.title: Pin enable_parallel_replicas off for 00673_subquery_prepared_set_performance
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113575 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `00673_subquery_prepared_set_performance` fails `TOO_DEEP_RECURSION` in `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel)` on its 21-deep nested subquery. Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #113575, whose own randomized-settings minimization pinned the culprit to `enable_parallel_replicas 1` + `parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree 1`. Two facts compose. `tests/clickhouse-test:1772` is the only site that sets `enable_parallel_replicas`, and it is guarded by `automatic_parallel_replicas_mode == 2` (`:1769`, p=0.25), so the culprit pair appears only on mode-2 runs. And `STACK_SIZE_FREE_RATIO` is 20 under TSan versus 2 otherwise (`checkStackSize.cpp:150-157`), so the `maximum stack size: 8388608` in the message is the raw stack while the enforced ceiling is 419430 B. The overshoot is against that TSan-only 5% budget, not against 8 MB. This is a CI signal problem rather than a user-facing one. Measured server-side at the byte ceiling a non-TSan build has (while still paying TSan-inflated frames), nesting is stopped by `max_subquery_depth` (default 100) with `TOO_DEEP_SUBQUERIES` at depth 100, and the stack itself is fine to depth 250. The deepest reachable query is depth 99. CIDB shows one row matching this signature in 180 days and none on master. So this pins the one setting on the one test rather than changing planner recursion: ``` -- Random settings limits: enable_parallel_replicas=(0, 0) ``` I did not use `-- Tags: no-parallel-replicas`: the dedicated `ParallelReplicas` job is `amd_llvm_coverage` only (`job_configs.py:789`, `:795`), so it runs at ratio 2 and uses 8.6% of its ceiling. It cannot hit this limit, and the tag would skip the test there for no benefit. No SQL is changed and the test is not skipped anywhere. <details><summary>Validation</summary> CI-faithful TSan build (clang-22, `-DSANITIZE=thread`, Build ID `7d85b446...`). The enforced ceiling is the independent variable, calibrated with `ulimit -s 7000` into the window between the two arms' measured depth-21 usage (355408 < ceiling <= 362576), since CI's absolute byte count is not reproducible here (CI's frames measure ~18% wider on the same compiler). | arm | result | |---|---| | pre-fix, culprit pair forced at the client, unmodified file | 5/5 `Code: 306`, control 5/5 pass | | pre-fix, real runner, 50 randomized runs | 18 fail / 50; every failure `mode=2` + setting `1`, every pass mode-0 | | directive parses (runner's own parser, real file) | `{'enable_parallel_replicas': (0, 0)}` | | clamp changes the value (runner's own `apply_random_settings_limits`) | mode 2: `1` -> `0`; mode 0: absent both ways | | post-fix, mode 2 forced, value read back | `epr_pre=1 epr_post=0 prnr=1`, 3/3 pass (same harness pre-fix: 5/5 fail) | | negative control: corrupt the directive to `limitsX:` | unparsed, `epr_post=1`, 3/3 fail again | | post-fix, real runner, 50 randomized runs | 50/50 pass, 6-12 runs drew mode 2, zero `306` | | `--no-parallel-replicas` and `--no-random-settings` | run, not skipped | The negative control matters because an unparsed `Random settings limits:` line is just a comment, and because ~75% of runs draw mode 0 and pass regardless of the directive. </details> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1410` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Do not let a post-run coverage diagnostic discard a finished test run's exit code
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `NightlyCoverage` shards exit 1 after every test has already passed. CIDB gets a pseudo-test row `clickhouse-test` / FAIL whose whole context is `clickhouse-test exited with code 1`, while the report shows the shard `OK` with `Failed: 0`. On master: 83 such rows in 30 days, 26 nights, all 8 shards, 6 of them on one nightly. Cause: `main()`'s post-run coverage block printed one diagnostic line built from two `FINAL` aggregates over `system.coverage_log`, the only two statements in that block outside a `try/except`. `clickhouse_execute` defaults to `timeout=30` and re-raises after 5 retries, and the aggregates sit at that cap: the job's own exporter runs the same aggregate over the same 23.4-25.4M rows in 20-29s. The `TimeoutError` propagates out of `main()`, so `sys.exit(exit_code.value)` never runs and Python exits 1 with every result already collected. That costs a red job for a non-failure, and an exit status that no longer separates a test failure from a teardown timeout. The statement is deleted rather than guarded because in this job it is a vestigial duplicate: `CoverageExporter.do()` re-runs the identical aggregate about 30s later, prints a strict superset of the numbers, and raises when the row count is zero. Nothing reads `cov_rows`/`cov_tests`. A local run drops the export stage, so it loses the line rather than seeing it duplicated. Validated locally: the extracted block exits 1 before the change and 0 after, with negative controls confirming the probe is specific to this timeout. Every remaining `clickhouse_execute` in the post-run block is now guarded (checked by AST). The pre-run block is untouched: it is meant to fail the run when coverage is broken. Two siblings are left alone: `coverage_indirect_calls` is redundant the same way but already guarded, and `reportCoverage` is unguarded but no CI job passes `--report-coverage`. CI report, shard 3/8 of the 2026-08-13 nightly: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=3da3cf323b91553960bdf55780a3b94e9deb5793&name_0=NightlyCoverage&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage_per_test%2C%20per_test_coverage%2C%203%2F8%29

signals.title: Propagate NDV through functions with constant arguments
signals.text: ## Summary - Propagate expression NDV bounds through deterministic functions with exactly one row-varying argument. - Track the row-varying argument instead of assuming it is the first child. - Cover `dateTrunc('month', date)`, where the first argument is constant. ## Root cause NDV propagation only handled deterministic single-argument functions and always traversed the first child. As a result, a deterministic expression with constant arguments, such as `dateTrunc('month', order_date)`, lost the NDV of its row-varying input. Aggregation planning then fell back to the input row count. ## Testing - `git diff --check` - Added `ColumnStatsDerivation.FunctionWithConstantArgumentsPropagatesBound` Closes ClickHouse/clickhouse-private#68097 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry: Fixes inaccurate cardinality estimates for deterministic functions with constant arguments, which can improve aggregation query plans for expressions such as `dateTrunc`.

signals.title: Replace the AggregatingInOrderTransform cancellation test with a failpoint integration test
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110104 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107941 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110104 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107941 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04512_aggregation_in_order_cancellation.sh` guards the per-key-interval cancellation check from #110104, but asserts on aggregation CPU as a multiple of scan CPU after a shell-issued `KILL`. It prints `not cancelled in time` on master again: 6 such failures on 2026-08-13 (2 on master, 4 on unrelated PRs), 5 on `amd_asan_ubsan, distributed plan, parallel`. Eighth rewrite of the assertion. The oracle prices the window between "rows are read" and "the `KILL` flips `is_cancelled`", and two `clickhouse-client` startups sit on that path; `04410_primes_source_cancellation.sh:48-49` records ~8 s for one invocation on a loaded sanitizer build. On all five failures that printed the CPU diagnostics the checkpoint was firing, stopping at 48-75 % of the loop, not 100 %: only the window grew, and the shell cannot close it, since read progress is published only after the source's `work()` returns (`ExecutionThreadContext.cpp:57-75`). So this adopts the mechanism `LimitByTransform` already uses (`e20a67394329867` and follow-ups): a `PAUSEABLE_ONCE` failpoint on interval 6, after the cancellation check and inside the loop, a `LOG_TEST` marker in the existing cancellation branch, and an integration test that pauses there, kills, resumes and asserts the marker appears exactly once. No timing, no threshold, no free constant. Exactly once, not merely present: `is_cancelled` latches, so dropping only the `return` prints the marker once per remaining interval (94 here) while every other assertion still passes. Mid-loop matters for the same reason: a pre-loop pause resumes straight into the first `isCancelled()`, staying green with that check hoisted out of the loop, which is what #110104 fixed. All three mutations (checkpoint deleted, check hoisted, `return` deleted) redden the new test, the failpoint still pausing in each so no arm is vacuous. Removing `SYSTEM ENABLE FAILPOINT` fails loudly; `test_limit_by_transform_kill_query` stays green. Hot-path cost is not measurable, and dropping the 40 M-row fixture removes its `max_estimated_execution_time` exposure. `04409_skip_index_build_cancellation.sh` has a weaker form of the same pattern (bounded `KILL ... SYNC` at `timeout 10`); left unchanged.

signals.title: Reject an absurd `kafka_num_consumers` instead of failing an allocation
signals.text: `kafka_disable_num_consumers_limit` lifts the `kafka_num_consumers` limit derived from the number of CPU cores, but nothing else bounded the value. With the setting enabled, a `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Kafka ... kafka_num_consumers = 9223372036854775807` reached `StorageKafka::StorageKafka`, where `consumers.resize(num_consumers)` threw `std::length_error`. That surfaces as `Logical error: 'std::exception. Code: 1001, type: std::length_error, e.what() = vector` (STID 2508-3132) and aborts in the debug build. Found by the AST fuzzer, which randomizes `kafka_disable_num_consumers_limit` and fuzzes the `kafka_num_consumers` literal of `04662_kafka_num_consumers_attach`: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101783&sha=1656dc6761df74e97d13d3fe888a20bd58ce0f57&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29 - Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101783 A single consumer can read any number of partitions, so an absolute cap of 10000 consumers is now enforced regardless of `kafka_disable_num_consumers_limit`, and an over-large value is rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`. The 1000 consumers used by `04662_kafka_num_consumers_attach` keep working. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Reject an absurdly large `kafka_num_consumers` with a clear error instead of failing an allocation inside the `Kafka` table engine. Previously, with `kafka_disable_num_consumers_limit` enabled, such a value produced a `std::length_error` exception.

That PR: (1) Marks the two DROP contexts that `CREATE OR REPLACE` builds internally as DDL-internal (`InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2245` for the non-Atomic `replace_view` path, `:2535` inside `make_drop_context` used by both the post-swap drop of the replaced object and the catch-block cleanup of the … **1. Post-swap internal DROP untested when replaced object is a View or Dictionary** `src/Interpreters/InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2535`, `src/Interpreters/InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2854` **Risk:** `InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2854` runs the post-swap drop with the context from `make_drop_context` (`:2535`); `InterpreterDropQuery.cpp:205` reads `isDDLOrOnClusterInternal` and `:220-228` rewrites the DROP to TRUNCATE when the storage does not store data on disk. signals.title: Do not consult the query context when building a CAST
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109946 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR: Context has expired` exception when a stored expression containing `accurateCastOrDefault` or a `to<Type>OrDefault` function is evaluated after the query that created it has finished, for example a `MATERIALIZED` column default on `INSERT` or a mutation expression. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109946 `CastOverloadResolverImpl` inherited `WithContext`, which holds only a `weak_ptr<const Context>`, and its `buildImpl` passed `getContext()` to `createFunctionBaseCast`. That is safe only during analysis, while a caller still holds a strong `ContextPtr`. #109946 made `FunctionCastOrDefault` store that resolver as a member and call `build()` at execute time. The `ActionsDAG` keeps the resolver alive but nothing keeps its context alive, and both affected paths build the DAG from a function-local `Context::createCopy` that dies on return (`inplaceBlockConversions.cpp:230` for materialized-column defaults, `MutationsInterpreter.cpp:1762` for mutations). Evaluating such an expression later throws `Context has expired`: an exception in release builds, a server abort under debug and sanitizers. This captures the conversion settings in the resolver's constructor, while the context is provably alive, and has `buildImpl` consume that snapshot. `FunctionCast` used its `ContextPtr` for nothing but `settings(context, ...)`, so the snapshot moves one step earlier in the same call chain rather than being introduced. The resolver now holds no context at all, so the `WithContext` exception for this file in `various_checks.sh` is removed. The two build paths keep their distinct `DateTimeOverflowBehavior`: `Saturate` for `createInternalCast`, `Ignore` for `buildImpl`. Sharing one snapshot between them would silently change date-time conversion. Since a snapshot replaces a live context, every context-derived conversion setting was compared before and after and is byte-identical, including all three `date_time_overflow_behavior` modes, `cast_keep_nullable`, `precise_float_parsing`, the IPv4/IPv6 error settings and timezone substitution. `04510_accurateCastOrDefault_settings` from #109946 passes unchanged. The new test aborts a master server at `CastOverloadResolver.cpp:195` and passes with this change, 50/50 green under randomized settings. signals.title: Keep a text index direct read from widening a filter step's output header
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113320 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114460 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Cannot find input column ... on its position in inputs of expression actions DAG`) when a query has a `JOIN` above a table whose text-indexed column is used by both a `PREWHERE` and a `WHERE` text-search predicate. ### Description #114460, the fix for #113320, introduced the column retention this change works alongside. It is unreleased, so no released version is affected. On default settings, a `JOIN` over a table with a text index fails when the same indexed column is read by both a `PREWHERE` and a text-searchable `WHERE` predicate: ```sql SELECT DISTINCT t.value FROM tab AS t FINAL GLOBAL NATURAL INNER JOIN (SELECT name FROM system.columns) AS r PREWHERE hasTokenCaseInsensitive(t.key, 'foo') WHERE hasAllTokens(t.key, 'foo'); -- Logical error: 'Cannot find input column key on its position in inputs of -- expression actions DAG, expected inputs [__table1.value, key], [__table2.name]' ``` Found by the AST fuzzer ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111867&sha=775787f0654602c107b33178c068b3ef74665b35&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_msan%29), STID 2409-5283); that PR does not touch the planner. Root cause: the rewrite drops the indexed column from a filter DAG's inputs, but the column stays in the reading step's output header under its raw storage name because it is deliberately kept in the read set for another reader - the `PREWHERE`, or a row policy. `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` appends such an unmatched header column to its result. The rewrite runs in the second optimization pass, after all header reconciliation, so the widened header reaches the join, whose DAG inputs lack it. The join only detects it. The retention step already computes which columns it keeps for another reader, and now makes each an input of the filter DAG at that same point, so nothing is appended to the output header. Both the `WHERE` and the `PREWHERE` rewrite go through that one step, and the column still reaches the reader that needs it. Reverting only the added loop reddens the new test with the original message at the original site. Also covered, as nine direct-read off/on pairs returning identical values: with and without `FINAL`, `NATURAL`/`ON` and `GLOBAL`/non-`GLOBAL` joins, both predicates in `WHERE`, no join, a row policy as the retaining reader, and a `Merge` parent that visits the reading step twice. #113320's test stays green.

signals.title: Read and checksum the UNIQUE KEY dense-index SST through IDataPartStorage
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow the UNIQUE KEY to work on encrypted and remote disks by reading and writing its dense-index SST through the part storage abstraction; the SST is now recorded in `checksums.txt`. ### Description The per-part UNIQUE KEY dense index (`unique_key_index.sst`) was opened and written by local filesystem path, which only worked on local disks and left the sidecar outside the part's checksum accounting. This PR drives the SST through `IDataPartStorage` using a custom RocksDB `Env`(a read-only `FileSystem` over `IDataPartStorage::readFile` for the reader, a `WriteBuffer`-backed one for the writer), so encrypted and remote disks work as well. The SST is now recorded in `checksums.txt`, so it is transferred by backup/fetch like any other part file and validated by `checkConsistencyBase`: a missing or wrongly-sized SST fails the standard consistency check and the part is detached as broken, while size-preserving corruption is caught at load time by `ensureValidDenseIndex` (RocksDB block-checksum + entry-count validation), which removes and rebuilds the index. On readonly storage a corrupt or absent SST fails the load closed instead of activating an unprobeable part. The previous restriction that UNIQUE KEY tables must reside on local-only storage policies is removed.

signals.title: Speed up window functions by evaluating each `MergeTree` partition independently
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108326 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114645 A window function plan sorts its input partitioned by the window `PARTITION BY` columns: every row is reshuffled across streams by `ScatterByPartitionTransform` (a hash pass over the `PARTITION BY` columns plus a repack of every column of every row through a full cross-stream `Resize`), so that whole window partitions land in single streams before the per-stream sort and `WindowTransform`. If the partition expression of the `MergeTree` table is a deterministic function of the window `PARTITION BY` columns, the reading will now emit each partition through a single port instead: every stream already carries whole window partitions, so the scatter is skipped entirely and the read, sort, and window all stay within per-partition streams. ```sql CREATE TABLE test_16 (a UInt64, b UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() PARTITION BY sipHash64(a) % 16; INSERT INTO test_16 SELECT number % 100000, number FROM numbers_mt(30000000); OPTIMIZE TABLE test_16 FINAL; EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT a, sum(b) OVER (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY b) FROM test_16 SETTINGS allow_window_partitions_independently = 1, max_threads = 16; ``` ```response (Expression) ExpressionTransform × 16 (Window) Resize 16 → 16 WindowTransform × 16 (Sorting) MergeSortingTransform × 16 LimitsCheckingTransform × 16 PartialSortingTransform × 16 <- was: fed through Resize 16 → 1 + ScatterByPartitionTransform 1 → 16, reshuffling every row across streams (Expression) ExpressionTransform × 16 (ReadFromMergeTree) MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPoolInOrder, algorithm: InOrder) × 16 0 → 1 <- per-partition reading (16 partitions → 16 streams) ``` On `test_str_64 (a UInt64, b UInt64, s String)` with 30M rows, 100k window partitions over 64 balanced table partitions (`PARTITION BY sipHash64(a) % 64`), and a 100-byte random string in `s`, at `max_threads = 16`: | query | off | on | speedup | |--------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|--------|---------| | `SELECT a, s, count(b) OVER (PARTITION BY a) FROM test_str_64` | 1.014s | 0.554s | 1.83× | | `SELECT a, s, sum(b) OVER (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY b) FROM test_str_64` | 1.492s | 0.956s | 1.56× | The scatter repacks every column of every row, so the win grows with the row width. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up window functions on partitioned `MergeTree` tables by reading each partition through its own stream and evaluating the windows per partition, skipping the hash scatter that ordinarily reshuffles every row across threads before the window sort. This applies when the table partition expression is a deterministic function of the window `PARTITION BY` columns and is gated by the same cost heuristic as per-partition `GROUP BY` / `DISTINCT` (enough partitions relative to `max_threads`, no dominant partition). Controlled by the new settings `allow_window_partitions_independently` (enabled by default), `force_window_partitions_independently`, and `max_number_of_partitions_for_independent_window`.
