signal.title: Fix data race on DataTypeAggregateFunction version during Native serialization
signal.text: Related: found by the `arm_tsan` and `azure, amd_tsan` Stress tests (STID 3977-4818, ThreadSanitizer data race). No existing issue. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/94859 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112052 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not for changelog. ### Description A single `DataTypeAggregateFunction` instance is shared across query result blocks: it lives once in the table's column description and is aliased by shallow column copies. `NativeWriter`/`NativeReader` called `setVersionToAggregateFunctions`, which walked to the leaf type and wrote its `mutable version` field in place. Two concurrent `Native` serializations of the same aggregate-function-typed column then raced on that field, and the version written for one old connection stayed on the shared type, so every later query read the states at that version - for `sumMap` over `Decimal32` that returns wrong values. Reports: * https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109496&sha=62eeb400eafe86cedff9b5a4e9a36aa722633cda&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29 * https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b59441bd06c2fcb6b103a30874528cc398afc723&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28azure%2C%20amd_tsan%29 **That fix has since landed on `master`** through #94859 and #112052: `setVersionToAggregateFunctions` now replaces every versioned nested type instead of mutating it, and `replaceNestedSimpleTypes` carries the custom names (`Nested`, `SimpleAggregateFunction`) over the rebuild. This branch is therefore resolved in favour of that implementation, and what it added on top of it - an `IDataType::transformChildren` override per container type, and the `unique_ptr` to `shared_ptr` switch of `DataTypeCustomNamePtr` - is dropped as duplicate machinery. What remains here is what `master` does not have, and it keeps this PR's intent - the race cannot come back, because the version can no longer be assigned in place at all: * `DataTypeAggregateFunction::setVersion` and `updateVersionFromRevision` are removed, and `version` is no longer `mutable`. Both mutators were left without callers by the rewrite on `master`; the version is now set only at construction (parsed from AST, decoded from the binary type encoding, or chosen by `setVersionToAggregateFunctions`, which builds a new type). * Unit and functional coverage of the behaviour, which `master` has only indirectly. ### Testing * `gtest_aggregate_function_version_race` (13 tests) pins the type-level behaviour: the shared type object is not mutated; a wrapper is rebuilt only when a leaf was actually replaced; the `Point`, `Nested` and `SimpleAggregateFunction` custom names survive; a `Variant` keeps its discriminator order and throws when two alternatives would collapse; a `JSON` typed path keeps the version spelled in its own type name; and an 8-thread x 2000-iteration stress over one shared type object is race-free. * `04612_aggregate_function_version_custom_type_names` round-trips `Nested`, `SimpleAggregateFunction` and a wrapper-named type through `Native` (which assigns the version in the writer and again in the reader) and through `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, and checks that a deeply nested `Nested` stays linear in the nesting depth. * `04613_aggregate_function_version_not_sticky` asks for a `Native` response at a revision below the one that introduced versioning and then checks the column again, so a version pinned for that one response would be visible both in the values read back (`sumMap` over `Decimal32`) and in `system.columns`. The revision is pinned explicitly and the type name the response carries is asserted, so the test cannot pass without that path having run.

signal.title: Support the Vortex file format
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87327 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/rust_vendor/pull/74 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added support for reading and writing the [Vortex](https://github.com/vortex-data/vortex) columnar file format (the `Vortex` input and output format). This closes [#87327](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87327). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes The implementation uses the Rust `vortex` crate (v0.83.0) through a new C FFI crate `rust/workspace/vortex` (`_ch_rust_vortex`), following the same pattern as `prql` and `polyglot`. Data crosses the FFI boundary through the Arrow C Data Interface and is converted with the same `ArrowColumnToCHColumn`/`CHColumnToArrowColumn` code as the `Arrow` format. IO is delegated back to ClickHouse through callbacks: reads go through ClickHouse's own read buffers (range reads for seekable inputs, whole-file buffering otherwise), and the produced file is streamed into the output buffer. All work is driven by a single-threaded runtime on the calling thread — the library spawns no threads, and Rust panics are caught at the FFI boundary and turned into exceptions. Features: - Reading with projection pushdown: only the columns used by the query are read from the file. - Schema inference and `count()`-only queries answered from file metadata without reading data. - Writing with the library's default adaptive compression (BtrBlocks-style cascading encodings + zstd), including a valid empty file for empty results. - Graceful errors on malformed and truncated files (fuzzer-friendly: no aborts, Rust panics become exceptions). Limitations (documented in `docs/reference/formats/Vortex.mdx`): - `Map`, `Int128`/`UInt128`/`Int256`/`UInt256`, `IPv6`, and `Interval` columns cannot be written (no corresponding Vortex type). - `String` and `FixedString` are written as Vortex `Binary` (ClickHouse strings are arbitrary bytes, while Vortex requires `Utf8` to be valid UTF-8). - The format is disabled in MSan builds: the MSan-instrumented library (with origin tracking) is so large that linking `unit_tests_dbms` overflows the 2 GiB `R_X86_64_PC32` relocation range (same approach as `wasmtime` and `delta-kernel-rs`). - Reading and writing are single-threaded in this first version: the whole scan (I/O, decompression, and decoding) runs on one thread, so on ClickBench reads are significantly slower than `Parquet`, which ClickHouse decodes with multiple threads (see the [benchmark results](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112950#issuecomment-5274283519) and [the explanation](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112950#issuecomment-5274483899)). Filter pushdown (added in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114373, `input_format_vortex_filter_push_down`, on by default) reduces the amount of data decoded by selective queries, but does not parallelize the scan. Writes are also slower than `Parquet` (the adaptive compressor samples many encodings per column) — parallelism can be added later. The 127 new vendored Rust crates are added in https://github.com/ClickHouse/rust_vendor/pull/74 (the `contrib/rust_vendor` submodule is bumped to that branch).

signal.title: Fix TSan data race on `std::cerr` in `gtest_filecache.cpp`
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Unit tests (tsan)` fails with a data race on the format state of the global `std::cerr` object. TSan runs with `halt_on_error=1`, so the report aborts the binary: 2172 of 19839 tests had run, and the rest lost coverage for that run. ``` SUMMARY: ThreadSanitizer: data race contrib/llvm-project/libcxx/include/ios:497 in std::__1::ios_base::width() const Location is global 'std::__1::cerr' of size 264 ``` Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114666&sha=000cc7f7a20b3f741b10fa78b6b643a6e0a16683&name_0=PR&name_1=Unit%20tests%20%28tsan%29 The character sink is locked; the `ios_base` members are not: libc++ reads `width()` and writes `width(0)` on every `operator<<`, and both stacks end there. Root cause: `src/Interpreters/tests/gtest_filecache.cpp` wrote the same stream under two different synchronisation disciplines. `FileCacheTest::SetUp` points the Poco root logger at a `ConsoleChannel(std::cerr)`, which serialises its writers under a static mutex (TSan's `M0`), so any thread that logs writes `cerr` while holding it. The file additionally performed 36 raw `std::cerr <<` writes, which take no lock. The second writer here is `ExternalLoader::PeriodicUpdater::doPeriodicUpdates` logging its startup line: the updater runs because the shared unit-test context leaves `application_type` at `SERVER`. This removes the unsynchronised writer. The 14 bare `"Step N"` markers are deleted (a failing `ASSERT_*` already reports file and line); the remaining diagnostics go through the logger, so every write takes the same lock, including the file's two worker threads. The logger is obtained on first use: a logger keeps whatever channel the root had when created, so one created before `SetUp` would silently drop every message. The redirection itself is untouched, so `FileCacheTest.LoadMetadataParallelism`, which asserts on captured stderr, still passes. Validated with a TSan build (clang-22, as pinned for the CI job). A harness forcing repeated `ExternalLoader` startup writes concurrently with the test reproduces the signature above before the change and produces none after it. Diagnostic output and all 37 `FileCacheTest.*` results match in both arms. 17 other gtest files write `std::cerr` raw (excluding commented-out code), which the style check permits under `/tests/`; this was the only one also installing a channel on it.

signal.title: Refuse to read Apache Paimon primary-key tables instead of returning superseded rows
signal.text: Refuse to read Apache Paimon primary-key tables instead of returning superseded rows <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113360 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113360 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reading an Apache Paimon primary-key table now throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` instead of silently returning wrong results. Merge-on-read is not implemented, so the reader returned the raw union of the snapshot's data files, including row versions superseded by later upserts. Set `paimon_allow_unmerged_primary_key_reads = 1` (or `compatibility = '26.7'`) to keep reading the files unmerged and accept the incorrect results. Closes [#113360](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113360). ### Description Reading a Paimon primary-key (LSM) table returned stale rows silently: after `INSERT (1,'old'),(2,'two')` then `INSERT (1,'new')`, Spark returns `1 new / 2 two` while `paimonLocal(...)` gave `1 new / 1 old / 2 two`. **Root cause.** All three read modes of `PaimonMetadata::iterate` funnel into `collectDataFilesFromManifests`, whose only data-removing filters are a `seen_files` set keyed on the file *path* and dropping whole `Kind::DELETE` files: no row ordering, no primary-key or sequence-number comparison. An upsert's new file and the old version's are both `ADD` entries, so every row of both is emitted. **The change.** `iterate` now throws when the schema declares primary keys, unless the new session setting `paimon_allow_unmerged_primary_key_reads` (default `false`) is on. It sits above all three mode branches, so one check covers them. Merge-on-read needs per-row key/value/row-kind decoding and merge-engine semantics absent from the tree. The hatch is there because `paimon*()` table functions are ungated, unlike the `Paimon*` engines, so an unconditional refusal would break queries working today; the docs now state the limitation. The guard keys on the primary key, not on table options: a single-commit or compacted table does read correctly today and now throws, but `full-compaction.delta-commits = 1` alone compacts nothing and `deletion-vectors.enabled` alone returned 0 of 2 rows, so neither option identifies the safe case. The check is per query, not the constructor, where a throw breaks `Merge` over a catalog database. **Validation.** New stateless test `04749_paimon_primary_key_unmerged` with a committed two-snapshot fixture (README has the recipe): the default `SELECT` and `count()` throw, the opt-in and `compatibility = '26.7'` both return the raw union, `DESCRIBE` works, an append-only table still reads, 50/50 randomized runs pass. Six mutants: five each redden a different arm, the sixth pins the error code. The hatch restores the previous output byte-for-byte on all 13 shapes I measured.

signal.title: Sync BACKUP FROM SNAPSHOT settings and failpoints
signal.text: `BACKUP FROM SNAPSHOT` is already parsed in this repository (`ParserBackupQuery`, `ASTBackupQuery`), but the settings and failpoints of its **resumable** mode existed only in the Cloud repository. As a result the two settings surfaces and failpoint registries had drifted apart, and the shared files conflicted on every sync. This declares them here, and says plainly in each place that the feature behind them is available in ClickHouse Cloud only: - `resumable_backup_from_snapshot` — experimental session setting. - `resumable_backup_batch_size` and `resumable_backup_batch_size_bytes` — backup-query settings bounding how much work a failed attempt replays. - the `backup_from_snapshot_*` failpoints the feature's tests inject. Nothing in this repository reads the batch limits or injects the failpoints. The declarations exist so that both builds accept and reject the same queries, and so these shared files stop conflicting on every sync. `fromBackupQuery` still rejects a zero batch limit, keeping that validation identical in both builds. signal.title: Push tuple element predicates into Parquet and ORC subcolumn reads
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112575 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Filter pushdown now works for `Tuple` subcolumns in Parquet and ORC files. A predicate such as `WHERE tup.1 = 555555` over `file()`, `s3()` or `url()` now prunes row groups and row index strides using the tuple element's own statistics instead of reading the whole file. ### Description Closes: #112575 Three independent defects, all needed for the reported query to prune. Parquet's reader itself was fine. **The analyzer never produced a subcolumn.** `StorageFile`/`StorageURL`/`StorageObjectStorage` return `false` from `supportsOptimizationToSubcolumns`, so `tupleElement(tup, 1)` was never rewritten to `tup.1`; the pass also accepted only `TableNode`, skipping table functions. That blanket `false` keeps #106147 fixed (`NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` on `.null` in PREWHERE), so rather than flipping it this adds a narrow `supportsOptimizationToTupleElementSubcolumns` virtual defaulting to the existing one, with a `{Tuple, tupleElement}`-only allow-list. `04303_object_storage_prewhere_isnotnull_subcolumn` passes unmodified. Source identity also moves to the table-expression node: every `file()` resolves to the same `_table_function.file` ID, so two such sources shared a key. Accepting table functions generally also makes `format()`, `values()` and `view()` eligible for the other transformers; those storages already answer `supportsSubcolumns()`, so the default covers them. **ORC's search argument builder resolved top-level names only,** so any dotted name emitted `YES_NO_NULL` while the read path in the same file resolved them recursively. Resolving recursively also reaches the flattened-`Nested` descent, which rewrites the type it is given, so the builder keeps the key's own type: an array-typed predicate over a flattened `Nested` leaf is not pushed, since scalar element statistics cannot decide it. **ORC built its KeyCondition from the reader header,** which carries only the parent column, so the predicate degraded to `unknown`. ORC now passes `initKeyConditionOnce` a local copy extended with the tuple element paths the filter references; `FormatFilterInfo`, the Parquet call site and the reader header are untouched. Admission requires a named tuple at every level (unwrapping `Nullable`/`LowCardinality`/`Array`), which refuses Map `.keys`/`.values`: they use `SubstreamType::TupleElement` but have no per-element statistics. <details> <summary>Measurements (100k rows, one row group / stride per 10k)</summary> | Arm | master | this PR | |---|---|---| | ORC `WHERE tup.1 = 55555` | 200000 rows read | **20000** | | ORC `WHERE id = 55555` (control) | 20000 | 20000 | | Parquet `WHERE tup.1 = 55555` | 7 row groups / 0 pruned | **1 / 6** | | Parquet `WHERE id = 55555` (control) | 1 / 6 | 1 / 6 | Results identical in every arm. Refusal arms (Map `.keys`/`.values`, `.null`, `.size0`, unnamed tuple, `Array(Tuple)`, type-mismatch structure hint) return correct results with pruning off. Multi-level `tup.2.1` stays unpruned: correct, and a separate optimization. Regression sweep over `*functions_to_subcolumns*`, `*tuple_element*`, `*_parquet_*`, `*_orc_*` and the named pushdown tests, run on this build and on an unmodified master build for attribution: no regression attributable to this change. New tests are 50/50 green under randomized settings. </details> Also noticed, not touched here: reading a standalone dotted ORC tuple element with its inferred type returns column defaults, because `Nested::flatten` does not descend a `Nullable(Tuple)`. #109741 (open) rewrites that helper for the `Arrow` spelling.

signal.title: Propagate OpenTelemetry trace context into AsyncTaskExecutor fibers
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112738 The OpenTelemetry trace context is stored in a `FiberLocal`, but the fibers created by `AsyncTaskExecutor` (`ConnectionEstablisherAsync`, `PacketReceiver`, `RemoteQueryExecutorReadContext`) started with an empty fiber-local context. Remote queries of a distributed query were parented directly to the trace context supplied by the client, bypassing the spans of the initiator, and no spans were produced for the async tasks themselves. ## Changes - `AsyncTaskExecutor` captures `OpenTelemetry::CurrentContext()` on the thread that constructs it and installs a `TracingContextHolder` inside the fiber routine. This seeds the fiber-local context from the creating query and opens one span per task execution, named after the executor (`ConnectionEstablisherAsync`, `PacketReceiver`, `RemoteQueryExecutorReadContext`). It is a no-op when tracing is not enabled. - `Fiber` destruction fixes - `Fiber::local_data` is now keyed by `typeid(T).name()` instead of the address of the `FiberLocal` object, so the same fiber-local variable resolves to the same data from every shared object. ## Span hierarchy change Remote queries now descend from the initiator through the `Connection::sendQuery` CLIENT span instead of appearing as direct children of the client-supplied trace context: ``` client span └─ query (initiator) └─ Connection::sendQuery [CLIENT] └─ query (remote server) ``` The expectations of `01455_opentelemetry_distributed` are updated accordingly: only the initial query span is now a direct child of the input trace context. This is the first part of the distributed tracing improvements discussed in the linked issue; instrumentation of the distributed query plan is left for follow-up pull requests. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Propagate the OpenTelemetry trace context into the fibers used for asynchronous connection establishment and remote query execution (hedged requests, `async_socket_for_remote`, `async_query_sending_for_remote`). Spans of remote queries in a distributed query are now correctly parented under the initiator's `Connection::sendQuery` span instead of being attached directly to the client-supplied trace context, and each asynchronous task execution produces its own span.

signal.title: Add higher-order array functions to pack bits.
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/48830 Adds higher-order array functions that apply a lambda to each element of an array and pack the resulting bits into a compact representation. Useful for compression and quantization in vector-search workloads, where a single bit (or a small group of bits) is derived per dimension and packed into a fixed-width value. Six functions are added: - `arrayPackBitsToUInt64(f, arr)` — pack one bit per element into a `UInt64` (only the first 64 bits are used). - `arrayPackBitsToString(f, arr)` — pack one bit per element into a `String` of `ceil(size / 8)` bytes. - `arrayPackBitsToFixedString(f, n, arr)` — pack one bit per element into a `FixedString(n)`. - `arrayPackBitGroupsToUInt64(f, g, arr)` — the same, but the lambda returns an integer whose low `g` bits form a group, and the groups are packed contiguously (`N·g` bits). - `arrayPackBitGroupsToString(f, g, arr)` - `arrayPackBitGroupsToFixedString(f, n, g, arr)` Bits are packed most-significant-bit first within each byte and groups are packed contiguously, one after another (a group does not occupy a whole byte). The `*ToUInt64` variants interpret the packed byte stream in little-endian byte order, as requested in the issue, so `arrayPackBitsToUInt64(f, arr) = reinterpretAsUInt64(arrayPackBitsToString(f, arr))` and likewise for the group variants. The implementation is a single `ArrayPackBitsImpl` template parameterized by the result column type and a `PackGroups` flag. `FunctionArrayMapped` is extended with a `return_fixed_string` trait so that an implementation returning a `FixedString` can forward the constant size argument to `getReturnType`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added higher-order array functions to pack bits: `arrayPackBitsToUInt64`, `arrayPackBitsToString`, `arrayPackBitsToFixedString`, `arrayPackBitGroupsToUInt64`, `arrayPackBitGroupsToString`, `arrayPackBitGroupsToFixedString`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) The functions carry embedded `FunctionDocumentation` (description, syntax, arguments, returned value, examples), from which the user-facing documentation is generated.

signal.title: Add ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY ENGINE to change a MergeTree-family table's engine
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107551 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY ENGINE = ...MergeTree(...)` to change the engine of a MergeTree-family table in place (for example `MergeTree` into `ReplacingMergeTree` or `SummingMergeTree`). Gated behind the experimental setting `allow_experimental_alter_modify_engine`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107551 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107481 Requested by @ alexey-milovidov. `ALTER TABLE t MODIFY ENGINE = <engine>` changes a MergeTree-family table's engine in place. Only the merge semantics (`MergingParams`) change: columns, keys and settings are kept, and data is not rewritten. Existing parts re-merge under the new semantics via background merges and `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL`, as with the part-level reset in #107481. A new `MODIFY_ENGINE` alter command rewrites the engine clause in the CREATE query (`StorageInMemoryMetadata::new_engine` -> `applyMetadataChangesToCreateQuery`); `MergingParams::parseFromEngineAST` builds and validates the new merge params against the columns and final settings, so a rejection never leaves an unloadable CREATE on disk. Supported targets: `Replacing`, `Summing`, `Aggregating`, `Collapsing`, `VersionedCollapsing`, `Coalescing`, `Graphite`. A required column may be added in the same statement, before `MODIFY ENGINE`. Non-replicated tables only; old-syntax tables are rejected, their keys being positional engine arguments. Because data is not rewritten, a transition is refused when existing parts could not satisfy the target's invariants: a nullable or unreadable `Graphite` path/time column (the rollup reads them with `getDataAt`/`getUInt`), and `VersionedCollapsing` with the version column outside the sorting key, whose reload widens the key under existing parts. **Two questions for review:** 1. Reload-only, rather than a live swap: `merging_params` is read lock-free from hot paths and often bound by const reference for a whole query, and an exclusive lock cannot be taken there (the query holds `drop_lock` in read mode). An immediate swap needs either a `MultiVersion` `merging_params` or recreating the storage. Which do you prefer? 2. The coordinated `Replicated*MergeTree` switch (decision 3 on the issue) is not implemented. `ReplicatedMergeTreeTableMetadata` already persists the merge mode, so that is the natural next step. Tests: `04340_alter_modify_engine` (the gate, each transition's merge semantics under `FINAL`, the validation errors, the AST JSON round trip), `04341_alter_modify_engine_access` and `04342_alter_modify_engine_replicated`. Docs: `docs/reference/statements/alter/engine.mdx`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Implemented SIEVE eviction in cache framework
signal.text: Implements the `SIEVE` cache eviction policy in the cache framework (`CacheBase`), available alongside the existing `LRU` and `SLRU` policies. `SIEVE` is a simple, scan-resistant eviction algorithm: a single "hand" walks a FIFO queue of entries and evicts the first entry whose `visited` flag is clear, clearing the flag as it passes set entries. See the paper for details: https://junchengyang.com/publication/nsdi24-SIEVE.pdf This continues the original work by @Vectorshine, brought up to date with `master`: - Reworked `SIEVECachePolicy` to match the current `ICachePolicy` interface (`CurrentMetrics` tracking, `maxCount`, `contains`, per-entry `OnRemoveEntryFunction`), mirroring `LRUCachePolicy`. - Fixed a bug in `remove` where the stored queue iterator was advanced in place and the wrong node was erased. - Added unit tests in `gtest_sieve_cache.cpp`, including a step-by-step test of the eviction logic. - Randomized the mark and uncompressed cache policy across `LRU`, `SLRU` and `SIEVE` in stateless functional tests (`ci/jobs/functional_tests.py`) and the stress test (`tests/docker_scripts/stress_runner.sh`). `SIEVE` is only implemented for the `CacheBase`-backed caches, so the filesystem cache (backed by `FileCachePolicy`) is not randomized to it, and it is excluded during bugfix validation, which runs downloaded master-side binaries. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/58910 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a new cache eviction policy `SIEVE`. It can be selected for the in-memory caches backed by `CacheBase`, such as the mark cache and the uncompressed cache, via the corresponding `*_cache_policy` server settings (for example, `mark_cache_policy` and `uncompressed_cache_policy`). It is not available for the filesystem cache. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signal.title: Fix ANY INNER JOIN with OR conditions depending on which table is built
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114354 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114676 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111645 `ANY INNER JOIN` returns one row per key, from both the left and the right table. With several `OR`-ed conditions in `ON`, the key of a condition was claimed through the used flag of the right row that the key is stored for — and one right row can be the stored row of a different key in each condition, so claiming it for one key silently retired the others. The result therefore depended on which side the hash table was built from. On the dataset from the issue, `t1 ANY JOIN t2` returned 3 rows and `t2 ANY JOIN t1` returned 6, and the same query returned 3 or 6 depending on `query_plan_join_swap_table`, which is a plan setting and must not change the result. `JoinUsedFlags` now keeps one flag array per condition, indexed by the cell of that condition's map, exactly as `per_offset_flags` does for a single condition, so the claim names the key of a condition rather than a right row. A left row visits every condition instead of stopping at the first match, so it may be joined once per condition whose key it claims — hence `ANY INNER JOIN` results are replicated now. The residual-condition path (`joinRightColumnsWithAdditionalFilter`) claims the same way, after applying the filter to the candidates of a key. The outcome is the union of the single-condition joins: a pair of rows matching through several conditions is joined once per condition, and the number of result rows no longer depends on the probe order, on the order the tables are written in, or on the plan. Deduplicating those pairs instead was measured to leave the row count dependent on which left row claims a key first, and so on the probe order — 39 runs out of 40 disagreed with the 40th at `max_threads = 8`. That semantics change moves two existing references, both for pairs that match through more than one condition: - `01660_join_or_inner`: `2 3 2 3` is returned twice, matching both `a2 = a3` and `b2 = b3`; - `03006_join_on_inequal_expression_fast_2`: `(1, 1, 1) INNER ANY JOIN (1, 1, 1) ON t1.a = t2.a AND (t1.b > 0 OR t2.b > 0)` returns its row twice, and in `ON t1.key = t2.key AND t1.a < t2.a OR t1.a = t2.a` one left row is now dropped because another left row with the same key claimed it, as single-condition `ANY INNER JOIN` already does. `SEMI`, `ANTI` and the `LEFT`/`RIGHT` forms of `ANY` are unaffected: their unit is the right row, which a per-row flag expresses exactly, and every branch added here is gated on `INNER` + `ANY`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ANY INNER JOIN` with several `OR`-ed conditions in the `ON` section returning a different number of rows depending on which table the hash table is built from, that is on the order the tables are written in and on the `query_plan_join_swap_table` setting. Such a join now returns one row per key of every condition, from both tables.
signal.author: vdimir

signal.title: Support DEFINER / SQL SECURITY for dictionaries
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85293 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Support `DEFINER` and `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` for dictionaries, like for views. A dictionary with a local `CLICKHOUSE` source can name the user whose privileges its load runs with, instead of storing a user and password in `SOURCE(...)`. Rotating that user's password no longer breaks the dictionary. ### Description A dictionary with a `CLICKHOUSE` source authenticates every load with the credentials in `SOURCE(...)`, so rotating that password breaks all later reloads. A deployment issuing short-lived credentials must embed a long-lived one, or load as `default` with excess authority. Name the identity instead: `DEFINER = dict_owner`, with no `USER`/`PASSWORD` in `SOURCE(...)`. The load then runs with that user's privileges, consults no credential, and is bounded by the definer's settings constraints. It reuses the view definer machinery, inheriting the `SET DEFINER` grant check and the guard against dropping a live definer. `04869_dictionary_definer.sh` covers rotation against a stored-credential control, privilege and settings bounding, `SET DEFINER`, the metadata round trip, every rejection, and locality both ways, each arm mutation-verified. Scoped to a **local** `CLICKHOUSE` source, as @ pufit confirmed on the issue: any other authenticates against a foreign system with credentials a locally resolved identity cannot replace, so the clause is rejected at `CREATE` time. Locality is decided on the effective configuration, resolving named collections and `PORT tcpPort()` first; an unprovable source is rejected too. `DEFINER` is the only accepted type and must name somebody: `INVOKER` because a dictionary loads from a background pool with no invoker, `NONE` because nothing consults the type at load time. A dictionary without the clause is unchanged; `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Dictionary(...) SQL SECURITY ...` keeps failing closed. Three limits come from the shared UUID-keyed definer registry, and each is master's behaviour for views today: an ephemeral `<user>:definer` clone can go uncollected when a `CREATE` is rejected late or the object leaves a UUID-bearing database; drop protection does not apply in `Memory` or `Ordinary` databases; and a `DROP USER` racing a `CREATE` can pass its dependency check before the object registers (over 60 attempts, 21 hits for views on master against 2 for dictionaries here).
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Reuse the previous row's result for equal consecutive rows in Set execution
signal.text: The per-row execution of `x IN <set>` (`Set::executeImplCase`) hashes the full key for every row — SipHash128 for hashed multi-column keys. When the key columns are clustered (e.g. they are a primary-key prefix, so the data arrives sorted), consecutive rows form long runs of equal values, and the previous row's result can be reused after a cheap raw-byte comparison instead of repeating the hash+probe. With this change, when all key columns are non-nullable fixed-width (tuples are flattened element-wise), each row's raw bytes are compared with the previous row's, and on equality the previous result is reused, skipping the hash+probe entirely. Motivation: in SQL transpiled from PromQL selectors over `TimeSeries` tables, the per-row `id IN (tags subquery)` filter computes SipHash128 of a 24-byte `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)` per row into a `HashSet<UInt128>`. On tsbench, a PromQL benchmark over the ClickHouse `TimeSeries` engine (30 days of scrape data at 15s step, scale 1 = 1.06 billion samples / 6112 series, Ryzen 9950X, query result cache disabled, best of 3), this filter took ~17.5% of CPU of a 30-day rate query scanning 69M rows. With this change the hashing disappears from the profile (~3% of cheap byte comparisons remain), and raw-selector benchmark queries improved 1.4–2.3x. The optimization is generic: any `IN` over clustered/sorted key columns benefits; for unclustered data the added cost is a few loads per row. Bitwise comparison is applied only to POD column layouts (fixed-width raw bytes in one contiguous buffer, tuples flattened element-wise), where bitwise equality implies key equality; strings, arrays, `Nullable` and other non-POD layouts keep the existing path. The new performance test `tests/performance/set_in_clustered_keys.xml` covers both the clustered case (runs of equal consecutive keys) and the unclustered regression control (consecutive rows always differ). Note: tsbench scale-64 validation is in progress; numbers will be added before merge. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up execution of `IN` over clustered (e.g. sorted by primary key) columns by reusing the previous row's result for equal consecutive rows.
signal.author: nikitamikhaylov

signal.title: group_by_each_block_no_merge setting
signal.text: ### Changelog category: - New Feature ### Changelog entry: Added the `group_by_each_block_no_merge` setting (off by default). When enabled, a query with `GROUP BY` is processed in a streaming fashion: aggregation is performed, finalized, and flushed for every block of data, without fully merging the partial results. The exact output is plan-dependent and not deterministic in general. This is intended for special cases such as populating a materialized view with `POPULATE`, where the partial results are merged later in the background. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/9604 ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) The setting is documented in `src/Core/Settings.cpp` (rendered into the settings reference). > Information about CI checks: https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/development/continuous-integration/

signal.title: Remove `WINDOW VIEW`
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61069 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/88706 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The experimental `WINDOW VIEW` feature is removed, together with the `WATCH` statement and the `windowID` function. It has been non-functional since version 24.12 (inserts into the source table were silently not delivered to window views) and was never supported by the analyzer, which is enabled by default since 24.3. The settings `allow_experimental_window_view`, `window_view_clean_interval`, `window_view_heartbeat_interval`, and `wait_for_window_view_fire_signal_timeout` are kept as obsolete no-ops. The time-window functions `tumble`, `tumbleStart`, `tumbleEnd`, `hop`, `hopStart`, and `hopEnd` are kept. If you still have window views defined, drop them before upgrading: a server that finds a window view in its metadata fails to start (`Cannot parse definition from metadata file ... (SYNTAX_ERROR)`), the same way the removal of the `Lazy` database engine behaves. Similar functionality will be reimplemented on top of streaming queries (issue [#114738](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738)). The removal, in detail: - `src/Storages/WindowView/` (`StorageWindowView`, `WindowViewSource`, `StorageBlocks`), `WatermarkTransform`, the `ParserCreateWindowViewQuery` parser, and the whole `WATCH` statement stack (`ParserWatchQuery`, `ASTWatchQuery`, `InterpreterWatchQuery`, the `IStorage::watch` virtual) — window views were the last implementor of `watch`, and the `WATCH` statement was already documented as deprecated. - The `ASTCreateQuery` watermark/lateness fields and their AST JSON serialization and validation. The `clickhouse_json` boundary fails closed rather than silently reinterpreting legacy payloads: `ASTCreateQuery::readJSON` rejects a set `is_window_view`, watermark strategy or `allowed_lateness` flag and the `watermark_function` / `lateness_function` children (otherwise such a payload deserialized as an ordinary `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` and was executed as an immediate-population table create), while `ASTViewTargets::readJSON` rejects the `Inner` target kind, which nothing produces any more and which formatted back to parser-impossible `INNER ENGINE ...` SQL. Both are covered by `04892_ast_json_removed_window_view_state`; the `PushingToWindowViewSink` and `ViewType::WINDOW` branches in `InsertDependenciesBuilder`; window-view special cases in `InterpreterCreateQuery`, `InterpreterInsertQuery`, `StorageFactory`, `DatabaseOrdinary`, `DatabaseReplicated`, `DDLDependencyVisitor`, `QueryFuzzer`, BuzzHouse, and the ArrowFlight table-type mapping. - The `windowID` function and the `UInt32` single-argument forms of `tumbleStart`/`tumbleEnd`/`hopStart`/`hopEnd` (they only accepted `windowID` output). The rest of the time-window function family stays, since these are ordinary functions usable in a regular `GROUP BY` and are exactly the vocabulary for the streaming-queries replacement. - The keywords `WATCH`, `EVENTS`, `ALLOWED_LATENESS`, and `STRICTLY_ASCENDING` (the `WATERMARK` keyword stays: the streaming-queries `WATERMARK FOR` clause uses it), the error code `QUERY_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_WINDOW_VIEW`, and the corresponding fuzzer dictionary and ANTLR grammar entries. - Kept for compatibility: `QueryViewsLogElement::ViewType::WINDOW` (so existing `system.query_views_log` tables keep their schema) and `ViewTarget::Inner` (so old DDL log entries still parse), following the same pattern as the `LIVE VIEW` removal. - The `allow_experimental_window_view` constraint in `tests/docker_scripts/stress_tests.lib` is kept (only the constraint, not the profile value, which would mark an obsolete setting as changed and add a `system.warnings` entry): the upgrade check runs the previous release's suite under the previous release's binary, whose window-view tests are not dropped afterwards because `--upgrade-check` implies `--fake-drop`, and the leftover metadata would then stop the new server from starting. - Tests: the four remaining window-view tests are removed. The pure time-window-function coverage of `01049_window_view_window_functions` moved to a new `04891_time_window_functions` test, which also pins the new `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` behavior of `tumbleStart(UInt32)`. - Docs: the `Window View` section of `CREATE VIEW`, the `WATCH` page (with its navigation entries and locale twins) are removed and the old-slug redirects retargeted; the window-view entries are removed from the generated settings/functions reference pages (second commit, hence the `pr-autogenerated-docs` label): the `window-view.mdx` settings page, the four settings' entries in the pages/manifest/navigation/settings explorer, and the `windowID` section of `time-window-functions.mdx`. The unrelated drift accumulated on master since the last nightly regeneration is deliberately not included; the nightly docs-autogen job will pick it up. Why now: the feature has been non-functional since Dec 2024 — commit `ceae84c87a2` removed the explicit view-dependency registration and `DDLDependencyVisitor` never extracted the source table of a `CREATE WINDOW VIEW`, so inserts into the source table were silently not pushed to window views, and direct inserts failed with `std::out_of_range` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113493). Nobody noticed for ~1.5 years. It was never ported to the analyzer (with `enable_analyzer = 1`, the default, existing window views load permanently inert), its tests were removed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73822 because they were inherently flaky, and it kept costing triage time (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114097 is a recent server SIGSEGV through `getSourceTableSelectQuery`). The full assessment, including the plan for reimplementing this functionality on top of streaming queries (`SELECT ... FROM t STREAM`, `WATERMARK FOR`, emit-on-watermark windowed aggregation), is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114738. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signal.title: Fix data race and use-after-free on DataLakeConfiguration::current_metadata
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113265 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a data race and a use-after-free on the metadata of a DeltaLake or Iceberg table. Two concurrent queries that read `total_rows` or `total_bytes` from `system.tables` for the same table could have one query replace the table's metadata while the other was still reading it, which could crash the server. Closes #113265. ### Description Two concurrent `SELECT ... FROM system.tables` scans over the same DeltaLake or Iceberg table race on `DataLakeConfiguration::current_metadata`. The field was a plain `std::unique_ptr` with no synchronization, while the configuration is shared: `StorageObjectStorage::totalRows` and `totalBytes` both call the mutating `configuration->update()` and then read the metadata back. TSAN reported the pointer race, but the consequence is worse. The read path was `assertInitialized()` followed by a separate `current_metadata->totalRows(...)` statement, while `update()` destroys the old metadata, so a reader can pass the null check and then call through the freed pointer. A local TSAN repro shows both the race and a heap-use-after-free freed by `~DeltaLakeMetadataDeltaKernel` on that line, and it kills the server. `current_metadata` becomes a `std::shared_ptr` guarded by a mutex, and every reader takes a copy of the pointer under the lock and calls through that copy. Holding a strong reference for the whole call is what closes the use-after-free: guarding only the null check would narrow the window without removing it. Writers build the new metadata outside the lock and publish under it, and the displaced object is destroyed after the lock is released, because `~IcebergMetadata` waits for its background prefetch task. Seven of the eight touched source files are there only because `getExternalMetadata` had to stop returning a raw pointer, so its six consumers keep the metadata alive while they use it. `StorageSystemIcebergFiles` needs that: it parks the pointer across `generate()` calls. The metadata subclasses are unchanged, and all 12 template instantiations are covered because the fix is in the template body. `TSA_GUARDED_BY` under `-Weverything -Werror` makes any remaining unguarded access a build error. Validation: a TSAN repro of 4 concurrent unrestricted `system.tables` scans reports the race 29 times before the fix and 0 after, at identical query counts (48 scans each), and the server survives only with the fix.

signal.title: Lazy materialization for reading local Parquet files (`file` / `File`)
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110970 Follow-up to the lazy materialization for object storage (#110970), as discussed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110970#issuecomment-5247858385: implement it for plain local Parquet files read through `StorageFile` — the `file` table function and the `File` table engine. For `ORDER BY ... LIMIT n` queries, the columns that are not needed for sorting and filtering are read only for the `n` rows that survive the `LIMIT`. The format side (row-selective Parquet reads via `FormatFilterInfo::rows_to_read`) and the plan split (`JoinLazyColumnsStep`, `LazyMaterializingTransform`) from #110970 are reused as-is; this PR adds the `StorageFile` counterpart of the two branches: - The main pass appends a `__global_row_index` column (file index in a per-query `LazyFileRegistry` + physical row numbers from `ChunkInfoRowNumbers`) in `StorageFileSource::generate`. - The lazy branch (`LazilyReadFromFile` → `LazyReadFromFileSource` → `StorageFileLazyRowsSource`) reopens only the surviving files (at most `LIMIT n` of them) with a per-file set of rows to read and `parquet.preserve_order`. - The storage-agnostic column-split logic of `ReadFromObjectStorageStep::keepOnlyRequiredColumnsAndCreateLazyReadStep` (which columns can be deferred: `DEFAULT` expression dependencies, PREWHERE inputs, hive partition and virtual columns) is extracted into the shared `splitLazilyReadColumnsFromFormatInfo` and reused by both storages. **Generation safety.** POSIX has no conditional read, so the reread cannot be pinned the way `If-Match` pins it on S3. Instead the reread fails close with the new `FILE_CHANGED_DURING_READ` error when the file's generation token — sub-second mtime + inode + size, reusing `computeFileCacheVersionToken` from the query condition cache integration — no longer matches the one captured when the main pass opened the file. The token is validated at file registration time in the main pass, and both before and right after the reopen in the lazy pass. Replace-by-rename (the common atomic-update pattern) is always caught since it changes the inode; an in-place rewrite is caught up to the filesystem timestamp tick (and already tears a single-pass read today). **Gates** (`ReadFromFile::canUseLazyMaterialization`): Parquet format only, no file descriptor reads (stdin cannot be reopened), no archive entries, no `distributed_processing`, no `--rename_files_after_processing`, uncompressed files only. Controlled by the new setting `query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization_for_file` (enabled by default), on top of `query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization`. **Bug fix for #110970 shared via the helper:** deferring a requested subcolumn (e.g. of a `JSON` column) left the lazy branch's format header empty and the query failed with `Not found column or subcolumn ... in block`, because the format header contains the parent column of a requested subcolumn while the split filtered it by subcolumn names. The split now maps requested columns to their storage-level names — the parent of a deferred subcolumn moves to the lazy branch, and stays in the main branch as well when a sort key still needs another subcolumn of it. Covered for both storages by the new tests. On a 1 GB local Parquet file (2M rows × 105 columns equivalent shape: two 300-byte strings), `SELECT * ... ORDER BY k DESC LIMIT 5` runs 3× faster (0.15 s vs 0.45 s, page-cache warm), with results verified identical with the optimization on and off. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Lazy materialization for `ORDER BY ... LIMIT n` queries (#110970) now also applies to local Parquet files read with the `file` table function and the `File` table engine: the columns that are not needed for sorting and filtering are read only for the `n` rows that survive the `LIMIT`. The second read of a surviving file fails close with the new `FILE_CHANGED_DURING_READ` error if the file was modified between the two passes. Controlled by the new setting `query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization_for_file` (enabled by default). Also fixes lazy materialization for object storage failing with `Not found column or subcolumn ... in block` when a requested subcolumn (e.g. of a `JSON` column) is deferred.

signal.title: Add mutation completion time `finish_time` to `system.mutations`
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/89216 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105255 Adds a `finish_time` column to `system.mutations` reporting when a mutation was completed; `0` means the mutation is not finished yet or its completion time is unknown. This is a rework of #105255 that avoids any new persistent state: no mutation-file format changes and no new Keeper znodes, so there is no upgrade path, no cleanup changes, and no retry/idempotency concerns. For non-replicated `MergeTree` tables the value is tracked in memory (like `latest_fail_time`) and stamped only when the completion is observed by the event that caused it: the commit of the last mutated part, or the creation of a mutation that has no parts to process. Mutations whose completion moment was not observed (entries loaded at startup, parts removed by `DROP PARTITION`) report `0` instead of a fabricated timestamp. For `ReplicatedMergeTree` tables the value is per-replica and equals the modification time of the replica's `mutation_pointer` znode — the write that marks mutations done on the replica. After the replica state is reloaded (e.g. server restart), the completion time of the mutation the pointer points at is restored from the znode `mtime`; older completed mutations report `0`. A cluster-wide completion time can be obtained with `max(finish_time)` grouped by `mutation_id` across replicas. Note for the CH Inc sync: `SharedMergeTree` constructs `MergeTreeMutationStatus` positionally and will need a follow-up to populate `finish_time`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a `finish_time` column to `system.mutations` that records when a mutation was completed. Unfinished mutations and mutations whose completion time is unknown report zero. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: Add UUID2 data type with correct sorting
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110066 Introduces `UUID2`, a variant of the `UUID` data type with correct (lexicographic) sorting. ## Motivation For historical reasons, the `UUID` data type sorts by the *second half* of the value. This is unexpected and, in particular, hurts the performance of primary indexes built on `UUIDv7` columns, whose most significant bits are a timestamp: with sorting by the second half, primary-key analysis cannot prune granules by the timestamp. ## What this does `UUID2` stores the 128-bit value as a plain big-endian integer of the 16 canonical bytes, so that natural integer comparison of the underlying value matches the textual (lexicographic) order and the canonical byte order used by most other systems. It reuses the `UUID` column and `Field` representation (like `DateTime` reuses `UInt32`), so sorting is correct with no extra comparison code, and its binary/interchange serialization is the canonical big-endian byte order. - `UUID1` is an alias of the current `UUID` type. - A new setting `uuid_type_version` (default `1`) controls whether the bare name `UUID` resolves to `UUID` (`1`) or `UUID2` (`2`) at `CREATE`/`ALTER` time. The resolved concrete type is materialized into the stored table definition (including nested types such as `Array(UUID)`), so reads never depend on the session setting and existing tables are never rewritten. The default will be flipped to `2` in a later, separate change. - Conversions to/from `String`, `UInt128`, `FixedString(16)` and `UUID`, plus `toUUID2` / `toUUID2OrZero` / `toUUID2OrNull`. - Parity across functions (`hex`/`bin`, `reinterpretAs*`, `UUIDv7ToDateTime`, `UUIDToNum`, `empty`/`notEmpty`, `min`/`max`, hashing, `uniq`), formats (`RowBinary`, `Native`, `JSON`, `CSV`, `TSV`, `Arrow`, `Parquet`, `Avro`, `BSON`, `MsgPack`, `Protobuf`, `CapnProto`, `JSONExtract`) and storage (`generateRandom`, `bloom_filter` skip index). The `UUID` type is unchanged (verified: still sorts by second half, identical conversions, default `uuid_type_version = 1`). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a new data type `UUID2`, a variant of `UUID` that sorts by its textual (lexicographic) representation instead of by the second half of the value. The setting `uuid_type_version` (default `1`) selects whether the type name `UUID` resolves to `UUID` or `UUID2`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signal.title: Do not drop a named collection that a detached table still uses
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/96181 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/77366 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110529 A table detached with a plain `DETACH TABLE` keeps its metadata file, so the server attaches it again on the next start. It is gone from `DatabaseCatalog` though, so `isTableExist` returns false for it, and the `check_named_collection_dependencies` check (added in #96181) treated its dependency as a stale leftover of a failed `CREATE TABLE`: it removed the dependency and let `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` succeed. The `ATTACH` replayed at startup then threw `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST`, which aborts loading the metadata, and the server did not start at all. This is how the `Stress test (arm_tsan)` job fails on master with `Cannot start clickhouse-server`: the AST fuzzer makes `04320_url_engine_dispatch_partition_and_format` leave its `URL(named_collection)` table detached (the test's `ATTACH TABLE` never reaches the server), and the test then drops the named collection. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=8aad759007771032aa94d7f4eee3e18103dd63c3&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29 ``` Application: Caught exception while loading metadata: Code: 722. DB::Exception: Waited job failed: Code: 695. DB::Exception: Load job 'load table test_3.04320_..._n' failed: Code: 669. DB::Exception: There is no named collection `04320_..._nc`: Cannot attach table `test_3`.`04320_..._n` from metadata file store/e5b/.../04320_..._n.sql from query ATTACH TABLE ... ENGINE = URL(`04320_..._nc`, format = 'JSON'). (NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST) ``` The same signature accounts for 6 of the 8 `Cannot start clickhouse-server` failures with a missing named collection in the last 60 days (per `play.clickhouse.com`); the other two come from `03822_named_collection_drop_dependency_check`, which drops the collection with `check_named_collection_dependencies = 0` on purpose, and are the case #110529 handles by tolerating the missing collection at startup. ### Changes Per review feedback, the implementation is a simple in-memory bookkeeping in `NamedCollectionFactory` (an earlier revision inspected the metadata the detached table would be attached from, which required probing database disks and sweeping metadata directories after renames): - `DETACH TABLE` (and `DETACH DATABASE`, for every table inside) moves the dependencies of the table into a list of (collection, database, table) entries. - `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` is refused with `NAMED_COLLECTION_IS_USED` while an entry for the collection exists. - `ATTACH` does not remove the entry by itself: the dependencies are registered while the engine arguments are resolved, and the attach can still fail after that (an unknown format name, a failure creating the storage), leaving the table detached — the entry must keep protecting it. Instead, the entry is removed by the events that prove the metadata under that name is gone or harmless: `DROP TABLE`, `DETACH TABLE ... PERMANENTLY`, and `RENAME` of the (necessarily re-attached) table; `DROP DATABASE` removes the entries of the database's detached tables, and `RENAME DATABASE` re-keys them. The `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` check itself removes nothing: the table's existence in `DatabaseCatalog` is racy against in-flight attaches and detaches (the table can exist while nothing in the drop query has validated its live dependency), so the drop path is read-only and every recorded entry refuses the drop. - `DETACH TABLE ... PERMANENTLY` does not record an entry: a permanently detached table is not loaded at startup, so dropping a collection it references cannot break the server start. A later explicit `ATTACH` of such a table fails cleanly with `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST` and is recoverable by recreating the collection. - The list lives in memory only, which is consistent across a restart: a plainly detached table is attached again at the next start, where regular dependency tracking picks it up, and a permanently detached one records no entry at all. The list is deliberately imprecise in one direction: a stale entry may keep refusing the drop for a while after the detached table itself is gone, or after the table was attached back (until the table is dropped or renamed). In exchange, the `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` path performs no disk access at all. - A `RENAME TABLE` that moves a table between an `Ordinary` and an `Atomic` database changes the identity the dependency is keyed by: the move into `Atomic` assigns a fresh UUID to the table and the move out of it drops the UUID, while a dependency is keyed by the UUID for tables of `Atomic` databases and by the name for tables of `Ordinary` ones. The rename interpreter only knows the names, so the entry used to keep the identity the table had before the move and nothing found it afterwards: the detach recorded no entry and, for the `Atomic -> Ordinary` direction, the drop check even classified the entry of the still attached table as a leftover of a failed `CREATE` and dropped the collection from under it. `DatabaseOnDisk::renameTable` now re-keys the entries of the moved table to its new `StorageID`, where both identities are known. `EXCHANGE` is unaffected: it is only supported between two `Atomic` databases, where the UUIDs do not change. - A table of a database with `lazy_load_tables = 1` is attached as a `StorageTableProxy` and its real storage is built only on the first access, so the engine arguments are not resolved at load time and the dependency on the named collection they name stayed unregistered. `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` was then allowed while such a table still referenced the collection - breaking it at the first access with `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST` - and a `DETACH` of it had no dependency to move to the list of the detached ones, so the protection above silently disappeared in that mode. `DatabaseOrdinary::loadTableLazy` now registers the dependency straight from the metadata, via the new `tryGetUsedNamedCollectionName` helper. An identifier first argument counts as a collection reference only for the engines that resolve their arguments through named collections (a new `StorageFactory::StorageFeatures::supports_named_collections` flag) - for other engines an identifier means something else, e.g. a cluster name for `Distributed` - and for them the signal is time-stable: whether the collection currently exists is deliberately not checked, so the dependency of a collection that is missing at load time (say, after a drop with `check_named_collection_dependencies = 0`) protects it when it is recreated later. The exception is `Remote`/`RemoteSecure`, where the same identifier is also a valid positional argument - a cluster name - when the named-collection lookup does not resolve (marked by the new `StorageFeatures::named_collection_argument_is_ambiguous`; every other flagged engine treats an unknown collection as an error, not as a fallback to a positional form). For them the helper decides from the shape of the argument list first, replicating the decision the engine's own argument parsing would make on the same metadata - which is exactly what a non-lazy load of it does. A `key = value` second argument occurs only in the named-collection form: no positional signature of `Remote` accepts one there, so `parseRemoteFunctionArguments` reports a missing collection instead of reparsing the arguments positionally, and the shape alone proves the reference - the dependency is registered without looking at the collection namespace, exactly as for the unambiguous engines, so a collection missing at load time is protected when it is recreated later. Only a genuinely positional-looking list (`Remote(cluster, system, one)`) or a bare `Remote(x)` consults the namespace, because there the meaning of the stored definition itself depends on it, and the engine resolves it the same way at the same moment. `SETTINGS` are skipped when the shape is examined, as `parseRemoteFunctionArguments` does. `MongoDB` and `MaterializedPostgreSQL` were the only flagged engines whose eager argument resolution did not pass the dependent table to `tryGetNamedCollectionWithOverrides` (they registered the dependency at the lazy load but not when the storage is built); they now pass it, so both load modes register the same dependency. `addDependency` ignores an exact duplicate, because the same dependency is registered again when the proxy is materialized. Tables created with `CREATE TABLE ... AS f(...)` need no lazy branch: a database with `lazy_load_tables = 1` deliberately loads them eagerly as a `StorageTableFunctionProxy` (see `DatabaseOrdinary::shouldLazyLoad`), and that load registers the dependency via `ITableFunction::getUsedNamedCollectionName`. - The cleanup of stale *active* dependencies (leftovers of a failed `CREATE TABLE`, pre-existing from #96181) no longer treats the table's absence from `DatabaseCatalog` alone as a proof of staleness: the dependency of an in-flight `CREATE`/`ATTACH` is registered while the engine arguments are resolved, before the table is committed to the catalog, and a concurrent `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` could prune it and drop the collection while the create later succeeds — recreating the broken metadata this PR fixes. The creating query holds the `DDLGuard` of the table name for the whole window between the registration and the commit, so the drop re-checks the table's existence under that guard before pruning: once the guard is acquired, no create is in flight, and the table's absence proves the entry is stale. (Entries with an empty database name come from dictionaries defined in the configuration files, which are not created through DDL; they are pruned as before.) The pruning removes only the exact stale entry (the collection and the recorded database, table and UUID): `CREATE TABLE ... UUID` can reuse the UUID of a failed create under a different table name, which the guard of the recorded name does not synchronize with, and removing everything under the UUID would erase the live dependency of such an in-flight create — the collection it uses could then be dropped from under the committed table. A new `create_table_pause_before_commit` failpoint keeps a create inside the window for the tests. ### Documented behavior impact `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` now rejects a collection that a detached table or a table in a detached database references, where it previously succeeded (and left a server that could not start). This is what `check_named_collection_dependencies` already promises - "Check that DROP NAMED COLLECTION will not break tables that depend on it" - so the documented behavior of the setting does not change, and setting it to `0` still allows the drop. No documentation update is needed. ### Verified locally (release build) - Before: `CREATE NAMED COLLECTION` + `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = URL(nc)` + `DETACH TABLE` + `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` succeeds, and the server then fails to start with the exact error chain above (exit code 210). Same with `DETACH DATABASE`. - After: the drop is refused, the collection stays, the table attaches back, and a restart of a server with the detached table present succeeds. - `04660_drop_named_collection_detached_table`, `04698_drop_named_collection_detached_after_rename`, and `04823_drop_named_collection_broken_attach` (all new, covering plain `DETACH TABLE` (blocks the drop), `DETACH TABLE ... PERMANENTLY` (does not block; the later `ATTACH` fails cleanly), `DETACH DATABASE`, `Ordinary` databases, renames of the table and of the database before and after the detach, stale dependencies of failed `CREATE TABLE`, and an `ATTACH` that fails after the dependencies were registered — the drop stays refused), and `04836_drop_named_collection_inflight_create` (new, runs `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` against a `CREATE TABLE` and an `ATTACH TABLE` paused between the dependency registration and the commit to the catalog: the drop blocks on the `DDLGuard` and is refused), and `04840_drop_named_collection_cross_engine_rename` (new, moves a table between an `Ordinary` and an `Atomic` database in both directions and then detaches the table and its database), and `04848_drop_named_collection_reused_uuid` (new, prunes the stale entry of a failed `CREATE TABLE ... UUID` while a create of a different table reusing the UUID is paused inside the window: the drop of the old collection succeeds, and the drop of the collection the new table uses stays refused; verified to fail without the fix), plus `03822_named_collection_drop_dependency_check` and `04003_named_collection_drop_dependency_check_dict` pass. - `test_named_collections/test.py::test_drop_while_used_by_lazily_loaded_table` (new integration test: a table using a named collection in an `Atomic` database with `lazy_load_tables = 1`, a server restart so the table comes back as a never-accessed proxy, and the drop refused both while it is attached and after `DETACH TABLE`). It is an integration test because the hole is only reachable once the in-memory list is empty, i.e. after a restart: without one, the `DETACH DATABASE` that precedes `ATTACH DATABASE` leaves its own entry behind and that entry refuses the drop on its own. Verified that it fails without the fix (the drop succeeds) and passes with it. - `test_drop_collection_recreated_under_lazily_loaded_table` (new integration test: the collection is dropped with `check_named_collection_dependencies = 0`, the server restarts while it is missing, and the drop of the recreated collection is refused; verified to fail without the fix), and `test_drop_not_used_by_lazily_loaded_distributed_table` (new integration test: a collection named after the cluster of a lazily loaded `Distributed` table is droppable; passes before and after, pinning the behavior). - `test_drop_collection_recreated_under_lazily_loaded_remote_table` (new integration test: an `ENGINE = Remote(nc, database = 'system')` table in a database with `lazy_load_tables = 1`, the collection dropped with `check_named_collection_dependencies = 0`, a restart while it is missing, and the drop of the recreated collection refused - the unambiguous `key = value` shape registers the dependency from the AST alone), and `test_drop_not_used_by_lazily_loaded_remote_table` (new integration test: a collection named after the cluster of a lazily loaded `ENGINE = Remote(cluster, system, one)` table, created after the table, is droppable after a restart; verified to fail without the fix - the drop was refused with `NAMED_COLLECTION_IS_USED` by the unrelated table), and `test_drop_while_used_by_lazily_loaded_table_function` (new integration test pinning that a `CREATE TABLE ... AS bigquery(collection)` table in a database with `lazy_load_tables = 1` keeps blocking the drop after a restart, before the first access and after a `DETACH TABLE`: such tables are loaded eagerly as a `StorageTableFunctionProxy`, which re-registers the dependency; passes without any code change, confirming no lazy table-function branch is needed). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the server failing to start after a named collection was dropped while a detached table (or a table in a detached database) still referenced it. `DROP NAMED COLLECTION` now counts detached tables as dependents and is refused with `NAMED_COLLECTION_IS_USED`, as `check_named_collection_dependencies` already does for attached tables.

signal.title: Treat a leading CSV null as the first Tuple element in the escaping-rule dispatcher
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114402 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109744 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed reading a `Tuple` column whose first element is `NULL` in the `CustomSeparated`, `Regexp` and `Template` formats with the `CSV` escaping rule. A bare `Tuple` occupies one field per element there, so the leading `\N` field is that element and not the whole column. Previously it was consumed as the whole column, shifting the remaining element fields onto the following columns, so `CustomSeparated` could not read back its own output. Closes #114402. ### Description Closes: #114402 Related: #109744 **The problem.** `CustomSeparated` with `format_custom_escaping_rule = 'CSV'` and a comma field delimiter writes `(NULL, 1), 7` as the bytes `\N,1,7`, and could not read them back. With `input_format_custom_allow_variable_number_of_columns = 1` the row parsed as `(NULL,0)` and `1` -- the tuple's second element was dropped and the next column took it. With that setting off the row was rejected outright. **Root cause.** A bare `Tuple` read with the CSV escaping rule takes one field per element, so a leading null field is the first element, not the whole column. `CSVFormatReader::readFieldImpl` already accounted for that; the shared dispatcher `deserializeFieldByEscapingRule` did not, so every format routing through it consumed the leading null as the whole tuple column and inserted the type default. This is not new behaviour: it reproduces identically on 26.6 and 26.7. **The change.** The predicate moves into `EscapingRuleUtils` as `isCSVSeparateColumnsTuple` and both call sites share it, so they cannot drift. `SerializationTuple::deserializeTextCSV` already applies `null_as_default` per element, so suppressing the short-circuit routes the field to that path. `input_format_csv_deserialize_separate_columns_into_tuple = 0` still restores the old reading, and `Nullable(Tuple)` is still read from a single field. The predicate also bails out when `csv.custom_delimiter` is set: a multi-character field delimiter leaves `csv.delimiter` stale, and the tuple does stay inside one field there. Two carriers the report expected to be unaffected are affected too, and both are fixed here: `Regexp` silently dropped the second element of a tuple inside one capture group (`\N,1` gave `(NULL,0)`), and `Template` rejected the row. **Not fixed here.** A `Tuple` as the *last* `CustomSeparated` column stays broken, because `updateFormatSettings` swaps `csv.delimiter` for `custom.row_after_delimiter` there. That is a separate pre-existing defect, and not specific to nulls: the all-non-null `7,2,1` fails the same way. <details> <summary>Per-arm verification, pre-fix vs post-fix binaries</summary> Both binaries built from `0eb5eba20b929f8`; the pre-fix arm is the pristine-HEAD build. | input | before | after | |---|---|---| | `2,1,7` (control) | `(2,1) 7` | `(2,1) 7` | | `\N,1,7` | `(NULL,0) 1` | `(NULL,1) 7` | | `\N,\N,7` | parse error | `(NULL,NULL) 7` | | nested `Tuple(Tuple(..),..)`, `\N,1,7` | `((0,0),0) 1` | `((0,0),1) 7` | | `Regexp`, tuple in one capture group | `(NULL,0) 7` | `(NULL,1) 7` | | `Template`, `${t:CSV},${b:CSV}` | parse error | `(NULL,1) 7` | | opt-out setting `= 0` | `(NULL,0) 1` | `(NULL,0) 1` | | multi-character field delimiter `\|\|` | `(NULL,0) 7` | `(NULL,0) 7` | | `Nullable(Tuple)` | `\N 7` | `\N 7` | | `Tuple(Int32, Nullable(Int32))`, `2,\N,7` | `(2,NULL) 7` | `(2,NULL) 7` | Both new tests were confirmed to fail against the pre-fix binary. Existing suites `01016_input_null_as_default`, `00938_template_input_format`, `01014_format_custom_separated`, `01085_regexp_input_format`, `01086_regexp_input_format_skip_unmatched`, `02481_custom_separated_and_template_with_csv_field`, `04657_hive_text_tuple_whole_field_null` and `04405_csv_tuple_leading_null_null_as_default` all pass. </details>
