signal.title: Fix non-deterministic `quantileDeterministic` under parallel replicas and distributed queries
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/20480 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `quantileDeterministic`, `quantilesDeterministic` and `medianDeterministic` returning different results for the same data on every run when the query uses parallel replicas, a distributed table, or external aggregation, or when the states are stored in a table (including inside a `Dynamic` value). States written before this version under the unversioned type spelling keep the previous behavior, since their layout cannot change. ### Description `ReservoirSamplerDeterministic::write` never serialized `skip_degree`, and `read` left it at `0`. A state that had been thinned out to one sample per `2^skip_degree` rows was therefore indistinguishable from a complete one after a round trip, so `merge` treated the thinned samples as if they were the full set and under-weighted whichever state had seen the most rows. The in-memory merge path keeps `skip_degree` and is correct, so the bug only appears once states cross a serialization boundary: parallel replicas, distributed queries, external aggregation, or a stored `AggregateFunction` column. Because the split of rows between replicas varies from run to run, the same query over the same data returns different values — the one thing `quantileDeterministic` promises it will not do. This is the distributed half of the bug that was fixed for the single-server case in #20480. The fix gives the state a serialization version through the existing aggregate function state versioning mechanism. Version `1` appends a trailing `UInt8` skip degree after the samples, leaving the version `0` prefix byte-identical, and is gated on the new protocol revision `54491`, so an older peer keeps receiving version `0` states. Legacy stored states are read as version `0` and keep the old behaviour, since the skip degree is simply not present in those bytes. `quantileStateVersion` in `AggregateFunctionQuantile.h` is opt-in: a quantile data structure declares `static constexpr size_t state_version` and takes the version in `serialize`/`deserialize`. Every other quantile family is unversioned as before, so only `AggregateFunction(quantileDeterministic, ...)` gains a version in its type name. A fresh state spells it out: `toTypeName(quantileDeterministicState(...))` is `AggregateFunction(1, quantileDeterministic, ...)`. The **default** state version — the one an unversioned type falls back to — stays `0`, because unversioned spellings already exist in persisted data written before the version was introduced (old parts' `columns.txt`, old `Native` files, the type lists and shared-variant values of old `Dynamic` columns), and none of those media record a default, so a changed default would be ambiguous against data written by older servers. Version `1` applies where it is spelled out explicitly or derived from the negotiated revision on the `Native` wire. To make that spelling reach everywhere, `getStateType` of a versioned quantile returns the **explicitly versioned type**: a fresh `quantileDeterministicState(...)` result is typed `AggregateFunction(1, quantileDeterministic, ...)`, so an export through any generic format writes a header and a payload that agree with each other and with a fresh pinned table, and a state entering a `Dynamic` column carries its version on every medium — the type lists spell it in the name and the binary type encoding carries it in its explicit version field (including inside the values of the shared variant) — so the skip degree survives a `Dynamic` carrier too. `Dynamic` announces its nested types itself, identically for every peer, so they are never rewritten for a negotiated revision: a state inside a `Dynamic` value is always written at the version spelled in its type, and at version `0` when it spells none. So that stored `AggregateFunction` columns still get the fix, a fresh `CREATE TABLE` pins the revision-current state version explicitly into the persisted type name (`pinCurrentStateVersionToAggregateFunctions`) — for explicitly declared columns, for columns inferred from `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` (including a materialized view without an explicit column list), and for the explicit type of `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`, whose column has no pre-existing data. `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN` deliberately does **not** pin: it can be applied to a column that already holds data, and a state version change is a metadata-only conversion (the version is not part of `DataTypeAggregateFunction::equals`), so the pin would make the metadata claim a layout the stored parts do not have - and a rewrite could not repair them either, because a version `0` state does not carry the skip degree that would have to be written. Such a column can still be moved to the current layout for future writes by spelling the version out: `MODIFY COLUMN state AggregateFunction(1, quantileDeterministic, ...)`. The pin only ever raises the version above the function's default, so e.g. `-Merge`-typed columns (whose combinator forwards `getDefaultVersion` but not `getVersionFromRevision`) keep their storage format. For the pin to reach every stored-state path, a `Native` stream written with no negotiated revision at all (revision `0`: `StripeLog` data files, `Set`/`Join` backups, `Native` format files) keeps the version pinned on the type instead of downgrading the state to version `0` - there is no peer to derive a version for, and the stream is read back by whoever wrote it, so the type name in the stream carries the version. ### How it was found The `Stateless tests (amd_llvm_coverage, ParallelReplicas, s3 storage, parallel)` job, where `01913_quantile_deterministic` fails intermittently — 7 times since 2026-07-22, only ever on `ParallelReplicas` or `distributed plan` jobs: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=1d4408f794c389928bda6b52615aa612c12b938b&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20ParallelReplicas%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29 There is no tracking issue for it; the run above reported `medianDeterministic(oid, oid)` giving `503971` on 3 of 20 identical runs instead of `492708`. ### Testing New test `04652_quantile_deterministic_merge_split_independent` merges states stored in a table across four different splits of the same one million rows and requires all of them to match the single-state value. On the pre-fix build the lopsided splits diverge and the balanced ones do not: | split | pre-fix | fixed | |---|---|---| | single state | 492708 | 492708 | | 500k + 500k | 492708 | 492708 | | 990k + 10k | **506014** | 492708 | | 10 x 100k | 492708 | 492708 | | 1 + 999 + 9k + 990k | **486416** | 492708 | Verified end to end on a two-shard cluster with a lopsided 990k/10k split over a real TCP connection: pre-fix `506014`, fixed `492708`. Mixed-version clusters were checked in both directions (new initiator to old shards, old initiator to new shards) and fall back to version `0` without desynchronizing. New test `04819_dynamic_aggregate_function_state_version` pins the `Dynamic` behaviour: the nested type spells the state version across peer revisions, the binary type encoding, the flattened serialization, the shared variant, and a distributed round trip; a merge of two differently thinned states across a `Dynamic` serialization boundary is split-independent, while an explicitly unversioned spelling keeps the version `0` layout and the pre-fix merge behaviour. New test `04842_quantile_deterministic_format_round_trip` exports lopsided states through `RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes`, `TSVWithNamesAndTypes` and headerless `RowBinary` and re-imports them into a fresh pinned table, requiring the split-independent `492708` each time. New test `04820_quantile_deterministic_stripe_log` checks that the pinned state version survives the revision-0 `Native` round trip through `StripeLog` data files (pre-fix, the lopsided splits give `506014` and `486416` instead of `492708`). New test `04822_quantile_deterministic_create_as_select` checks that the pin also reaches columns inferred from `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` and from a materialized view without an explicit column list, survives a `DETACH`/`ATTACH` reload, and keeps the lopsided merge at `492708` (pre-fix: unversioned metadata and `506014`). New test `04824_quantile_deterministic_external_aggregation` forces the aggregation to spill its partial states to temporary files over a lopsided 990000/10000 block split and checks the merge stays split-independent (pre-fix: `506014`), with a `ProfileEvents` check proving the spill actually happened. New test `04825_quantile_deterministic_alter_add_modify_column` checks that the pin reaches a column added through `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`, survives a `DETACH`/`ATTACH` reload, and keeps the lopsided merge at `492708` (pre-fix: unversioned metadata and `506014`); it also writes lopsided version `0` states *before* an `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN` and checks that an unversioned `MODIFY COLUMN` changes neither the metadata version nor the read-back values, that an explicit version `1` `MODIFY COLUMN` keeps those older parts readable (a part records its own column types in `columns.txt`), including through the merge that rewrites them, and that states written after it do keep their skip degree. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1425` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Make ALTER MODIFY COLUMN on named Tuple metadata-only when adding subfields
signal.text: `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN <col> Tuple(...)` on a named `Tuple` that only adds new subfields is now metadata-only (no mutation). Gated behind `SET allow_experimental_metadata_only_named_tuple_alter = 1` (default `false`). Subfield additions through `Array`/`Map`/nested `Tuple` wrappers are also handled. `Nullable(Tuple(...))` is blocked (null map incompatibility). Removing/renaming subfields or changing types still triggers a mutation. Key/index/projection guards reject the metadata-only path when `primary.idx` or skip-index bytes would become invalid (whole tuple in key, or subcolumn whose type changes). Subcolumn references with unchanged types (e.g. `ORDER BY t.a` when only `t.c` is added) are allowed. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `ALTER TABLE ... signal.title: More settings to randomize
signal.text: Extends the stateless-test randomizers in `tests/clickhouse-test` with settings added since they were last swept, and pins the tests that were implicitly relying on the old defaults. `SettingsRandomizer`: * Broadens `query_plan_optimize_join_order_algorithm` to cover `dpsub` and `dphyp` (always with `greedy` kept in the fallback chain, since exhausting the chain throws `EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURE_ERROR`), and randomizes `query_plan_optimize_join_order_max_searched_plans`. * Adds ~35 further query-level settings (`LIMIT BY` / `FINAL` / lazy-`FINAL` / runtime-filter / text-index / statistics / regexp-compilation toggles and their numeric companions). * Adds `use_statistics_for_part_pruning` → `use_statistics` and `use_projection_index_in_read_pools` → `optimize_use_projection_filtering` to `conditional_settings`, so a child setting is not enabled while its parent is off. * Randomizes `function_implementation` over the values the server actually supports, probed at startup: it globally filters every `ImplementationSelector`-backed function and each has a different arch-tag set, so a forced value that some function lacks would raise `NO_SUITABLE_FUNCTION_IMPLEMENTATION`. * A few settings are deliberately left commented out with the reason recorded in place, e.g. `use_constant_folding_in_index_analysis` (unsafe per-part min-max prune, and the trigger for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109893), `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer`, `min_filtered_ratio_for_lazy_final` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112332) and `max_streams_for_union_step`. `MergeTreeSettingsRandomizer`: * Randomizes `concurrent_part_removal_threshold_for_remote_disk`. * The implicit min-max index settings (`add_minmax_index_for_block_number_column`, `add_minmax_index_for_block_offset_column`, `part_minmax_index_columns`) are explicitly kept out: they are not transparent to queries. The first two add real `MINMAX` skipping indices named `auto_minmax_index__block_number` / `auto_minmax_index__block_offset`, which surface in `SHOW INDEXES`, `system.data_skipping_indices`, part checksums and the `Skip` section of `EXPLAIN indexes = 1`; `part_minmax_index_columns = with_block_number_offset` gives every table a part-level min-max index even with no partition key, so `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` grows an extra `Min-Max / Condition: true` block everywhere. This is the same reason their siblings `add_minmax_index_for_{numeric,string,temporal}_columns` were never randomized — all five are `isReadonlySetting`, i.e. part of the table schema. The rest of the diff pins the affected settings in the stateless tests whose output depends on them. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107586 (fixes the `Invalid binary search result in MergeTreeSetIndex` logical error this randomization made much more likely to be hit; merged, so it is pulled in by the branch update) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109893 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112332 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Running CI a few times before merging.

signal.title: Transport join runtime filters across distributed plan stages
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/63915 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/issues/63913 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/63046 A join runtime filter is currently local to its fragment: the build side creates it and only `__applyFilter` sites in that fragment see it, so a fact table scan in another stage crosses its shuffle exchange in full even if the filter would have removed most rows. If `distributed_plan_join_runtime_filters` is enabled, each build task now ships its partial filter through a bounded fan-in cascade of merge stages, and the final stage broadcasts the complete merged union to the probe-side fragments, which apply it before the shuffle. Everything fails open: rows pass unfiltered until the merged filter arrives, so a filter that never arrives (or half-arrives) can't change results. Only inclusion filters travel, a shipped filter never costs more on the wire than one of the configured static size, and filters are only shipped when the estimated build key set is small compared to the receiving scan. This replaces the prototype from https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/63046. There, the initiator collected and merged the filters and probe dispatch was rescheduled around filter readiness; here the partials just ride the exchange layer like any other stream, with no new worker operations, no dispatch changes, and no measurable planning cost. New settings: `distributed_plan_join_runtime_filters` (experimental, default off) is the only user-facing one; with it off, plans, wire traffic and results are identical to master, with one sizing-behavior exception: the exact phase of every runtime filter (including local ones under `enable_join_runtime_filters`) is now bounded by its actual key bytes rather than the hash-table buffer size, which moves the exact-to-bloom degradation point—earlier for long string keys (their bytes were previously uncounted) and later for short keys (the buffer, transiently up to ~2 MB per stream at the default 10000-row cap, no longer counts against the byte budget). Results are unchanged either way. The serialized plan additionally gains `join_runtime_filter_exact_bytes_limit`, which carries a transported filter's exact-phase byte budget to the workers. On public ClickHouse the transported exact-phase row cap is taken from the scan's row estimate, not from column-statistics NDV. HyperLogLog undershoots distinct keys, so using NDV as the cap overflowed complete key sets into bloom filters. An unindexed plan-time filter is also treated as unknown for transport sizing, so it keeps the settings geometry instead of letting statistics override it. ### TPC-H SF1000 r7g.4xlarge, ap-south-2, shared io2 volume read-only on every node, 2 warmups + 3 timed runs per variant, medians. Execution time only (planning excluded; it is identical with the setting on and off). | query | 4 nodes | 8 nodes | 16 nodes | exchange saved (4/8/16) | |---|---|---|---|---| | q17 | −77.6% | −65.6% | −60.8% | 202.7 / 202.6 / 202.6 GiB | | q02 | −71.9% | −67.1% | −45.9% | 51.7 / 51.6 / 41.5 GiB | | q20 | −63.7% | −49.6% | −33.9% | 34.6 / 33.7 / 25.3 GiB | | q11 | −42.9% | −27.0% | −17.7% | 25.1 / 24.8 / 23.6 GiB | | q07 | −23.3% | −18.6% | −16.6% | 37.2 / 37.2 / 36.9 GiB | The other ten campaign queries are ties, with one exception: q16 regresses (+0.15 s at 8 nodes, +0.39 s at 16) because a filter that ends up pruning nothing still gets broadcast and the broadcast grows with node count. The admission heuristic should catch this; tracked in the RFC. ### TPC-H SF100 on a real network From the prototype (https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/63046), included because it is the measurement over an actual NIC: 4× m8g.4xlarge, 9.53 Gbps between nodes, 0.116 ms RTT, medians of 5. The mechanism differs but the filters, admission logic, and apply sites are the same. | query | single node (s) | dist 4N off (s) | dist 4N on (s) | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---| | q02 | 0.448 | 1.214 | 0.446 | 2.72x | | q03 | 1.585 | 1.498 | 1.075 | 1.39x | | q07 | 1.582 | 1.501 | 1.186 | 1.27x | | q10 | 2.024 | 1.853 | 1.606 | 1.15x | | q11 | 0.317 | 0.593 | 0.293 | 2.02x | | q12 | 1.156 | 0.830 | 0.615 | 1.35x | | q17 | 1.321 | 3.206 | 0.831 | 3.86x | (q04, q09, q13, q14, q16, q19, q20, q22 were flat there; q05/q08/q15/q18 excluded for environment reasons unrelated to the transport, see https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/63046.) Plan shapes for the two headline queries, from the SF100 evidence runs: *q17 without the transport, both `lineitem` scans run in full:* *q17 with it, both scans collapse ~996x before their shuffles:* *q02 without the transport, both 80M-row `partsupp` arms feed the join unpruned:* *q02 with it, the union reaches both `partsupp` scans and the cascade collapses:* ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Join runtime filters now travel across distributed plan stages when `distributed_plan_join_runtime_filters` is enabled: build-side tasks ship partial filters over the exchange layer and probe-side scans apply the merged union before their shuffle exchange, dramatically reducing the number of rows crossing the network. All failure modes are fail-open and results never depend on the filters.

signal.title: Do not mark granule empty when rows are removed from a chunk
signal.text: With `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1`, the read is split into PK-range layers (same machinery as FINAL); a boundary granule belongs to two layers, and the FilterSortedStreamByRange` border filter drops the other layer's rows. The query condition cache write in `FilterTransform` assumes a zero-rows-after-filter chunk contained every row of its mark ranges, so it recorded the whole granule as non-matching even though its rows in the other layer matched. Later queries with the same condition skipped the granule and returned too few rows. Cause of the `03821_join_use_nulls_outer_to_inner` flakiness. New flag `MarkRangesInfo::has_dropped_rows`, set (copy-on-write) by `FilterSortedStreamByRange` on chunks that lost rows; `FilterTransform` skips cache writes for flagged chunks. Suppresses only writes for boundary granules - reads and interior-granule writes keep working - and covers any future consumer of `readByLayers`. `04891_query_condition_cache_join_by_pk_ranges`: deterministic minimal repro (returned `1`, `0` before the fix; `1`, `1` after). All existing QCC and FINAL split-ranges tests pass, including `03821` with the triggering settings forced. <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix query condition cache poisoning by JOIN queries with query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1, which made later queries with the same WHERE condition return too few rows.

signal.title: Read and checksum the UNIQUE KEY dense-index SST through IDataPartStorage
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow the UNIQUE KEY to work on encrypted and remote disks by reading and writing its dense-index SST through the part storage abstraction; the SST is now recorded in `checksums.txt`. ### Description The per-part UNIQUE KEY dense index (`unique_key_index.sst`) was opened and written by local filesystem path, which only worked on local disks and left the sidecar outside the part's checksum accounting. This PR drives the SST through `IDataPartStorage` using a custom RocksDB `Env`(a read-only `FileSystem` over `IDataPartStorage::readFile` for the reader, a `WriteBuffer`-backed one for the writer), so encrypted and remote disks work as well. The SST is now recorded in `checksums.txt`, so it is transferred by backup/fetch like any other part file and validated by `checkConsistencyBase`: a missing or wrongly-sized SST fails the standard consistency check and the part is detached as broken, while size-preserving corruption is caught at load time by `ensureValidDenseIndex` (RocksDB block-checksum + entry-count validation), which removes and rebuilds the index. On readonly storage a corrupt or absent SST fails the load closed instead of activating an unprobeable part. The previous restriction that UNIQUE KEY tables must reside on local-only storage policies is removed.
signal.author: JingYanchao

signal.title: Push dynamic TopN thresholds into MergeTree reads for ORDER BY ... LIMIT (2-3x on ClickBench Q24/Q26)
signal.text: **Use case.** `ORDER BY ... LIMIT n` over a sorted-by-something-else table with a narrow projection, e.g. ClickBench Q24/Q26: ```sql SELECT SearchPhrase FROM hits WHERE SearchPhrase <> '' ORDER BY EventTime LIMIT 10; SELECT SearchPhrase FROM hits WHERE SearchPhrase <> '' ORDER BY EventTime, SearchPhrase LIMIT 10; ``` The original build of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/81944 implemented a **dynamic TopN threshold pushdown** (`Push TopN threshold to MergeTreeSource`, commit `2e2f594308f4`, plus `Better query condition cache: make TopN dynamic filters deterministic and reusable`, gated by `max_limit_to_push_down_topn_predicate = 100`): while the partial-sort transform maintains the current top-`n`, the running n-th-best value of the `ORDER BY` key is pushed down into the `MergeTree` read as a dynamic threshold, so granules whose key range cannot beat the current top-`n` are skipped instead of read, decompressed, and sorted. This mechanism was dropped during the upstreaming of that PR (the scaffolding was removed from the branch; the surviving `RewriteOrderByLimitPass` is a different, row-offset-based approach — it is off by default and measures performance-neutral on ClickBench when enabled). Master's lazy materialization (`query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization`) covers the wide-`SELECT *` case (Q23), but does not prune reads for narrow projections: every granule passing the `WHERE` is still fully processed. Measured on identical single-part ClickBench data (hot, interleaved runs, 96-core aarch64), original bench-opt build (25.9.1.1) vs master `405e218ff`: Q24 0.009 s vs 0.013 s, Q26 0.008 s vs 0.013 s (1.2–1.3x with times this small). The gap is much larger on the official `c7a.metal-48xl` numbers: Q24 0.014 s vs 0.046 s, Q26 0.014 s vs 0.044 s (**2–3x**). A related consideration from the original design: the dynamic filter interacts with the query condition cache, so the thresholds need to be deterministic/reusable (or excluded from the cache key) — the original branch had a follow-up commit specifically making the TopN dynamic filters deterministic for that reason. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/81944 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/81944#issuecomment-5280709772

signal.title: Support Nullable(JSON) in tupleElement
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111234 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry: You can now access nested properties on a nullable JSON column, for example `col::Nullable(JSON).Id`. Previously this failed with `First argument for function tupleElement cannot be Nullable(JSON)`, which made it impossible to combine a cast to `Nullable(JSON)`, used to get `NULL` instead of an empty `{}` for a missing nested object, with property access on the result. Rows that are `NULL` in the outer column now yield `NULL` for the extracted path. ### Details `tupleElement` refused a `Nullable(JSON)` first argument in both `getReturnTypeImpl` and `executeImpl`. The refusal was specific to the JSON branch: | Probe | Before | | --- | --- | | `tupleElement(JSON, 'Id')` | works | | `tupleElement(Nullable(JSON), 'Id')` | `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` | | `Nullable(JSON)` as a type | legal; casts and NULL round-trip correctly | | `tupleElement(Nullable(Tuple(...)), 'a')` | already unwraps and propagates NULL | | `assumeNotNull(j).Id` | already produces the intended values | So the semantics were already implemented for `Tuple` and reachable via `assumeNotNull`; only the JSON branch rejected the input. This removes both throws and reuses the existing mechanism: - `getReturnTypeImpl` promotes the extracted path type with `makeExtractedSubcolumnsNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe` - `executeImpl` folds the outer null map into the extracted column with `NullableSubcolumnCreator` Both paths go through the same helper: `NullableSubcolumnCreator::create(DataTypePtr)` calls exactly that promotion function so the returned type and column cannot drift apart. Resulting behaviour: - a path with a type hint is promoted to `Nullable(T)` - an untyped path stays `Dynamic`, which cannot sit inside `Nullable` but can represent `NULL` itself, so the outer null map is applied to the `Dynamic` directly - `Nullable(QBit)` remains rejected, and the `Tuple` and `QBit` paths are untouched The two "must be Tuple, Nullable(Tuple), QBit, JSON or array of these" messages now also list `Nullable(JSON)`. ### Verification Added `04891_tuple_element_nullable_json`, covering const and materialized inputs, all-NULL input, mixed NULL/non-NULL rows, typed and untyped paths, a missing path, `Array(Nullable(JSON))`, chained access through a nullable sub-object, and the query from the issue. It also asserts `Nullable(QBit)` still throws, since that shares the type dispatch this changes. Verified against a `RelWithDebInfo` build of this branch: ``` SELECT tupleElement('{"Id":1}'::Nullable(JSON), 'Id') -> 1 SELECT CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(JSON)').Id -> NULL SELECT toTypeName('{"a":1}'::Nullable(JSON).a) -> Dynamic SELECT toTypeName(CAST('{"a":1}', 'Nullable(JSON(a UInt32))').a) -> Nullable(UInt32) SELECT (number % 2 ? NULL : '{"a":42}')::Nullable(JSON).a FROM numbers(4) -> 42, NULL, 42, NULL ``` Note the test orders by a companion `Int` column rather than by the result, because an untyped JSON path is `Dynamic` and `ORDER BY` on `Dynamic` is rejected by default (`allow_suspicious_types_in_order_by`).

signal.title: Add table schema to SQLInsert output
signal.text: Adds the `output_format_sql_insert_include_table_schema` setting for the `SQLInsert` output format. When enabled, `SQLInsert` prepends a `CREATE TABLE` statement derived from the query result schema, making the generated SQL directly replayable into an empty database. The table definition uses the result column names and types with `MergeTree` and `ORDER BY tuple()`. Source-table metadata such as keys, default expressions, codecs, TTLs, and indexes is not preserved. The setting is disabled by default and cannot be enabled together with `output_format_sql_insert_use_replace`. The change includes embedded documentation and stateless coverage for replaying the generated SQL, complex types, identifiers, empty results, batching, and incompatible settings. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/84736 ### Changelog category: - Improvement ### Changelog entry: The `SQLInsert` output format can now prepend a `CREATE TABLE` statement with result column names and types. Enable `output_format_sql_insert_include_table_schema` to produce a ClickHouse SQL script that recreates the table and loads the exported data.

signal.title: Delete Iceberg table files on DROP with iceberg_delete_data_on_drop
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108524 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `DROP TABLE` on an Iceberg table with `iceberg_delete_data_on_drop = 1` not deleting the table's files, which made re-creating a table at the same path fail with `TABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108524 With `iceberg_delete_data_on_drop = 1`, `DROP TABLE` on an Iceberg table left the underlying files in place, so a later `CREATE TABLE` at the same path failed with `Iceberg table with path ... already exists (TABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS)`. Long-standing (reproduces at least down to v25.9), not a recent regression. Two independent bugs, both in the self-managed Iceberg drop path: 1. `IcebergMetadata::drop` listed the files to delete with the table path passed as both the listing base and the prefix (`listFiles(..., table_path, table_path, "")`). `listFiles` keys on `path / prefix`, so it looked under `table_path/table_path` and matched nothing. Fixed by using an empty prefix so everything under the table path is enumerated (this matches the existing `create` and `Hudi` callers). 2. `StorageObjectStorage::drop` runs in a background pool and read `iceberg_delete_data_on_drop` from the global context, where it is always the default `false`, so the deletion never ran even after bug 1 was fixed. The value is now captured from the query context in `checkTableCanBeDropped` (called on the drop path with the query context, on the same storage object) and applied to a copy of the global context passed to the background drop. This is the same `mutable`-flag pattern `StorageNATS`/`StorageRabbitMQ` already use for drop-time state. Both the self-managed engine path (`Iceberg`/`IcebergLocal`) and the `DataLakeCatalog` database path go through the same `checkTableCanBeDropped` -> `drop()` on one storage instance, so both are covered. With the setting off (default) files are left in place, as before. Regression test `04365_iceberg_delete_data_on_drop_108524` fails without the fix (files survive the drop, re-create fails) and passes with it; it also checks the default-off behavior is unchanged.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Add SCANN Vector Index Support
signal.text: Add [Google ScaNN](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/scann) as a new approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) backend for the `vector_similarity` skip index in `MergeTree` tables, accessible via `TYPE vector_similarity('scann', ...)` syntax. ScaNN uses an IVF-based index with asymmetric hashing (LUT16) and exact reranking, complementing the existing HNSW backend. The implementation integrates three new contrib dependencies — `scann`, `highway` (portable SIMD), and `eigen` (header-only linear algebra) — without modifying any upstream submodule source files; all platform adaptation is in the corresponding `-cmake/` wrappers. **Supported distance functions:** `L2Distance`, `cosineDistance`, `dotProduct`. **New query-tuning settings:** - `scann_num_leaves_to_search` — number of partitions to search at query time (0 = use the index-configured default, typically `num_vectors^0.25`). - `scann_candidate_pool_size` — asymmetric hashing candidate pool size fed into the exact reranker (0 = automatic: `1000 × topK`). All training artifacts (partitioner proto, asymmetric hashing codebook, hashed dataset, datapoint-to-token mapping) are serialized to disk on index build via `SingleMachineSearcherConfig`, so search results are deterministic across server restarts without retraining. **Example:** ```sql CREATE TABLE tab ( id UInt64, vec Array(Float32), INDEX idx vec TYPE vector_similarity('scann', 'cosineDistance', 128) GRANULARITY 100000000 ) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; -- Query-time tuning SELECT id, cosineDistance(vec, [...]) AS dist FROM tab ORDER BY dist LIMIT 10 SETTINGS scann_num_leaves_to_search = 80, scann_candidate_pool_size = 5000; ``` ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added Google ScaNN as a new backend for the vector_similarity index type (syntax: TYPE vector_similarity('scann', 'cosineDistance', N)). Supports L2Distance, cosineDistance, and dotProduct distance functions with deterministic results across restarts. Two new settings — scann_num_leaves_to_search and scann_candidate_pool_size — allow per-query tuning of recall/latency trade-offs. ### Related issue: Closes #103664. The issue mentions ScaNN, but the reply references SPANN — not sure if that was a typo. I went ahead and implemented ScaNN as originally requested, and would welcome any response.

signal.title: Reject a table reference in the IN operator of a constraint expression
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107424 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A constraint whose `IN` operator had a bare identifier on the right-hand side, such as `CONSTRAINT c CHECK a IN (b)`, silently rewrote it into a table reference `default.b` and persisted it. The resulting table rejected every `INSERT` with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, and the server refused to start once the referenced column was dropped. Such a constraint is now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS` when it is supplied by `CREATE TABLE`, a full-definition `ATTACH TABLE`, or `ALTER TABLE ... ADD/MODIFY CONSTRAINT`, and when it is copied by `CREATE TABLE ... AS` or `CLONE AS`. Existing tables keep loading. ### Description `AddDefaultDatabaseVisitor` turns an `IN` right-hand side into a table identifier. Correct in a SELECT, where `x IN t` is shorthand for `x IN (SELECT * FROM t)`, but wrong for a constraint, evaluated against the inserted row. The rewritten AST is persisted. Measured on master, for `CHECK a IN (b)` with `b` a column: `SHOW CREATE` reports a constraint the user never wrote (`IN (default.b)`), and every `INSERT` fails `Code: 47 UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`. Dropping that column makes the metadata unloadable, fatal at startup. Found on `Stress test (amd_msan)` in three unrelated PRs, as the fuzzer's operand-swapped mutation of `02841_not_ready_set_constraints`. This adds `checkConstraintExpressionIsValid`, mirroring #107424's key-expression check, applied only to user-supplied DDL. The recursion stops at subquery boundaries, so `IN <table>` inside a subquery keeps working. **Cases found in review.** `CREATE TABLE ... AS src` and `CLONE AS src` parse no declaration; they copy the source constraints, so a legacy source could seed the shape into a new table. Copied constraints go through the same gate. An `ALTER` command that stores nothing (`ADD ... IF NOT EXISTS` on an existing name, `MODIFY ... IF EXISTS` on a missing one) stays accepted as on master, judged against the commands preceding it in the same statement. **What this removes.** Where the identifier names an existing table the constraint did work, but only in the process that parsed the DDL: the load path never applies that visitor, so after a restart `INSERT` fails `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`. I reject it rather than keep a form that write-deads a table at the next restart. Tell me if you would rather keep it. Unlike #107424 I do not reject at load time: such metadata exists in the wild. Existing tables keep loading, stay ALTER-able including `DROP CONSTRAINT`, and Replicated databases still recover them.

signal.title: Rebuild skip indices, projections, TTL and MATERIALIZED columns left stale by ALTER MODIFY / UPDATE / CLEAR COLUMN
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112302 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/85985 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112302 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/85985 A mutation decides what to rebuild by comparing the mutated column against the columns that an index / projection / TTL expression requires. When the expression reads a **subcolumn** (`t.a`, `json.a`), those required columns carry the subcolumn name while the mutation tracks the whole stored column (`t`), so the comparison never matched. On **wide parts** the dependent files (`skp_idx_*`, projection parts, TTL info) were then hardlinked into the mutated part, leaving them describing data that no longer exists. Compact parts are unaffected, because a mutation rewrites the whole part. Every such site now resolves an expression's required columns to their top-level columns through one shared helper, `getRequiredColumnsWithSubcolumnsReplaced`, which rewrites subcolumns to `getSubcolumn` — the same rewrite used for `MATERIALIZED` expressions in #85985 — and re-analyzes the expression. The rewrite is applied where the value is recomputed as well, so it is derived from the *updated* parent column instead of a subcolumn pre-extracted from the source part. What is fixed: - **Skip index on a subcolumn** — rebuilt on `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN`, `ALTER UPDATE`, `ALTER CLEAR COLUMN` and patch updates of the parent. The recompute in the partial-rewrite path (`MutateSomePartColumns`) now extracts the subcolumn from the updated parent instead of failing with `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` or reading stale data. - **Projection** — rebuilt when the altered column feeds its sort key (a subcolumn sort key was missed) or its `WHERE` clause. Both decide what the projection stores: the sort key is persisted as raw bytes in the projection's own primary index, and the `WHERE` fixes the stored rows and aggregate states. A column used only in the projection's `SELECT` needs no rebuild, because that payload is converted on read. - **`alter_column_secondary_index_mode`** — the `throw`/`compatibility` guard in `checkAlterIsPossible` now also fires for an explicit index defined on a subcolumn of the altered column, instead of accepting the ALTER and then failing (or silently dropping the index) during the mutation. - **TTL on a subcolumn** — a `TTL t.a` is recalculated when the parent column is mutated, so rows and columns whose TTL moved into the past actually expire. `SHOW CREATE TABLE` still shows the original expression. - **`MATERIALIZED` column** — recalculated when `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN` changes the type of a column it reads (whole column or subcolumn), including chains of `MATERIALIZED` columns, and everything depending on them is rebuilt too. Previously only `ALTER UPDATE` recalculated them, so a value-changing conversion left them holding values computed from data the mutation had just rewritten. A `MATERIALIZED` column that is part of a key cannot be recalculated in an existing part — its sort order and partition id are fixed when the part is written, which is also why `MATERIALIZE COLUMN` refuses key columns — so such an ALTER is now rejected unless the conversion preserves values. Reproductions, all silent wrong results before this PR: ```sql -- skip index on a subcolumn CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32, t Tuple(a Int32, b String), INDEX idx t.a TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS index_granularity = 4, min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0, min_rows_for_wide_part = 0; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, (number, 'x') FROM numbers(16); ALTER TABLE t MODIFY COLUMN t Tuple(a Float32, b String); SELECT count() FROM t WHERE t.a >= 1; -- 0 before, 15 now SELECT count() FROM t WHERE t.a >= 1 SETTINGS use_skip_indexes=0; -- 15, ground truth -- projection filtered on a column whose type changes CREATE TABLE t2 (id UInt64, x Int64, PROJECTION p (SELECT sum(id) WHERE x < 0)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0; INSERT INTO t2 SELECT number, toInt64(3000000000) + number FROM numbers(100); ALTER TABLE t2 MODIFY COLUMN x Int32; -- every value wraps negative, so WHERE x < 0 now matches all rows SELECT sum(id) FROM t2 WHERE x < 0; -- 0 before, 4950 now -- MATERIALIZED column computed from a column whose type changes CREATE TABLE t3 (x Int64, m Int64 MATERIALIZED x) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() SETTINGS min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0; INSERT INTO t3 VALUES (5000000000); ALTER TABLE t3 MODIFY COLUMN x Int32; SELECT x, m FROM t3; -- 705032704, 5000000000 before; 705032704, 705032704 now ``` Tests: `04617_stale_subcolumn_skip_index_after_mutation` and `04840_recalculate_materialized_column_on_source_type_change`. Known gaps left for follow-up pull requests: a subcolumn in a projection `WHERE` is accepted at `CREATE` but fails at `INSERT` (`Not found column t.a in block`), and the aggregation assignments of a GROUP BY TTL are not covered by the rewrite. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong query results caused by a mutation leaving data derived from the mutated column stale on wide parts. A skip index or a TTL expression defined on a subcolumn (for example a `Tuple`, `Nested`, `Map` or `JSON` element) is now rebuilt or recalculated when `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN`, `ALTER UPDATE` or `ALTER CLEAR COLUMN` changes the parent column; a projection is rebuilt when the altered column feeds its sort key or its `WHERE` clause; and a `MATERIALIZED` column is recalculated when `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN` changes the type of a column it is computed from. An `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN` that would change the values of a `MATERIALIZED` column used in the sorting or partition key is now rejected, because such a column cannot be recalculated in an existing part.

signal.title: Hold the table lock across a lightweight UPDATE pipeline
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104431 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server abort (`Logical error: Part patch-... doesn't exist`) when a `DROP TABLE` runs concurrently with a lightweight `UPDATE` on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table. The update now holds the table's shared lock until its patch part is committed, so the `DROP` waits instead of removing it. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #104431 as an unrelated `Upgrade check (amd_release)` failure with no fix on master: STID `3208-458f`, 4 hits on 4 unrelated PRs in 6 days ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104431&sha=7970f08a82eaf2ad5217d57a7796ae1c5e920030&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade+check+%28amd_release%29)). **What breaks.** A lightweight `UPDATE` racing a `DROP TABLE` aborts the server, release builds included: `Transaction::commit`'s `modifyPartState` calls sit in `NOEXCEPT_SCOPE`, whose catch-all is `std::terminate`. **Root cause.** `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute` takes `lockForShare` into a function-local holder and parks only the *storage* in the returned pipeline; `QueryPlanResourceHolder` keeps `storage_holders` and `table_locks` separately, so the lock dies when `execute()` returns, long before the sink commits the patch part. A concurrent `DROP` then takes the exclusive lock, `dropAllData()` clears `data_parts_indexes`, and the commit cannot find its own part. Reproducing it needs a UUID-less database (`Memory`/`Ordinary`), where `DROP` removes the data inline instead of deferring it, hence the intermittency. **The change.** Move the already-acquired lock into the pipeline's resources, as the INSERT path does at `InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:1297`. Three entry points: `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute`, `InterpreterAlterQuery::executeToTable` (lightweight rewrite), and `StorageAlias::updateLightweight`, which resolves a *different* storage and so needs the target's own lock, as `StorageAlias::read` does. `DELETE FROM` rewrites to `UPDATE` and is covered transitively. A concurrent `DROP` or `DETACH` now waits for an in-flight lightweight update, as it already does for `INSERT`. `TRUNCATE` is unaffected: for `MergeTree` it takes no exclusive lock (`InterpreterDropQuery.cpp:332`). **Validation.** New test `04905_lwu_drop_race_table_lock.sh`, one arm per fixed carrier. `sleep_before_commit_local_part_in_replicated_table_ms` opens the commit window, and each arm waits for the sink to log that pause before dropping, so an arm that never reaches the window reports that instead of passing quietly. Fails on master with the reported abort, passes with the fix, 50/50 runs green. <details> <summary>Both-directions matrix (every cell measured, Build IDs asserted against the running server)</summary> | binary | `UPDATE` | `ALTER ... UPDATE` | via `Alias` | |---|---|---|---| | master `1b90b99d` | ABORT | ABORT | ABORT | | interpreters-only `6ab7bac7` | pass | pass | ABORT | | full fix `33fc2917` | pass | pass | pass | The middle row is the control that shows the `StorageAlias` change is necessary: with both interpreter fixes applied, the alias arm is the only one that still aborts. The lock demonstrably serializes the two queries: `dropAllData: waiting for locks` moves from 1.47 s after the patch-part rename (inside the commit window) to 4.03 s after it (past the commit). Deadlock check: the change only extends the lifetime of a *Read* acquisition, and no sink on this path acquires the table lock at all. `update_sequential_consistency = 1`, which waits on the replication queue while the lock is held, and a following `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` both complete normally. </details>

signal.title: Resolve the 25.8 cherry-pick conflict of #112327
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112327 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114796 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a use-after-free when a `LEFT JOIN` to a dictionary with `join_algorithm = 'direct'` had a join key that is serialized `Sparse`. `getColumnVectorData` returned a `PaddedPODArray` reference into a column owned only by a function-local `ColumnPtr`, so the dictionary lookup read freed memory. ### Description Backport of #112327 to `25.8`. The robot cherry-pick #114796 is `CONFLICTING`, so the automation cannot carry it. The conflict is in one file. `getColumnVectorData` materializes its key column with `removeSpecialRepresentations` on master and with `recursiveRemoveSparse` here; `removeSpecialRepresentations` does not exist on this branch. The resolution keeps 25.8's call and takes the fix's predicate, so the resolved change is the same 8 insertions and 7 deletions as the merged commit. On this branch the copy therefore guards `Const` and `Sparse`; `ColumnReplicated` does not exist here and is dropped from the comment's carrier list. `25.8` is affected. On the official `25.8.30.17` binary the repro (a 2M-row sparse probe joined to a `FLAT()` dictionary) segfaults in 2 of 7 runs, and with jemalloc junk filling it fails 4 of 4 with `Invalid number of rows in Chunk ... expected 65409, got 0`. The same data written densely passes. Comparing returned values alone cannot see this, because freed but intact memory still yields the correct numbers. Verified in both directions with a clang-19 Debug build, this branch's pinned compiler, asserting build ids against the running server. Pristine `25.8` aborts on the first assertion of the ported test, at `PODArray::operator[]` inside `FlatDictionary::hasKeys` reached through `IDictionary::getByKeys` and `DirectKeyValueJoin::joinBlock` - the mechanism reported on master. With the fix the test passes and the repro returns the correct result in 3 of 3 runs. One branch adaptation in the test: `enable_lazy_columns_replication` does not exist on `25.8` and is rejected as an unknown setting, so it is dropped from the `ARRAY JOIN` statement. signal.title: Add VALID FOR clause for users and credentials
signal.text: We support `VALID UNTIL` for users and credentials. This adds `VALID FOR <interval>` as a convenience shorthand. Instead of an absolute date and time, `VALID FOR` accepts an interval, and the expiration deadline is computed as the current time plus that interval at the moment the query is executed. The result is stored in the `VALID UNTIL` form, so `SHOW CREATE USER` always displays the resolved absolute deadline. It can be used everywhere `VALID UNTIL` can - at the user level and per authentication method, in both `CREATE USER` and `ALTER USER`. Examples: ```sql CREATE USER u1 VALID FOR INTERVAL 1 DAY; CREATE USER u2 IDENTIFIED WITH plaintext_password BY 'x' VALID FOR INTERVAL 3 MONTH; ALTER USER u1 VALID FOR INTERVAL 1 DAY + INTERVAL 12 HOUR; ``` Implementation notes: the current time is injected as a literal (rather than using `now`, which is non-deterministic and would not fold to a constant expression), and the deadline is computed with `toDateTime64` so that large intervals saturate at the `DateTime64` upper bound instead of overflowing the year-2106 boundary of `DateTime`. Note on the system table schema: to represent deadlines beyond the year 2106 exactly, the `valid_until` column of `system.users` changes from `Array(DateTime)` to `Array(DateTime64(0))`. This is a backward-incompatible change of a documented system table for tooling that introspects the column type; the values themselves keep second precision. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added the `VALID FOR <interval>` clause to `CREATE USER` and `ALTER USER` as a shorthand for `VALID UNTIL`. The expiration deadline is computed as the current time plus the given interval at query execution time and stored in the `VALID UNTIL` form. The `valid_until` column of the `system.users` table now has the type `Array(DateTime64(0))` instead of `Array(DateTime)`, so that deadlines beyond the year 2106 are represented exactly; tooling that reads this column should handle the new type. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: Physical column shadowing `_part`: `SELECT count() ... WHERE isNull(_part > 0)` throws NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK
signal.text: **Describe what's wrong** On a table that has a **physical column named `_part`** (shadowing the virtual column), an aggregate query whose `WHERE` wraps that column in `isNull(...)` fails with `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`, at default settings. The same predicate works in a plain `SELECT *`, and the same query works when the column does not shadow a virtual. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduces on current master, `26.8.1.1061` (official build). 20/20 deterministic. **How to reproduce** ```sql CREATE TABLE t_part_shadow (_part UInt32, x UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t_part_shadow VALUES (1, 100), (2, 200), (3, 300); SELECT count() FROM t_part_shadow WHERE isNull(_part > 0); -- throws ``` ``` Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column _part in block. There are only columns: _partition_id, _part_uuid, _part_data_version, _disk_name. (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) ``` No settings required — plain defaults over HTTP and native client, old and new analyzer both throw. **Expected behavior** `0` — `_part` here is the user's `UInt32` column (`_part > 0` is never NULL), which is what `SELECT count() FROM t_part_shadow WHERE isNull(toNullable(_part) > 0)` and `SELECT * FROM t_part_shadow WHERE isNull(_part > 0)` correctly return. **Additional context — scope probed** - `SELECT * ... WHERE isNull(_part > 0)` **works**; `SELECT count()`, `EXPLAIN SELECT count()`, and the `PREWHERE` form all **throw** — the trigger is the read that needs no physical columns, where the filter becomes a candidate for part-level evaluation over virtual columns. - The exception's block dump (`_partition_id, _part_uuid, _part_data_version, _disk_name`) is the virtuals-only filter block: `getHeaderWithVirtualsForFilter` correctly *skips* virtuals shadowed by physical columns (`if (columns.contains(name)) continue;` in `MergeTreeData`), but the predicate analysis still classifies the `isNull(_part > 0)` conjunct as evaluable over virtuals, so `filterPartsByVirtualColumns` evaluates it on a block that (correctly) has no `_part`. - Un-wrapped comparisons on the shadowed column work: `WHERE _part = 2`, `WHERE (_part = 2) AND (_part > 0)` are fine; `isNull(...)` / `IS NULL` composition is what reaches the broken path. `NOT (_part > 0)` and `(_part > 0) = 1` also work. - Shadowing `_partition_id` instead does not trigger it. - The existing test `04201_virtual_column_override_where_filter.sql` pins the simple-predicate forms of this exact shadowing scenario; the `isNull` composition is the gap. Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signal.title: Keep the column default when another MODIFY COLUMN restates the type
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a single `ALTER` with two `MODIFY COLUMN` subcommands on the same column silently corrupting that column's default: a default set by one subcommand was dropped, and a `REMOVE DEFAULT`/`MATERIALIZED`/`ALIAS` was undone, whenever a following subcommand restated the column type. ### Description Two `MODIFY COLUMN` subcommands on one column silently corrupted its default in two opposite directions, from plain DDL, returning success and logging nothing. Wrong results: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (event String, c UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY tuple(); ALTER TABLE t MODIFY COLUMN c UInt32 MATERIALIZED JSONExtractUInt(event, 'x'), MODIFY COLUMN c UInt32 CODEC(T64, LZ4); INSERT INTO t (event) VALUES ('{"x":42}'); SELECT c FROM t; -- 0, expected 42; default_kind was empty ``` Valid input rejected: `MODIFY COLUMN c REMOVE MATERIALIZED, MODIFY COLUMN c UInt32 CODEC(...)` left the `MATERIALIZED` in place, so a later `INSERT INTO t (event, c)` failed with `ILLEGAL_COLUMN` where it succeeds after a plain `REMOVE`. Omitting the type was already correct, so one token decided whether it worked. `AlterCommand::apply` replaced the column default whenever the subcommand carried a data type, writing an empty default over what a preceding subcommand had written into the shared metadata copy. `AlterCommands::prepare` compensated by back-filling from the table, but it reads the pre-ALTER column: nothing to back-fill for a default just set, and a stale default to resurrect for one just removed. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113853#discussion_r3737650442 The default is now replaced only when the subcommand carries a default expression, and the back-fill is gone, making `MODIFY_COLUMN` match `ADD_COLUMN`. One accepted statement starts being rejected: dropping a `MATERIALIZED` that made the column nullable while restating the type as non-nullable now reports the conversion it cannot perform, as those statements issued separately already do. New test `04904` fails on the parent commit and passes with the fix; 50/50 randomized runs are green. A 55-test ALTER neighbour set ran on both binaries: nothing fails only with the fix. Also noticed, not addressed here: an existing default unreadable as the new type is rejected even with a single `MODIFY COLUMN`, pre-existing in `validate()`.

signal.title: Fix logical error in optimize_or_like_chain with aggregate/window function on LIKE LHS
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error (`Function node with name '...' is not resolved as ordinary function`) that could occur with `optimize_or_like_chain` enabled when an aggregate or window function appeared on the left-hand side of a `LIKE`/`ILIKE`/`match` inside an `OR` chain. ### Description Found by the BuzzHouse fuzzer (STID 3477-117d) on [this CI run](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107567&sha=16ccfffe167f14e51996ce4ec16384f92e4d15d0&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_msan%29). Not caused by that PR — it is a trunk analyzer bug the fuzzer happened to surface there. `isExpressionNonDeterministic` in `ConvertOrLikeChainPass` guarded its `getFunctionOrThrow()` call with `FunctionNode::isResolved()`. `isResolved()` returns true for aggregate and window functions too (it only checks that the function pointer is set), but `getFunctionOrThrow()` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when the function kind is not `ORDINARY`. So a resolved aggregate (e.g. `count()`) or window function nested under a `LIKE` argument in an `OR` chain tripped the assertion — an exception in release builds, an abort in debug/sanitizer builds. Fix: guard with `isOrdinaryFunction()` instead, matching the existing correct guard in `PlannerExpressionAnalysis`. Aggregate/window functions are never non-deterministic-in-scope-of-query at this point, so recursing into their children is sufficient. Minimal reproducer (aborts before the fix on a debug build): ```sql SET optimize_or_like_chain = 1; SELECT toString(count()) LIKE '%1%' OR toString(count()) LIKE '%2%' FROM numbers(3); ``` Covered by `tests/queries/0_stateless/04545_optimize_or_like_chain_aggregate_lhs.sql` (aggregate and window variants, plus an ordinary-function control that must still collapse).
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: query_plan_join_swap_table changes the result of ANY INNER JOIN with OR-ed ON conditions (deterministic, max_threads = 1)
signal.text: ### Describe the bug The planner's automatic build-side swap (`query_plan_join_swap_table`, default `auto`) changes the result of an `ANY INNER JOIN` with **OR-ed conditions** in `ON`. On identical single-part tables, single-threaded, the swapped plan deterministically returns **6 rows** and the unswapped plan **3 rows** — the swapped output is a strict superset. `EXPLAIN actions = 1` shows both plans keep `Type: inner | Strictness: any | Algorithm: HashJoin` while the table read order flips, so the `ANY` deduplication is applied to opposite sides. With a single equality condition (no `OR`) both plans agree, so the multi-disjunct key path is the trigger. ### How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE l (a Int32, b Int32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; CREATE TABLE r (a Int32, b Int32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; INSERT INTO l SELECT number % 8, number % 3 FROM numbers(12); INSERT INTO r SELECT number % 5, number % 8 FROM numbers(12); SELECT * FROM l ANY JOIN r ON l.b = r.b OR l.a = r.a ORDER BY ALL SETTINGS max_threads = 1, query_plan_join_swap_table = 'true'; -- 6 rows SELECT * FROM l ANY JOIN r ON l.b = r.b OR l.a = r.a ORDER BY ALL SETTINGS max_threads = 1, query_plan_join_swap_table = 'false'; -- 3 rows ``` Outputs, stable across 20/20 runs per arm (`clickhouse local`, one part per table, `max_threads = 1`): ``` -- swap 'true' (and the default 'auto', which swaps here): 0 0 0 0 0 2 0 2 1 1 1 1 2 2 2 7 3 0 3 3 4 1 4 4 -- swap 'false': 0 0 0 0 0 2 0 2 1 1 1 1 ``` Whatever row choice `ANY` is permitted to make per key, the two plans do not even agree on the **number** of emitted rows, and the divergence is controlled purely by a performance plan setting. Note also that both outputs emit only a small subset of the left keys that have matches (for example `l = (2, 1)` matches `r = (4, 1)` via `b` but is emitted by neither plan), so the intended `ANY` + `OR` semantics may be off in both plans — the deterministic swap-controlled difference is the unambiguous part. ### Affected versions Reproduced on master 26.8.1.1068 and on 26.7. Not bisected. ### Related Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112640 (the `ANY LEFT JOIN` + `OR` face of the swap: racy under `max_threads > 1`; this `INNER` face is deterministic and single-threaded) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111645 Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).
signal.author: zlareb1

signal.title: Throw instead of reporting success for an unsupported OPTIMIZE
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114765 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114765 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `OPTIMIZE TABLE` on an object-storage table whose engine does not implement compaction reported success while doing nothing. It now raises an error, like every other engine that does not support the statement. This affects `DeltaLake`, `Paimon`, `Hudi` and plain object-storage engines (`S3`, `GCS`, `COSN`, `OSS`, `AzureBlobStorage`, `HDFS`, and object-storage-backed `URL`); `Iceberg`, which does implement compaction, is unchanged. Closes #114765. ### Description Requested by @ PedroTadim (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114765#issuecomment-5291252538); reported by @ zlareb1. `StorageObjectStorage::optimize` overrides the throwing `IStorage` default and forwards to `configuration->optimize`, which resolved to one of two defaults returning `false`. `InterpreterOptimizeQuery` discards that `bool`, so the statement reported Ok. Verified: three parquet files and a four-file `_delta_log`, unchanged before and after. The fix goes into those two defaults, not the wrapper. `IStorage.h` documents the return as "whether any work has been done", and `StorageMergeTree` relies on that for a legitimate no-op under `optimize_throw_if_noop`, so reading `false` as "unsupported" at the wrapper would mislabel an implementation that ran and did no work. Both forwarders are untouched. Two defaults, reached by disjoint engine sets: `StorageObjectStorageConfiguration::optimize` (plain configurations) and `IDataLakeMetadata::optimize` (the 4 non-Iceberg lake metadata classes). `optimize` was the only unsupported-operation default in either header returning a value instead of throwing. Iceberg is unaffected: it is the sole override and never returns `false`. Its `allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction` gate is asserted as a control. Two error codes, as elsewhere in these headers: plain object storage `NOT_IMPLEMENTED (48)`, lakes `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD (1)` naming the lake type. One line to unify if you prefer one code. No setting or format change, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry, and no doc change (the support matrix has a `Compaction` row only in the Iceberg tab). 0 stateless and 0 integration tests affected: every existing `OPTIMIZE` on an object-storage engine is Iceberg, and the `S3`/`Azure` hits are `MergeTree` on an object-storage disk. BuzzHouse absorbs the new error (`disallowed_error_codes` is unset in `buzzhouse_job.py`, `compare_success_results` pinned `False`). Hudi has no local engine, so it is covered by sharing `IDataLakeMetadata::optimize` with the Delta and Paimon arms.
